WIND SENSORS
Anemometer (Cup or Propeller Type)
Mechanical 	sensor 	that 	measures 	wind 	speed 	by
rotating cups or a propeller. The rotational speed is
proportional 	to 	wind 	velocity, 	typically 	generating
electrical pulses or voltage.
Typical use in ABE:
Monitoring wind speed for greenhouse ventilation
control systems.
Managing spray drift operations in crop protection.
Logging data for wind energy potential studies on
farms.

MSU 	GENSAN
ABE 	Dept
MSU GENSAN
ABE Dept
WIND SENSORS
Wind Vane
Mechanical device with a tail and pointer that aligns
with the wind direction, moving a potentiometer or
encoder to give a directional electrical signal.
Typical use in ABE:
Determining wind direction for positioning orchard
sprayers.
Irrigation 	pivot 	systems 	to 	avoid 	spraying 	into
prevailing winds.
Planning windbreak layouts or shelterbelts.

MSU 	GENSAN
ABE 	Dept
MSU GENSAN
ABE Dept
WIND SENSORS
Ultrasonic Anemometer
Non-mechanical sensor that measures wind speed
and direction by sending ultrasonic pulses between
transducers. The time difference caused by wind flow
gives precise velocity and direction.
Typical use in ABE:
High-resolution microclimate studies in precision
agriculture.
Advanced research on evapotranspiration rates.
Monitoring 	conditions 	for 	controlled 	environment
agriculture (CEA).

MSU 	GENSAN
ABE 	Dept
MSU GENSAN
ABE Dept

1.Temperature sensors
2.Humidity sensors
3.Light sensors
4.Rainfall sensors

ABE 	Dept
MSU GENSAN
ABE Dept
CROP SENSORS
NDVI Sensors
(Normalized Difference Vegetation Index)
Optical sensors that measure reflected red and
near-infrared light to compute NDVI, indicating crop
vigor, biomass, or stress.
Typical use in ABE:
Precision 	agriculture: 	mapping 	crop 	health
variability to guide variable-rate fertilization.
Irrigation management: detecting water stress.
Yield forecasting in large plantations.

MSU 	GENSAN
ABE 	Dept
MSU GENSAN
ABE Dept
CROP SENSORS
Chlorophyll Meters
Handheld 	or 	inline 	sensors 	that 	estimate
chlorophyll 	content 	by 	measuring 	light
absorption at specific wavelengths, indicating
nitrogen status.
Typical use in ABE:
On-the-spot 	nutrient 	management
decisions.
Scheduling side-dress fertilizer applications
in cereals or corn.

MSU 	GENSAN
ABE 	Dept
MSU GENSAN
ABE Dept
CROP SENSORS
Canopy Temperature Sensors
(Infrared Thermometers)
Non-contact 	IR 	sensors 	that 	measure 	leaf 	or
canopy surface temperature, which rises under
water stress.
Typical use in ABE:
Scheduling irrigation by detecting crop stress
early.
Studies on evapotranspiration.
Field trials and precision agriculture

MSU 	GENSAN
ABE 	Dept
MSU 	GENSAN
ABE 	Dept
CROP SENSORS
Soil-Plant Moisture Sensors
(Capacitive, Resistive, TDR)
Sensors that measure soil water content near the
root zone, providing a direct indicator of available
moisture for plant uptake.
Typical use in ABE:
Scheduling 	irrigation 	to 	keep 	soil 	moisture
within optimal levels for each crop stage.
Studying 	root-zone 	water 	dynamics 	and
supporting precision water management.

MSU 	GENSAN
ABE 	Dept
MSU GENSAN
ABE Dept
CROP SENSORS
Multispectral / Hyperspectral Sensors
Advanced 	optical 	sensors 	capturing
reflectance in multiple bands beyond visible
and NIR, for detailed crop stress, disease, or
nutrient assessments.
Typical use in ABE:
Research trials on crop variety responses.
Detecting 	early 	fungal 	or 	nutrient
deficiencies.

AUTOMATED
CONTROLS
Automated 	controls 	refer 	to 	the
use of electronic, mechanical, and
computer-based 	systems 	to
monitor 	and 	control 	agricultural
operations.
The primary purpose is to improve
precision, 	reduce 	human 	labor,
and optimize resource utilization.

REASON FOR BUILDING
AUTOMATED CONTROL
SYSTEMS
1.Power Amplification (Gain) - Adjusting the steering angle of a large
autonomous tractor with slight electrical signals from a GPS-guided
controller.
2.Remote Control - Robotic arm used to pick up AB materials.
3.Ease of Input – Setting irrigation schedules by simply selecting the desired
time on a digital timer.
4.Disturbance Compensation – Regulating greenhouse vents to maintain set
temperatures even when sudden cold winds cause rapid heat loss

process directly without using feedback.

SYSTEMS
Closed-loop 	feedback 	- 	uses 	a 	measurement 	of 	the
output and feedback of the output signal to compare it
with the desired output or reference.

MSU 	GENSAN
ABE 	Dept
MSU GENSAN
ABE DeptBASIC ELEMENTS OF
AUTOMATED CONTROL SYSTEMS
1⃣ Control Signal
initial command or input that
tells the system what to do.
Example: A timer or remote
operator sends a signal to
start irrigation at 6:00 AM
for 30 minutes.
2⃣ Power Amplifier
This device boosts the control signal’s power so it
can drive large equipment.
In your case, it ensures there is enough power to
start and run the large motor for the sprinkler.
3⃣ Motor
Receives the amplified signal
and converts electrical energy
into mechanical energy.
It drives the pump that pushes
water into the sprinkler system.
4⃣ Process
The actual operation on the field — the sprinkler
system sprays water over the banana plantation.
5⃣ Actual Output
The result: water applied to the banana plants.
However, because this is an open-loop system,
there is no sensor to check if the soil actually
needs water or if enough was applied.

MSU 	GENSAN
ABE 	Dept
MSU GENSAN
ABE DeptBASIC ELEMENTS OF
AUTOMATED CONTROL SYSTEMS

MSU 	GENSAN
ABE 	Dept
MSU GENSAN
ABE DeptBASIC ELEMENTS OF
AUTOMATED CONTROL SYSTEMS
1⃣ Set-point
(Reference Input)
Keep greenhouse
temperature at
28 °C.
2⃣ Error calculation
Error = Set-point−Actual
Output
If the greenhouse is at
30 °C when you want
28 °C, the error is -2 °C
(too hot)
3⃣ Controller
Receives the error
signal.
Decides what
corrective action to
take to minimize the
error.
Example: A
microcontroller
determines that
sprinklers must turn
on.
4⃣ Actuator
The controller sends a
controlled signal to
the actuator.
The actuator executes
the action that
physically affects the
system.
Example: An electric
solenoid valve opens,
allowing water to flow
to the sprinklers.
5⃣ Disturbance input
Any external disturbances
influences the system here.
This means the manipulated
variable combines with
disturbances to affect the process.
6⃣ Process
The actual system being controlled.
e.g. the greenhouse air temperature drops
as sprinklers cool it through evaporation.
7⃣ Sensor
A temperature sensor measures the
actual output (current temperature
inside the greenhouse).
8⃣ Feedback Signal
The sensor sends this measured value back to
the first summing point.
This closes the loop, continuously checking if
the process output matches the set-point.

MSU 	GENSAN
ABE 	Dept
MSU GENSAN
ABE DeptBASIC ELEMENTS OF
AUTOMATED CONTROL SYSTEMS
✅ Overall loop:
1.Set desired condition (28 °C).
2.Measure actual condition
(sensor reads, say, 30 °C).
3.Calculate error (difference: -2 °C).
4.Controller decides action (turn sprinklers on).
5.Actuator executes
(valve opens, sprinklers cool air).
6.Process responds (temperature lowers).
7.Sensor updates measurement, repeats the
cycle.
8.If temperature reaches 28 °C, the controller
might shut sprinklers off.

CONTROLLERS
A 	controller 	is 	a 	programmable 	electronic 	device 	that
receives input signals from sensors or operators, processes
these inputs through a set of predefined logical operations or
decision rules, and then sends output signals to control and
manipulate external components or systems.

circuits, 	which 	execute 	the 	actual 	instructions—whether
implemented 	through 	hardware 	gates 	or 	programmable
software logic. These logic circuits form the core of how the
controller interprets inputs and determines appropriate outputs.

resistance on rotor)

Engr. Jackielou L. Paches
DEPRECIATION
A property is depreciable if it meets all three requirements as follows:
1. It must be used in business or held for the production of income.
2. It must have determinable life, and the life must be longer than one
year.
3. It must be something that wears out, decays, gets used up, become
obsolete, or losses value from natural cause.

Engr. Jackielou L. Paches
DEPRECIATION
TERMS
• Depreciation Cost – depends upon the physical or economic life of the
equipment and its first cost.
• Physical Life – the length of time during which it is capable of
performing the function for which it was designed and manufactured.
• Economic Life – the length of time during which it will operate at a
satisfactory profit.
• Useful Life – the period of time as asset is kept in productive use in a
trade or business.

Engr. Jackielou L. Paches
DEPRECIATION
TERMS
• Value – present worth of all future profits that are to be received
through the ownership of a property.
• First Cost – includes the original purchase price, freight and
transportation charges to the site, installation expenses, initial taxes and
permits to operate, and all other expenses needed to put the equipment
into operation.
• Salvage Value – second-hand value or resale value; the amount for
which the equipment or machine can be sold as second-hand.
• Scrap or Junk Value – amount the equipment can be sold for, when
disposed of as a junk.

Engr. Jackielou L. Paches
DEPRECIATION
TERMS
• Market Value – the amount which a willing buyer will pay to a willing
seller for a property, where each has equal advantage and is under no
compulsion to buy or sell.
• Utility or Use Value – is what the property is worth to the owner as an
operating unit.
• Fair Value – is usually determined by a disinterested third party in order
to establish a price that is fair to both seller and buyer.
• Book Value/ Depreciated Book Value – is the worth of a property as
shown on the accounting records of an enterprise.

Engr. Jackielou L. Paches
DEPRECIATION
TERMS
• Going Value or Going-Concern Value – considered to be an intangible
value, which can actually operating concern has due to its operation.
• Goodwill Value – that element of value, which a business has earned
through the favorable consideration and patronage of its customers
arising from its well-known and well-conducted policies and operations.
• Rate-Base Value – the value assigned to the property for the purpose of
establishing rates.
• Franchise Value – is an intangible item of value arising from the
exclusive right of the company to provide a specific product or service in a
stated region of the country.

Sum of Years' Digits (SYD) Method
The Sum of Years' Digits (SYD) method is an accelerated depreciation
method used in accounting. It results in higher depreciation expenses
in the early years of an asset's life and lower expenses in later years,
reflecting the idea that assets are typically more productive when
they are newer.

The Author:
Alexis T. Belonio is a Professional Agricultural Engineer and a registered ASEAN Engineer. He
finished his Bachelor of Science in Agricultural Engineering and Master of Science degrees from
CLSU. He is a Senior Research Fellow at the Philippine Rice Research Institute, Science City of
Munoz, Nueva Ecija. He served as Affiliate Professor at the College of Engineering, Central
Luzon State University (CLSU), Science City of Munoz, Nueva Ecija and as Adjunct Assistant
Professor at the Departments of Agricultural and Chemical Engineering at the College of
Engineering and Agro-Industrial Technology, University of the Philippines at Los Banos. He was
former an Associate Professor at the Department of Agricultural Engineering and
Environmental Management, College of Agriculture, Central Philippine University, Iloilo City.
Since 1983, he has been deeply involved in teaching, research, technology development, and
entrepreneurial activities related to the field of agricultural engineering. He served as a
Reviewer for the Agricultural Engineering Board Examination at TGIM, CLSU, BUCAF, CBSUA,
SPAMAST, and MSU Gen San Review Centers, in the fields of Agricultural Power, Machinery
and Allied Subjects as well as Agricultural Processing, Structures and Allied Subjects.
He was awarded by the Philippine Society of Agricultural Engineers (PSAE) as the “Most Outstanding
Agricultural Engineer in the field of Farm Power and Machinery”, in 1993. In that same year, he was
named by the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC) as the “Outstanding Professional in the field of
Agricultural Engineering”. And in 1997, he was awarded by the TOYM Foundation and the Jerry Roxas
Foundation as the “Outstanding Young Filipino (TOYF) in the field of Agricultural Engineering”. In 2008,
he was awarded as “Associate Laureate of the Rolex Awards for Enterprise ” (Geneva, Switzerland) and
in 2010 as a “Laureate in Economic Business Development Category of The Tech Awards” (San Jose,
California). He was adjudged as one of the “Inspiring Modern-Day Filipino Heroes” by Yahoo Southeast
Asia in 2011 and one of the “25 Heroes-for-Better” by the Western Union in 2015. Recently, he has
received the “2016 ASEAN Outstanding Engineering Achievement Awards” given by the ASEAN
Federation of Engineering Organizations (AFEO).
As a dedicated professional, he is technically assisting various agricultural companies in the country. He
has written and published several research and technical papers, technical handbooks, including
instructional and review materials.

a. 	Adaptive design

a. 	Original design
b. 	Development design

d. 	None of the above

activities, and creative brain.
a. 	Original design
b. 	Development design
c. 	Adaptive design
d. 	None of the above

d. 	None of the above
5. During testing of agricultural
machines, thermometer sensors should
be partially shielded to minimize ___.
a. mechanical damage on thermometer
sensor
b. error on the effect of heat of
radiation
c. error from heat of conduction from
wall of the machine
d. None of the above
6. During the test of agricultural
machines, shaft speed is measured
using ___.
a. speedometer
b. velocity meter
c. tachometer
d. None of the above
7. Instrument used to measure the
draft of a plow.
a. Dynamometer
b. Spring scale
c. Pressure gauge
d. All of the above
8. Holding capacity of a mechanical
dryer during testing, as prescribed by
PAES, should be based on the ___ of
the sample and other accompanying
information, such as moisture content
and purity.
a. volume
b. weight
c. density
d. None of the above
9. Based on the PAES standard,
milling test of samples in testing a
mechanical grain dryer should be
conducted at least ___ after drying.
a. 24 hours
b. 48 hours
c. 36 hours
d. None of the above
10. Test carried out on every single
component of an equipment to check
the specifications.
a. Acceptance test
b. Routine test
c. Inspection
d. None of the above
TESTING AND EVALUATION OF MANUFACTURED/DISTRIBUTED
AB MACHINERY

11. Sensing instrument made of two
dissimilar wires used to measure the
temperature of air in a dryer.
a. 	Thermometer wire
b. 	Thermocouple wire
c. 	Thermo wire
d. 	All of the above
12. Interval of time measurement of test
parameters in a heated-air mechanical
grain dryer, as specified in the PAES
Test Method.
a. 15 minutes
b. 30 minutes
c. 	45 minutes
d. 60 minutes
e. None of the above
13. Minimum number of trials required in
testing heated-air mechanical grain
dryer, as specified in the PAES.
a. One
b. Two
c. Three
d. None of the above
14. Maximum moisture content of grains
to be used in testing mechanical
threshers should not be more than ___.
a. 18%
b. 24%
c. 28 %
d. None of the above
15. Grain-straw ratio for samples to be
used for testing a mechanical rice
thresher should be at ___ range.
a. 0.35 to 0.50
b. 0.50 to 0.65
c. 0.65 to 0.80
d. None of the above
16. Required water temperature in
testing pumps.
a. 10°C and below
b. 10°C – 40°C
c. 	40°C - 60°C
d. None of the above
17. Pressure drop of air-moving
devices is usually measured using a
___.
a. pressure gauge
b. pitot tube
c. manometer
d. None of the above
18. Amount of material needed in
testing a thresher should be enough to
run the machine for at least ___ hour.
a. 1/2
b. 1
c. 2
d. All of the above
19. Recommended test material for
testing a rice thresher should have ___
straw length.
a. 30 to 45 cm
b. 45 to 50 cm
c. 50 to 65 cm
d. None of the above
20. Minimum permissible noise for
power tillers.
a. 85 db
b. 92 db
c. 98 db
d. None of the above
21. Mnimum area required for testing a
power-operated seeder.
a. Not less than 100 m2
b. Not less than 500 m2
c 	Not less than 1000 m2
d. None of the above

22. Minimum operating time required for
testing a power tiller without breakdown
and malfunction.
a. 1 hour
b. 5 hours
c. 8 hours
d. None of the above
23. Minimum number of hours required
in testing rice threshers based on PAES
standards.
a. 0.5 hour
b. 1 hour
c. 2 hours
d. None of the above
24. Instrument used to measure the
speed of a windpump.
a. 	Manometer
b. 	Anemometer
c. 	Tachometer
d. 	None of the above
25. Instrument used to measure the
static pressure at the plenum chamber of
a dryer.
a. 	Manometer
b. 	Anemometer
c. 	Tachometer
d. 	None of the above
26. Instrument used to determine the
acidity and alkalinity of a substance.
a. 	Refractrometer
b. 	pH meter
c. 	Moisture meter
d. 	None of the above
27. Instrument used to measure the
amount of water present in a sample.
a. 	Hygrometer
b. 	Hydrometer
c. 	Moisture meter
d. 	All of the above
28. Thermometer used in measuring
the temperature of a surface without
the sensor touching it.
a. Thermocouple wire sensor operated
thermometer
b. Bimetallic surface measuring
thermometer
c. Infrared thermometer
d. None of the above
29. Instrument used in measuring the
velocity of water in a conveyance
channel.
a. Thermoanemometer
b. Anemometer
c. Current meter
d. None of the above
30. Velocity of the air passing through
the duct of the blower of a dryer is to be
determined, what instrument would you
recommend to measure the velocity?
a. Manometer
b. Thermometer
c. Thermoanemometer
d. None of the above
31. Which of the following cannot be
used in measuring the velocity of the
air?
a. Anemometer
b. Pitot-tube and manometer
c. Orifice and manometer
d. None of the above
32. Rate of flow of hot gas is to be
measured in a duct. As an Agricultural
Engineer, what instrument would you
recommend to determine the velocity of
the gas?
a. 	Thermoanemometer
b. 	Current meter
c. 	Pitot-tube manometer
d. 	None of the above

33. Air velocity at the air duct can be
measured using a manometer by taking
the ___.
a. 	static pressure
b. 	velocity pressure
c. 	velocity and static pressure
d. 	None of the above
34. Amount of current passing through a
wire can be measured using ___.
a. 	voltmeter
b. 	ammeter
c. 	Hertz meter
d. 	None of the above
35. Voltmeter is connected to a wire in
___ to measure voltage.
a. 	series
b. 	parallel
c. 	series and parallel
d. 	All of the above
36. AC Clamp meter is connected to a
wire in ___ to measure the amperage.
a. 	series
b. 	parallel
c. 	series and parallel
d. 	None of the above
37. In determining the ambient
conditions during testing of a mechanical
dryer, the surrounding ___ are usually
measured.
a. 	air temperature and humidity
b. 	air temperature and velocity
c. 	air velocity and humidity
d. 	None of the above
38. In order to measure the power input
in a motor, the ____ are measured and
then multiplied by the power factor.
a. 	voltage and hertz
b. 	current and hertz
c. 	voltage and current
d. 	None of the above
39. Hertz meter is connected in ___ to
measure the cycle of the lines.
a. 	series
b. 	parallel
c. 	series and parallel
d. 	None of the above
40. Unit of noise level of a sound
meter is expressed in ___.
a. 	hertz
b. 	decibels
c. 	% loudness
d. 	None of the above
41. Actual field capacity of a tractor
and of plowing implement can be
determined by ___.
a. measuring the velocity of travel of
the tractor multiplied by the width of cut
of the implement
b. measuring the area plowed by the
tractor divided by the time it finished
the operation
c. measuring the area plowed by the
tractor multiplied by the travel speed
d. None of the above
42. When measurement needs to be
done to gather sets of data in a defined
period of time, what instrument would
you recommend to be included in your
instrumentation set-up as an
Agricultural Engineer?
a. 	Data encoder
b. 	Data compiler
c. 	Data logger
d. 	None of the above
43. Electronic device that records data
over time.
a. 	Data logger
b. 	Data encoder
c. 	Data compiler
d. 	None of the above

44. Which thermocouple-wire sensor is
capable to measure higher temperature
(up to 1260°C)?
a. 	Type C
b. 	Type J
c. 	Type K
d. 	None of the above
45. Low-temperature thermocouple-wire
sensor.
a. 	Type T
b. 	Type J
c. 	Type K
d. 	None of the above
46. Thermocouple wire made of copper
and constantan wires.
a. 	Type T
b. 	Type J
c. 	Type K
d. 	All of the above
47. Thermocouple-wire sensor
consisting of chromel and alumel wires.
a. 	Type T
b. 	Type J
c. 	Type K
d. 	All of the above
48. When testing a mechanical grain
dryer, the static pressure can be
measured using a ___.
a. 	pressure gage
b. 	manometer
c. 	vacuum gage
d. 	All of the above
49. When testing a rice mill, the
throughput capacity is determined as
___.
a. 	weight of paddy input over time
b. 	weight of brown rice output over
time
c. 	weight of milled rice output over time
d. 	None of the above
50. When testing a paddy dryer, the
capacity is determined by the ___.
a. 	weight of input paddy
b. 	weight of dried paddy
c. 	weight of dried paddy over time
d. 	None of the above
51. When testing a rice thresher, the
throughput capacity is the ___.
a. weight of clean threshed grain over
time
b. weight of panicle fed over time
c. weight of paddy input after
removing the straw over time
d. None of the above
52. Testing of engine used for power
tilling showed that a 7hp diesel engine
consumes 0.85 liter of diesel per hour.
What is the specific fuel consumption
of the engine, in grams per second,
per brake horsepower (g/sec-bhp) if
the specific gravity of diesel is 0.7 and
the brake power is 80% of the rated
horsepower? (Problem 1)
a. 	0.0295 g/sec-bhp
b. 	0.0357 g/sec-bhp
c. 	0.0412 g/sec-bhp
d. 	None of the above
53. Customized device in which all the
instruments are set to facilitate testing
of a machine.
a. 	Test rig
b. 	Test duct
c. 	Test instrument
d. 	None of the above
54. In testing animal-drawn and power-
operated agricultural machines, the
test plot is required to be in a ___
shape.
a. 	square
b. 	triangular
c. 	rectangular
d. 	None of the above

55. Required length-to-width ratio of a
test plot for animal-drawn and power-
operated agricultural machines.
a. 	2:1
b. 	4:2
c. 	6:3
d. 	All of the above
e. 	None of the above
56. In testing agricultural machines, the
first thing that the engineer must do is
___.
a. 	to prepare the instruments and data
sheet needed for the test
b. 	to get acquainted with the
construction and operation features of
the machine
c. 	to figure out what testing procedure
to be done
d. 	None of the above
57. Which of the following available
information need to be looked into by
the test engineer before testing a
machine?
a. 	Instruction book
b. 	Operation manual
c. 	Technical information
d. 	All of the above
e. 	None of the above
58. Amount of fuel consumed by a
machine during the test can be simply
determined by ___.
a. measuring the amount of fuel
remaining in the tank after testing using
a volumetric flask
b. filling the tank with fuel and the
amount of fuel added to make the tank
full is the amount of fuel used
c. starting with empty tank and then the
amount of fuel gradually added is the
amount of fuel used
d. All of the above
59. Required distance in measuring the
operational speed of an agricultural
machine during testing.
a. 	10 m
b. 	20 m
c. 	30 m
d. 	None of the above
60. Preliminary tests need to be done
in testing the machine so the machine
will ___.
a. be easy to be tested
b. be seen by test engineers and
helpers before testing it
c. be kept in best working condition
d. None of the above
61. Adjusting the machine should be
done when testing as per
recommendation by ___.
a. 	the operator
b. 	the manufacturer
c. 	the test engineer
d. 	None of the above
62. When testing agricultural
machines, the testing operator must be
___ the machine.
a. strong enough to operate
b. well knowledgeable with the design
of
c. fully conversant with the operation
of
d. None of the above
63. Difference in the distance traveled
by the tractor tire in 10 revolutions with
and without load during the tests over
the distance traveled at no load times
100 is the ___ of the tractor.
a. percentage downtime efficiency
b. percentage traction efficiency
c. percentage wheel slip
d. None of the above

64. Accurate data can be obtained
during testing when ___.
a. appropriate instrumentation is used
b. the instruments to be used are
properly calibrated
c. testing is to be done by a skillful
technician
d. All of the above
65. In testing the field capacity and field
efficiency of a machine, the ___.
a. non-working time should be
eliminated
b. overall time used should be
considered
c. speed of the machine should only be
considered
d. None of the above
66. A spring, hydraulic or strain-gauge
operating device that measures the
capacity required in pulling a machine.
a. Load cell
b. Spring scale
c. Dynamometer
d. None of the above
67. In testing a mechanical paddy grain
dryer during the wet harvest season, the
required moisture of samples to be used
must be at ___.
a. 	20% +/- 1.0%
b. 	23% +/- 1.2%
c. 	25% +/- 1.0%
d. 	None of the above
68. In testing a mechanical paddy dryer
during the dry harvest season, the
required moisture of paddy samples
must be at ___.
a. 	20% +/- 1.0%
b. 	23% +/- 1.2%
c. 	25% +/- 1.0%
d. 	None of the above
69. The line of pull to determine the
drawbar horsepower of a machine is
the ___ line of pull measured by the
drawbar dynamometer.
a. horizontal
b. inclined
c. vertical
d. None of the above
70. Effective field capacity of the
machine is the area tilled over the
___.
a. productive time
b. non-productive time
c. productive and non-productive time
d. None of the above
71. In testing rice threshers, the
threshing efficiency is determined by
the amount of ___.
a. threshed grains received at all
outlets divided by the total grain input
times 100
b. threshed grains received at all the
outlets divided by the input paddy fed
into the machine multiplied by 100
c. threshed grains from the paddy
straw outlet to the total grain input
multiplied by 100
d. None of the above
72. In testing rice threshers, the
threshing recovery is determined by
the amount of ___, expressed as
percent by weight.
a. threshed grains at the main outlet
of the thresher with respect to the
weight of paddy and panicle input
b. threshed grains at the main outlet
of the thresher with respect to the total
grain input
c. threshed grains from the different
outlets with respect to the total grain
input
d. None of the above

73. Total grain input to the thresher
includes the ___.
a. weight of threshed grains collected at
the main grain outlet per unit time
b. weight of threshed grains collected at
all outlets per unit time
c. weight of unthreshed grains from all
outlets per unit time
d. All of the above
74. Which of the following criteria is
considered in evaluating rice threshers?
a. 	Applicable kind of crops
b. 	Output capacity
c. 	Machine vibration
d. 	Power requirement
e. 	Labor requirement
f. 	Ease of adjustment, cleaning and
replacement
g. 	Operating cost of the machine
h. 	All of the above
i. 	Three of the above
75. A rice thresher was tested in
threshing newly harvested rice. Tests
have shown that 2000 kilos of palay was
threshed in 3 hours. The amount of
losses gathered were as follows: blower
loss - 90 kilos; separation loss - 200
kilos; unthreshed loss - 50 kilos; and
scattering loss - 120 kilos. What is the
percentage blower loss? (Problem 2)
a. 	10.9%
b. 	19.7%
c. 	26.1%
d. 	43.5%
e. 	None of the above
76. What is the percentage
unthreshed loss of the thresher in
Item 75? (Problem 2)
a. 	10.9%
b. 	19.7%
c. 	26.1%
d. 	43.5%
e. 	None of the above
77. What is the percentage
separation loss of the thresher in Item
75? (Problem 2)
a. 	10.9%
b. 	19.7%
c. 	26.1%
d. 	43.5%
e. 	None of the above
78. What is the percentage scattering
loss of the thresher in Item 75?
(Problem 2)
a. 	10.9%
b. 	19.7%
c. 	26.1%
d. 	43.5%
e. 	None of the above
79. What is the threshing capacity of
the thresher, in kg per hour, in Item
75? (Problem 2)
a. 	666.7 kg/hr
b. 	676.6 kg/hr
c. 	766.6 kg/hr
d. 	None of the above

80. This involves verification of
performance, ease of handling, and
safety features of a machine both in
laboratory and field.
a. 	Testing and evaluation
b. 	Research and development
c. 	Operation check up
d. 	None of the above
81. Testing and evaluation is done
simply to ___ the machine meets the
specifications suitable for local farming
condition and provides efficient
operation.
a. 	check
b. 	ensure
c. 	rate
d. 	All of the above
82. What are the key aspects of testing
and evaluation?
a. 	Verifying machine specification
b. 	Performance testing
c. 	Ease of handling and safety
d. 	Inspection of components and
assembly
e. 	Evaluate benefits in operating the
machine
f. 	Report preparation
g. 	All of the above
h. 	Three of the above
83. What is the importance of testing
and evaluation?
a. 	Ensure machine quality
b. 	Promote the use of efficient farming
practices
c. 	Protects farmer’s investment
d. 	All of the above
e. 	Two of the above
84. What are the things to consider
when doing initial assessment and
preparation before doing testing and
evaluation of agricultural machines?
a. 	Test site and crop condition.
b. 	Test material to be used in the test.
c. 	Verify machine specification.
d. 	All of the above
e. 	Two of the above
85. Performance testing of agricultural
machine comprises of ____.
a. 	operational testing
b. 	measurement of prescribed
samples to be used in the test
c. 	conduct minimum of three test
trials
d. 	record item inspected or measured
e. 	All of the above
f. 	Two of the above
86. Which of the following standards
and guidelines is used in testing
agricultural machines?
a. 	Philippine National Standards
b. 	AFMech Law (RA 10601)
c. 	AMTEC Methods of Test
d. 	All of the above
e. 	None of the above
87. In evaluating design and technical
specification according to functionality
and purpose, which items need to be
considered?
a. Assessment of machine intended
purpose
b. Determine working width and
capacity
c. Evaluate design features –
ergonomic, ease of maintenance, and
safety features
d. All of the above
e. None of the above

88. In reviewing the technical
specification of the machine during
testing and evaluation, which of the
following need to be done?
a. Review engine power and fuel
efficiency – in comparison with other
similar machine
b. Examine operating speed and field
capacity – can it cover the tasks and
area in a given time
c. Check dimension and weight – can it
be accommodate in storage and
transportation capabilities
d. All of the above
e. None of the above
89. Durability and reliability can be
assessed by ___.
a. 	conducting research of the machine
reputation for reliability
b. 	conducting evaluation of the quality of
components and materials
c. 	considering maintenance requirement
d. 	All of the above
e. 	None of the above
90. In evaluating the cost estimates of
the machine, which of the following
parameters is used?
a. 	Ownership cost
b. 	Operating cost
c. 	Total Cost
d. 	All of the above
e. 	None of the above
91. Additional considerations to be
undertaken during evaluation and testing
of agricultural machines.
a. 	Local regulations nd standards
b. 	Availability of support and training
c. 	Sustainability and environmental
impact
d. 	All of the above
e. 	None of the above
92. Test carried out to determine
whether the claims of the
manufacturer/supplier of the machine
conform with he actual data ad test
results.
a. 	Acceptance Test
b. 	Verification Test
c. 	Routine Test
d. 	None of the above
93. Test conducted to determine the
machine to be supplied is acceptable
for use by clients/beneficiaries based
on the performance standard.
a. 	Acceptance Test
b. 	Verification Test
c. 	Routine Test
d. 	None of the above
94. Which of the following is not a basic
measurement?
a. 	Time
b. 	Mass
c. 	Dimension
d. 	Temperature
e. 	Pressure
f. 	None of the above
95. Which of the following is a derived
measurement?
a. 	Area
b. 	Torque
c. 	Speed
d. 	Rate of application
e. 	All of the above
f. 	None of the above
96. For testing power tiller in wetland
area, which of the following is required?
a. 	Must be soaked for 24 hour.
b. 	Field must not be less that 500 m2.
c. 	Field side ratio 2:1.
d. 	Plowing depth of 10 cm +/- 1 cm.
e. 	All of the above
f. 	Two of the above

97. In testing seeder and planter, which
of the following is required?
a. Plain and level surface should be
used.
b. Not less than 500 m2 for manual
machine.
c. Not less than 1000 m2 for power
operated.
d. All of the above
e. None of the above
98. In testing combine harvester, which
of the following is required?
a. 	Area should not be less than 500 m2
b. 	Field side ratio 2:1
c. 	Cutting height 30 cm
d. 	All of the above
e. 	Two of the above
99. In testing rice thresher, which of the
following is required?
a. 	Use commonly grown variety
b. 	Mc 24% and below
c. 	Straw length 45 to 50 cm
d. 	Grain to straw ratio 0.55 – 0.65
e. 	2 trials with minimum time of 15 min
per trial
f. 	Material must be sufficient for at
least 1 hour
g. 	All of the above
h. 	Five of the above
100. In testing a heated-air mechanical
dryer, which of the following is required?
a. 	Initial MC must be 20% and above
b. 	Milling of samples at last 48 hours
after drying
c. 	MC of samples for milling is 14%
d. 	All of the above
e. 	None of the above
101. In testing a rice mill, which of the
following is a relevant requirement?
a. Samples must be sufficient for at
least 1-1/2 hour continuous operation
for single pass rice mill
b. Samples must be sufficient for 3
hours continuous operation for multi-
pass rice mill
c. At least 3 trials
d. All of the above
e. None of the above
102. Suspension of test is
implemented when machine ___ during
the test at the discretion of the Test
Engineer concurred by the
manufacturer’s representative.
a. 	stops due to lack of fuel
b. 	belt drive was misaligned
c. 	malfunction or breakdown
d. 	None of the above

Determination of Power Requirement
1. Power needed to move the
implement either pull or push by a
tractor.
a. 	Drawbar Power
b. 	Wheel power
c. 	PTO power
d. 	None of the above
2. Energy used by the machine, such
as electricity or fuel consumed during
operation.
a. 	Power input
b. 	Power rating
c. 	Power consumption
d. 	None of the above
3. Amount of fuel used over a specific
time period by a tractor or engine.
a. 	Specific fuel consumption
b. 	Fuel consumption rate
c. 	Amount of fuel used
d. 	None of the above
4. Area covered by a machine per unit
of time, considering both productive and
non-productive time.
a. 	Effective field capacity
b. 	Theoretical field capacity
c. 	Field efficiency
d. 	None of the above
5. Amount of input material processed
and the amount of output produced in
processing machinery.
a. 	Field capacity
b. 	Throughput capacity
c. 	Input and output capacity
d. 	None of the above
6. Distance between the outermost
points of a working implement.
a. 	Swath
b. 	Tool width
c. 	Implement width
d. 	None of the above
7. Ratio of actual field capacity to the
theoretical capacity.
a. 	Field efficiency
b. 	Field ratio
c. 	Field factor
d. 	None of the above
8. Percentage of input material
recovered as a usable product in
processing machinery.
a. 	Product recovery
b. 	Output recovery
c. 	Output ratio
d. 	None of the above
9. Amount of work done per unit of
fuel consumed.
a. 	Working efficiency
b. 	Fuel efficiency
c. 	Fuel recovery
d. 	None of the above
10. Quality of the output product, such
as moisture content, fineness, or
purity.
a. 	Product output
b. 	Product quality
c. 	Product Recovery
d. 	None of the above

BEARINGS

BOARD EXAM REVIEWER

7/24/25
2
INTRODUCTION
☐ Bearing permits relative motion of two parts in one or two
directions with minimum friction while resisting motion in the
direction of applied load.
3
COMMON USES OF BEARINGS
4

7/24/25
3
CLASSIFICATIONS OF BEARINGS
☐ Plain or Journal Bearing –
Loads are pass through the
surfaces of the parts by sliding
contact or separated by
lubricants.
☐ Anti-Friction or Rolling
Bearing – Loads are pass
through the surfaces of the parts
by rolling contact. It carries the

balls or other types of rollers.

PLAIN OR JOURNAL BEARING
☐ A bearing that develop a hydrodynamic pressure to carry the
loads and separate the bearing elements in order to minimize
friction.
☐ The bearing load per unit of projected area is directly
proportional to the viscosity of the lubricant and of the relative
speed of rotation and inversely proportional to the diametral
clearance.
☐ Plain bearings used in agricultural machines usually have thin
lubrication.

• It has the ability to resist corrosion; and

☐ Little or no service requirements
☐ Lower cost
☐ Greater tolerances
☐ No elaborate enclosure requirement

☐ A bearing that utilizes the rolling action of a number of balls
or other elements between two rings in order to reduce the
friction and prolong their lives.

4. Lubrication is simple and require little attention.
5. They are suitable for low speeds.
6. Replacement in case of failure is easy.
7. Starting friction and required torque is low.

1. Relatively expensive because of the cost of the bearing

and axial movement of the shaft to its housing.

• This is the common type of rolling

FACTORS TO CONSIDER IN
SELECTING BEARING
☐ Bearing space – The type and dimension of the bearing
must be selected according to the allowable space.
☐ Load carrying capacity – This includes the radial and the
thrust loads. The radial load capacity of roller bearing is higher
than tat of ball bearings.
☐ Limiting speed – The limiting speed of rolling bearings vary
according to dimension, cage type and material, bearing load,
lubrication and cooling method, as well as bearing types.
31
☐ Angular misalignment – Angular misalignment is brought
about by shaft deflection resulting from applied load, shaft and
housing inaccuracy, and bearing mounting alignment. The
maximum permissible angular misalignment differs according
to bearing type and working condition. In case of large degree
of misalignment, use self-aligning type bearings.
☐ Rigidity – Bearing rigidity depends primarily on the load
distribution among individual rolling element which varies with
the size and number, the type of contact between raceway and
rolling elements. For main shaft, always increase both the
shaft and bearing rigidity. Roller bearings should be selected
since they are less susceptible to deformation from load than
ball bearings.

7/24/25
2
INTRODUCTION
☐ Belt-and-pulley drive is the most
simple method of transmitting
power in agricultural machines.
☐ It is widely adopted in driving
various production and
postproduction parts of agricultural
machines.
☐ Cost of transmitting power is
very much lower compared with
sprocket-and-chain and gear
drives.
3
CLASSIFICATIONS OF BELT AND
PULLEY DRIVE
☐ Flat Belt – is a flexible material
which is banded on two or more
pulleys where power is transmitted
from the driver to the driven pulley.
Power transmission primarily
depends on the friction between the
belt and the pulley surfaces.
☐ V Belt – is a transmission system
that consists of an endless flexible
belt that transmits power by
contacting and gripping the sheaves
which are keyed to the shaft of the
driving and the driven machine.
4

7/24/25
3
EXAMPLE APPLICATIONS OF BELT
AND PULLEY DRIVE
5
CHARACTERISTICS FLAT BELT AND
PULLEY DRIVE
☐ Suitable for high speed drives.
☐ Adaptable to dusty and abrasive
environment.
☐ Transmits power on a long distance
shaft.
☐ Longer life, high efficiency, low cost,
and low maintenance.
☐ Also applicable for short-distance
drive by using idler, pivoted or spring-
actuated motor bases.
6

7/24/25
4
☐ Requires tension to minimize slip
below 2 percent.
☐ High bearing load due to high
tension requirement for belt.
☐ Noisy operation.
7
CHARACTERISTICS OF V-BELT AND
SHEAVE DRIVE
☐ Suitable for long-center-distance
drive.
☐ Has the ability to transfer heavy
tensile load.
☐ Usually used to transmit power
between parallel shafts. In some cases
they can also be used for non-parallel
drives.
☐ Applicable for single or in multiple
sheaves.
8

7/24/25
5
☐ Prone to elongation because of wear and operation; hence, there
is a need of mechanism to maintain the proper tension to take up
the belt slacks.
☐ They rotate with slip and creep condition’ therefore, the angular
velocity between the two shafts is neither constant nor exactly equal
to the ratio of the sheave pitch diameter. Power losses caused by
slip and creep ranged from 3 to 5 % for most belt drives.
☐ They allow an efficient and easily operated method of varying the
angular velocity ratio by employing spring loaded adjustable-width
sheaves. The diameter of the sheave is a function of the belt
tension.
9
☐ In general, V-belt efficiency ranges from 70 to 95 percent.
Well selected belt has an efficiency of 90 to 95 percent.
☐ Torque load has a larger effect on the efficiency. That is, the
lower the load, the lower is the efficiency; conversely, excessively
high load also lowers the efficiency.
☐ Efficiency drops with small pulley size. Usually 4in pulley is
commonly used for agricultural drives.
10

7/24/25
6

Driven shaft speed can be changed during operation by adjusting
the sheave diameter of the driver shaft.
Driven
Pulley
Adjustable Driver
Pulley
Knob

TYPES OF BELT
☐ Flat Belt – is used to transmit
rotary motion and power between
two shafts which lie flat on the
face of the corresponding pulley.
☐ Narrow V-Belt – is a belt with
trapezoidal cross-section to
transmit rotary motion to parallel
shafts.
12

7/24/25
7
☐ Double V- Belt – is a V-belt
with inverted V on top making it
more suitable for multiple-
sheaves drive arrangement.
☐ Cogged Belt – is a V-belt with
teeth design for a special kind of
sheave to provide more gripping
action to obtain higher efficiency
hence minimizing belt slip.
13
☐ V-Ribbed Belt – combines
the features of a flat belt and
a V-belt. It operates very
efficiently and can run at a
very high speed.
☐ Variable-Speed Belt – is
most common where there is
a large center distance
between shafts or where
drive ratio goes beyond the
commonly supplied drive.
14

7/24/25
8
BELT MATERIALS
☐ Leather – It can carry significant
load of up to 500hp and can provide
long service life. However, it is costly
and requires to be cleaned and
dressed at all times. It is also prone to
stretch and shrink. Also, it is normally
limited to low or moderate speed.
☐ Rubberized fabric or cord - This is a
combination of both fabric and cord
reinforcement that provides the
strength of chord reinforcement and
the abrasion resistance of the fabric.
15
☐ Rubberized Fabric – This kind of belt material is the least
costly of all. For the same width and thickness, this type
transmits less power and has a shorter life than leather.
☐ Rubberized Chord - This is only available as endless belt and
not designed to be spliced. It carries 50% more power that
fabric reinforced belt.
☐ Reinforced Rubber or Plastic – This has a nylon member
covered by rubber or plastic. Its capacities ranged from
fractional horsepower to 100hp per inch of width. It is capable
of operating at 40,000 fpm.
Fabric – It is made either of plain or with chemical or rubberized
coatings. It has the ability to tract uniformly.

☐ Pulleys and sheaves are used to transmit the power from the

IDLERS

Idlers are grooved sheaves or flat pulleys which do not serve to

CLASSIFICATIONS OF BELT DRIVE
☐ Open-Belt Drive
• Pulley shafts are parallel with each other
• Pulleys have the same direction
• Shorter belt length
• Smaller arc of contact of belt on two pulleys
• Suitable for v-belt and flat belt drives
According to Type of Drive

☐ Cross-Belt Drive
• Pulley shafts are parallel with each other
• Pulleys direction are opposite
• Requires longer belt length
• Higher arc of contact of belt on pulleys
• Suitable for flat belt drive or special type of v-belt
31
☐ Quarter-Turn Drive
• Pulley shafts are perpendicular with each other
• Requires longer belt than open-belt drive
• Relatively higher arc of contact between belt and
pulley
• Suitable for flat belt or special type of v-belt

N1 = 1720 rpm

SPROCKET AND CHAIN

7/24/25
2
INTRODUCTION
☐ A chain drive basically consists of an endless chain whose links
engage the teeth of sprocket keyed to the shaft of the driving and
the driven mechanisms.
☐ This kind of drive is used to transmit power and to synchronize
motion or maintain a fixed-speed ratio between rotating shafts.
☐ In the Philippines, chain-and-sprocket drives are commonly used
in the construction of transmission boxes for power and puddling-
type floating tillers.
3
Characteristics
☐ Shaft distances are unrestricted, i.e. the drive is well suited for
long and short-center distances.
☐ They do not creep or slip. They maintain a positive speed ratio
between the driver and the driven shafts.
☐ They are physically more compact than belt drives.
☐ They require more accurate alignment of the shaft and the
sprockets.
☐ Arc of contact is smaller for chains than for belts.
☐ They are more practical for low speed.
4

7/24/25
3
TYPES OF CHAIN
☐ Detachable Chain
☐ Pintle Chain
• They are used for slightly higher
speed (up to about 450 fpm) and
heavier loads.
• They are made of individual
cast link having full round barrel
end with offset sidebars.
5
☐ Engineering Steel Chain
☐ Inverted-Tooth or Silent Chain
• They are high-speed chains
used predominantly for
prime mover power take-off
drive.
☐ Bead or Slider Chain
• They are used for manually-
controlled or slow-speed
drives.
6

7/24/25
4
☐ Roller Chain
• This is the most important type
for agricultural use. It is
available either single- or
multiple-strand type.
• Roller chain composed of
roller, links, and pin links,
alternately spaced throughout
the length of the chain. The
roller link consists of two sets
of rollers and bushing, and two
link plates, and the pin links
consists of two pins and two
link plates.
7
SPROCKETS
☐ Types
• A - plain plate
• B - with hub on one side only
• C - with hub on both sides
• D - detachable hub
8

7/24/25
5
Samples of Sprockets
☐ Materials
• Cast iron – for large sprockets
• Steel - small sprockets
• Stainless steel or bronze – for corrosion resistant application
• Formica, nylon, and special purpose plastic – for special
condition
9
SELECTION OF CHAIN AND
SPROCKETS
☐ Smallest applicable chain number is suitable for high speed
and quite operation.
☐ Power capacity varies with chain pitch.
☐ Short pitch with high working load can be obtained by the
use of multiple strand chain.
☐ Smallest sprocket selected must be large enough to
accommodate the shaft.

USEFUL TERMS
☐ Chain Pitch – It is the distance between adjacent joint members.
☐ Pitch Diameter - It is the diameter of the pitch circle that passes
through the center of the link pins as the chain wrapped on the
sprocket.
CHAIN AND SPROCKET SIZE
☐ The size of chain-and-sprocket drive is designated as RC
Number. The higher the chain number, the larger is the loading
capacity of the drive.
☐ Divide the chain first number by 8 to get the pitch length, in
inches. Example RC 80 is 8/8 is 1 in. pitch. The second number
indicates that it is a roller chain. Bush chain indicates a number of
5.
☐ Bicycle chain usually used RC 10 while RC 40 to 60 are
commonly used for power tiller transmission box.

FACTORS CAUSING CHAIN TENSION
☐ Pull required for power transmission.
☐ Centrifugal force generated as the chain travels around the
sprockets and over the curved path between sprockets.
☐ Catenary effect caused by the weight of the chain between

LUBRICATION

7/24/25
1
GEAR DRIVE
DESIGN, FABRICATION, AND TESTING OF
AGRICULTURAL MACHINES
by
Engr. Alexis T. Belonio, MS
Agricultural and Biosystems Engineer
ASEAN Engineer
2025 AGRICULTURAL AND BIOSYSTEMS ENGINEERING
BOARD EXAM REVIEWER
1
Disclaimer
Photos , illustrations and schematic diagrams of equipment or machine parts are shown in the
presentation solely for educational purposes to facilitate comprehension of the topics by the students.
Showing them does not endorse a product nor imply criticism of similar products not mentioned.
2

7/24/25
2
INTRODUCTION
☐ Gears are tooth wheels used to transmit power and motion
at a constant ratio from one rotating shaft to another by
means of a positive contact of successively engaging teeth.
☐ Compared with V-belts and chain drives, gear drives are
more compact and can operate at a higher speed. Gear
drive also provides precise timing of motion.
☐ In agricultural machinery, gears are commonly used in
transmission drives for tractors, self-propelled combines,
power tiller, and many others.
3
Gear Drive for Transmission Boxes
4

7/24/25
3
GEAR CHARACTERISTICS
☐ They are the most durable and rugged of all the mechanical
drives.
☐ They are usually used for transmission in compact drive
system.
☐ They transmit high power at efficiencies up to 98%.
☐ They are expensive and require high replacement cost.
☐ They require better lubrication and cleanliness.
☐ They are easily affected by shaft misalignment
5
Spline Shaft Gear
6

7/24/25
4
GEAR NOMENCLATURE
☐ Gear size – refers to the pitch circle or pitch diameter of the
gear.
☐ Addendum – is the height of the gear tooth beyond the pitch
circle.
☐ Dedendum – is the depth of the tooth below the pitch circle.
☐ Circular Pitch – is the spacing of the gear teeth measured
along the pitch circle.
☐ Diametral Pitch – is the ratio of the number of teeth to the
pitch diameter in inches.
7
8

7/24/25
5
☐ Gear Depth – is the sum of addendum and dedendum.
☐ Work Depth or Depth of Engagement – is equal to the
sum of the addendum.
☐ Line of Centers – is the line connecting the center of gear
rotation.
☐ Involute – is a curve formed that unwrapped around a
cylinder.
☐ Base Circle – is a curve generated from the involute.
☐ Pressure Angle – is a line through the point of tangency
and tangent to the base circle.
9
10

7/24/25
6
11
GEAR CLASSIFICATIONS
☐ Gear with Parallel Shaft
• Spur Gear
• Helical Gear
• Harmonic Gear
• Planocentric
12

7/24/25
7
13
14

7/24/25
8
☐ Gears with Intersecting or Skewed Shaft
• Worm
• Beveloid
• Hypoid
• Face
• Helicon
• Straight Bevel
• Spiral Bevel
• Zerol
• Crossed Helical
• Spiroid
• Cavex Worm
• Cone Drive
15
SPUR GEAR
☐ It is the most common type of
gear.
☐ Teeth are straight and parallel
to shaft axis.
☐ Its advantages are: (a) simple,
(b) low cost, and (c) easy to
maintain.
☐ Drawbacks are: (a) have less
capacity and (b) noisier than other
types.
16

7/24/25
9
HELICAL GEAR
☐ It can carry more load than the
equivalent size spur gear.
☐ Operates more smoothly and
quietly.
☐ More costly than spur gears.
☐ Herringbone is similar to double
helical gear.
17
WORM GEAR
☐ It provides a maximum reduction ratio
for a given center distance.
☐ It is quiet and smooth action.
☐ It is used only for speed reduction.
☐ Cannot back-drive at ratios greater
than 20:1.
☐ Contact area is large hence load
capacity is high.
☐ Shafts are almost always at right
angles.
18

7/24/25
10
STRAIGHT BEVEL GEAR
☐ This is the simplest type of gear for
intersecting shaft.
☐ It is commonly used for shaft
intersecting at right angle but can also
be used for shaft mating at any angle.
☐ Gears are designed in pairs thus
are not always interchangeable.
☐ Supporting shaft and bearings must
be rigid to maintain proper tooth
contact.
19
HYPOID GEAR
☐ Similar to spiral-bevel gears except
that the shafts do not intersect.
☐ Operates more smoothly and more
quietly and is stronger for a given ratio.
☐ Permits a very high drive ratios.
☐ Shaft angles usually 90 deg, but
other angles are possible.
☐ Higher load capacity with the size
and ratio of spiral bevel gear.
20

7/24/25
11
RING GEAR
☐ This is used for larger
transmission drive
reduction. It is designed
using a bevel or spur
gears as gear
combination.
☐ Example applications
includes: concrete mixer,
activate the opening and
closing of grate in rice
husk gasifier, drive for
rotary cylinder of grain
dryers, etc.
21
SPUR GEAR DESIGN PRACTICES
☐ Spur Gear Types are classified into:
☐ Materials
• Hot-rolled steel designation 1045 and 3140
• Ultimate strength of 600 MPa and 724 MPa.
• Brinell hardness number is 215 and 205.
22

7/24/25
12
FORMULA FOR SPUR GEAR
☐ Module = Circular Pitch / p

1
FLUID POWER TRANSMISSION
DRIVES
DESIGN, FABRICATION, AND TESTING OF
AGRICULTURAL MACHINES
by
Engr. Alexis T. Belonio, MS
Agricultural and Biosystems Engineer
ASEAN Engineer
2025 AGRICULTURAL AND BIOSYSTEMS ENGINEERING
BOARD EXAM REVIEWER
1
Disclaimer
Photos, illustrations and schematic diagrams of equipment or machine parts are shown in the
presentation solely for educational purposes to facilitate comprehension of the topics by the students.
Showing them does not endorse a product nor imply criticism of similar products not mentioned.
2

7/24/25
2
HYDRAULIC DRIVE
☐ Hydraulic drive is one of the
power transmission drives
commonly used in powering heavy
transmission drive in agriculture.
☐ This power transmission system
can be found in lifting and moving
components of tractors and heavy
equipment and machinery. An
example of this is when adjusting
the depth of plowing and harrowing
in tillage equipment, when raising
the header of combines, and many
others.
3
☐ Hydraulic power transmission is usually characterized by
operating on heavy load but of slower response speed as
compared with pneumatic power transmission.
☐ Understanding the principle and operation of this method of
transferring power is important to ABEs, especially to those who
are dealing with power and machinery field.
4

7/24/25
3
DEFINITION OF HD
☐ A transmission-drive system that uses pressurized hydraulic fluid to
drive machinery. It transfers hydrostatic flow and pressure of
energy, not of the kinetic energy. In agriculture, hydraulic-drive
systems are commonly used in tractors, in self-propelled machines,
and in field equipment to control depth of tillage operation. They are
also used for front and read loading and unloading operation.
5
Advantages
1. 	Small in size and light in weight;
2. 	High stiffness, high precision, and fast response;
3. 	Large driving force, suitable for heavy load and direct driving;
4. 	Greater flexibility of control and capability of obtaining an infinite
number of speeds between zero and maximum;
5. 	Possible to make provision for automatic reduction of the
delivery of a feed pump as the resistance of movement of a tool
increases;
6. 	Quick reversal without shock;
7. 	Simple and efficient control, both manually and automatically;
8. 	Silent operation with automatic lubrication by the transmission
oil, self-cooling and long life;
9. 	Lower power consumption which adjusts automatically to meet
resistance;
10. Safety ensured with the use of relief valves; and
11. Life tool on hydraulically-operated machine is increased by as
much as 50%.
6

7/24/25
4
Limitations
1. Hydraulic systems require intensive and periodic maintenance;
2. Systems frequently require parts with a very high degree of
precision;
3. Small leak in the hydraulic pipeline will be fatal to the transfer of
power;
4. Hydraulic drive can’t be employed in cases where an accurate
relation must be maintained between coordinated motions;
5. The occurrence of slip in hydraulic transmission drive has the
disadvantages where it is desired to maintain a uniform rate of
traverse; and
6. Speed of movement sometimes varies as affected by the
viscosity of the oil with change in temperature.
7
1. 	Brakes on tractor wheel
2. 	Power stirring for tractors and self-propelled equipment
3. 	Pushing and pulling equipment components
4. 	Raising and lowering attachment of field equipment (plows and
harrows, combine headers, etc.)
5. 	Controlling the depth of tillage such as chisel and subsoiler, etc.
APPLICATIONS OF HD
8

7/24/25
5
1. Hydraulic Pump – Draws the oil from the reservoir and sends it to
the control valve under high pressure. It uses either gear pump,
plunger pump, vane pump, or screw pump. Gear pump is widely
used in tractors because it can flow bigger amount of oil compared
with other pumps; also, oil pressure can be varied from 150 to 200
kg/m2. It is operated by the transmission drive of the engine.
2. Hydraulic Cylinder and Piston – Conveys the oil to the piston,
which raises the lifting arm, to cause it to operate.
3. Hydraulic Tank or Reservoir – Contains the oil used in the
system.
4. Control Valve - Controls the rate of flow of the oil.
5. Safety Valve – Directs the oil to the tank when there is over
pressure in the system.
6. Hose Pipe and Fittings – Delivers the oil from the pump to the
hydraulic cylinder and back to the reservoir.
7. Lifting Arms – Raises or lowers the attached implement.
COMPONENTS OF HD
9
10

7/24/25
6
☐ Open-Type Hydraulic System
☐ Close-Type Hydraulic System
TYPES OF HYDRAULIC SYSTEM
Open-Type Hydraulic System
☐ In an open system, the pump is always working, moving oil through
the pipes without building up pressure. Both the inlet to the pump and
the return valve are hooked up to a hydraulic reservoir.
☐ These are also called “open center” systems, because of the open
central path of the control valve when it is neutral. In this case,
hydraulic fluid returns to the reservoir. The fluid coming from the pump
goes to the device and then returns to the reservoir.
☐ There may also be a relief valve in the circuit to route any excess fluid
to the reservoir.
☐ Filters are usually in place to keep the fluid clean.
11
Advantages & Limitations of Open-Type Hydraulic System:
• 	Open systems tend to be better for low-pressure applications;
• 	They also tend to be cheaper and easier to maintain;
• 	One caution is that they can create excess heat in the system if
the pressure exceeds valve settings;
• 	Another location for added heat is in the reservoir, which needs to
be big enough to cool the fluid running through it.
• 	Open systems can also use multiple pumps to supply power to
different systems, such as steering or control.
An open system can handle more complex repair. Close systems
can work with less fluid in smaller hydraulic lines, and the valves
can be used to reverse the direction of the flow.
Note that the open system can be converted into a close system by
replacing some of the components and adding space for the oil to
go after the return trip.
12

7/24/25
7
Close-Type Hydraulic System
☐ A close-type system connects the return valve directly to the
hydraulic pump inlet.
☐ It uses a single central pump to move the fluid in a continuous loop.
☐ A valve also blocks the oil from the pump, instead sends it to an
accumulator where it stays pressurized. Oil remains under pressure
but doesn’t move unless it is activated.
☐ A charge pump supplies cool, filtered oil to the low-pressure side.
This step maintains pressure within the loop.
☐ A close-type system is often used in mobile applications with
hydrostatic transmissions and uses one pump to power multiple
systems.
13
PNEUMATIC DRIVE
☐ This is a fluid transmission system
that is extensively used in various
industries. This uses compressed
air to transmit and control energy
instead of fluid oil.
☐ In agricultural and biosystems
engineering, this power
transmission system can be found
mostly in agricultural and food
processing plants.
☐ This system rely on a constant
supply of compressed air to make
them work with the use of air
compressor.
14

7/24/25
8
☐ Basically, compressed air is provided by compressor that
stores air from the atmosphere and stores it into a pressure
tank. Compressed air is then supplied to the system through
series of pipes and valves.
☐ Pneumatic is all about using compressed air to do work.
Normally it works at a pressure of 6 to 8 kg/mm2. Maximum
force up to 50kN can be developed.
☐ Actuation of the controls can be done either manually,
pneumatically, or by electrical means. Compressed air is
mainly used to do work by acting on a piston or vane.
15
Advantages:
1. High Effectiveness – Unlimited supply of air from the
atmosphere to produce compressed air. Possibility of easy
storage of large volumes of air. Not restricted by distance as it
can easily be transported through pipes. After use, compressed
air can be released directly into the atmosphere without need of
processing.
2. High Durability and Reliability – Components are extremely
durable and cannot be damaged easily. Pneumatic components
generally are more durable and reliable.
3. Simple Design – Designs are relatively simple. They are more
suitable for use in simple automatic systems. Movement can be
either linear or angular with simple and continuously variable
operation speed.
16

7/24/25
9
4. 	High Adaptability to Harsh Environment – Compared with the
elements of other systems, compressed air is less affected by
high temperature, dust, and corrosive environment, etc.
5. 	Safety Aspect – Safer than electromotive systems because
they can work in inflammable environment without causing fire
or explosion. Overloading pneumatic system only leads to
sliding or cessation of operation.
6. 	Easy Selection of Speed and Pressure – Speed of the
rectilinear and oscillating movements of pneumatic systems is
easy to adjust and is subject to few limitations. The pressure
and the volume of the compressed air can be adjusted by using
a pressure regulator.
7. 	Environment Friendly – Operation does not produce pollutant.
It is environmentally clean and, with proper exhaust air
treatment, can be installed to clean to room standards. It can
work in environment that demand high level of cleanliness.
8. 	Economical – Not expensive. Pneumatic drives are durable
and the cost for maintenance is significantly lower.
17
Limitations
1. 	Low Loading - Cylinders are not very large; hence, cannot
drive too heavy loads.
2. 	Processing Required Before Use – Compressed air must be
processed before use to ensure the absence of water vapor or
of dust.
3. 	Uneven Moving Speed – Since air can be compressed, the
moving speeds of the pistons are relatively uneven.
4. 	Noise – Produced when the compressed air is released from
the system.
18

7/24/25
10
APPLICATIONS PD
1. Pneumatically-operated fruit presses
2. Unloading hoppers and bins to released the product durig
operation.
3. Controlling feeding grains and feeds on a delivery chutes
4. Dairy Processing Plant
5. Food and Feed Processing Plant
19
The types of compressors in the compressed-air systems are:
A. Piston or Reciprocating compressors
• Single-stage or double-stage piston compressor
• Diaphragm compressor
B. Rotary compressors
• Sliding-vane compressor
• Screw conveyor
C. Centrifugal compressors
D. Axial-flow compressors
TYPES OF COMPRESSOR IN
COMPRESSED-AIR SYSTEMS
20

7/24/25
11
Types of Air Compressor
21
COMPONENTS OF PD SYSTEM
1. Compressed-Air Production, Transportation, and Distribution
a. Air Compressor
b. Electric Motor Control Center
c. Pressure Switch
d. Check Valve
e. Storage Tank
f. Auto Drain
g. Filter
h. Air Lubricator
i. 	Pipelines
j. 	Valves
22

7/24/25
12
2. Compressed-Air Consuming System
a. Intake Filter
b. Air Cylinder
c. Air Intake Off Valve
d. Auto Drain
e. Air Service Unit
f. 	Directional Valve
g. Actuators
h. Speed Controllers
23
☐ Air cylinders and motors are the actuators which are used to obtain
the required movements of the mechanical elements of pneumatic
system. Actuators are output devices that converts energy from
compressed air into the required type of action or motion. In
general, pneumatic systems are used for gripping and/or moving
operations in various industries, which are carried out by using
actuators.
Classifications of actuators are as follows:
a. Linear actuators - convert pneumatic energy into linear motion;
b. Rotary actuators - convert pneumatic energy into rotary motion;
and
ACTUATORS
24

7/24/25
13
☐ The construction of hydraulic and pneumatic linear actuators is
similar. However, they differ in their operating pressure ranges.
Typical pressure of hydraulic cylinders is about 100 kg/sq mm and
that of pneumatic cylinders is around 10 kg/sq mm.
Linear Actuator 	Rotary Actuator
25
OPERATING PRINCIPLE
☐ Pneumatic system is a fluid power system that uses the energy
of a prime mover, either electric motor or diesel engine, to drive a
compressor to produce air at a pressure higher than atmospheric.
☐ The potential energy stored within the compressed air, which is
confined in the storage and distribution systems, is used to
transmit power. That is, when the air is used to operate a
machine, it will expand and release its energy.
☐ The power obtained by the machine is related to the pneumatic
system’s operating pressure and the airflow rate.
26

7/24/25
14
☐ Electric motor transforms electrical energy into mechanical
energy. It is used to drive the air compressor.
☐ The compressed air coming from the compressor is stored in the
air receiver or the tank.
☐ The purpose of air receiver is to smooth the pulsating flow from
the compressor. It also helps the air to cool and condense the
moisture present.
☐ The air receiver must be large enough to hold all the air delivered
by the compressor.
☐ The pressure in the receiver is held higher than the system’s
operating pressure to compensate pressure loss in the pipes.
☐ Also, the large surface area of the receiver helps in dissipating the
heat from the compressed air.
☐ Intake filter also known as air filter is used to filter out the
contaminants from the air.
27
☐ For satisfactory operation of the pneumatic system, the
compressed air needs to be cleaned and dried. Atmospheric air is
contaminated with dust and smoke that are humid. These particles
can cause corrosion. Hence, it is essential to treat the air to get rid
of these impurities. During compression operation, furthermore, air
temperature increases. Therefore, cooler is used to reduce the
temperature of the compressed air. The water vapor or moisture in
the air is separated from the air by using a separator or air dryer.
28

7/24/25
15
Pneumatic Drive in Rice Milling Plant
29
The air treatment can be divided into three stages, as follows:
☐ In the first stage, the large-sized particles are prevented from
entering the air compressor by an intake filter. The air leaving the
compressor may be humid and may be at high temperature.
☐ In the second stage, the compressed air from compressor is
treated. In this stage, the temperature of the compressed air is
lowered using a cooler and the air is dried using a dryer. Air-drying
system can be either adsorption type, absorption type, refrigeration
type, or the type that uses semi-permeable membranes. Also, an
inline filter is provided to remove any contaminant particles present.
This treatment is called primary air treatment.
☐ In the third stage, which is the secondary air treatment, further
filtering is carried out.
AIR TREATMENT IN THE COMPRESSOR
30

7/24/25
16
☐ Lubrication of moving parts of cylinder and valves is very
essential in pneumatic system. For this purpose, compressed-
air lubricators are applied on pneumatic equipment before
operating it.
☐ Lubricator introduces a fine mist of oil into the compressed-air.
This helps in the lubrication of moving components of the system
to which the compressed-air is applied. Usually, correct grade of
lubricating oil is with kinematic viscosity of around 20 to 50
centistokes.
31
GASES USED IN PNEUMATIC SYSTEM
☐ Compressed Air – This is a sustainable supply of gas in a
pneumatic system. It is used for fixed installations such as in
processing plants. Moisture from air has to be removed and a small
quantity of oil is applied to the compressor to prevent corrosion and
lubricate mechanical components.
☐ Compressed Oxygen – This is used for processing plants that has
the danger of poisonous gas from the plant itself since it uses
ambient air (79% nitrogen) or gases to be compressed. Using
compressed oxygen (approx. 21% of air) is safe and performs better
over air. However, cost and safety need to be considered.
32

TESTING AND EVALUATION
OF AGRICULTURAL
MACHINES
DESIGN, FABRICATION, AND TESTING OF
AGRICULTURAL MACHINES
by
Engr. Alexis T. Belonio, MS

7/24/25
2
☐ Analysis of the behavior of a machine compared with the
well-defined standards under ideal and repeatable
conditions.
☐ Performance of the machine parts itself like speed, forces,
functional capacity, power requirement, etc.
☐ During the development stage, it is a process by which the
quality of the machine is enhanced before it undergoes into
final stage prior to commercialization. It is also done to
verify the machine specification before it is finally adopted
for use.
INTRODUCTION
3
☐ Involves the measurement of machine performance under real
farm condition.
☐ Performance of the machine in relation to its environment.
☐ Usually testing done in actual field condition as affected by
parameters such a topography, climate, etc.
☐ Operational conditions, acceptability by the farmers, and many
other variables are considered in this testing.
Evaluation of Agricultural Machines
4

7/24/25
3
SEC. 18. Testing and Evaluation. – Agricultural & fisheries
machinery and equipment to be sold in the market shall pass
through testing and evaluation by the AMTEC in accordance with
the national policies and guidelines to be promulgated by the
Secretary.
Standards
Document, established by consensus, and approved by a
recognized body, that provides for common and repeated
use, rules and guidelines or characteristics for activities or
their results, aimed at the achievement of the optimum degree
of order in a given context
5
1. Determine whether the machine parts
function as designed or not;
2. Observe and gather information on the
specific performance of machine parts;
3. Determine parts of the machine that need to
be modified or improved;
4. Determine the overall performance
(technical and operational) of the machine;
5. Prepare the machine specifications;
6. Determine whether machine performs
according to the specification set by the
manufacturer; and
7. Compare the machine with other similar
machines in terms of technical, economics,

Testing and Evaluation are basically
conducted to:
6

7/24/25
4
1. At the stage of development – Tests conducted during the design
stage, proto-type development, manufacturing stage, as well as
the experiences of users.
2. For the potential beneficiaries – Test conducted for the benefit of
potential users of the machine, to control import in terms of
quality and services offered, to protect the economy, to ensure
safety, and to assess environmental impact.
CATEGORIES OF TESTS
7
1. Verification Test – Test carried out to determine whether the
claims of the manufacturer/supplier of the machine conform
with the actual data and test results. I is also done for
verification of specifications.
2. Acceptance Test – Test conducted to determine the machine
to be supplied is acceptable for use by clients/beneficiaries
based on the performance standard.
3. Routine Test - Test carried out on each and every part of an
equipment to check the specifications which are likely to vary
during production.
KINDS OF TESTS
8

7/24/25
5
Running In Period - preliminary operation of the machine to
make necessary adjustments prior to the conduct of test until the
operation is stable.
Test Rig - Customized device in which all the instruments are set
to facilitate testing of a machine.
9
Notes:
(1) In testing agricultural machines, as
prescribed in the PAES standard of test,
it should be operated by manufacturer’s
representative.
(2) In testing agricultural machines, the first
thing that the engineer must do is to get
acquainted with the construction and
operation features of the machine.
(3) Suspension of Test – when machine
breaks down or malfunctions during the
test, the testing may be suspended at
the discretion of the Test Engineer and
concurred by the manufacturer’s
representative.
10

7/24/25
6
1. 	Measurement of parameters is the essential part of any testing
to be done.
2. 	The and accuracy of measurement will depend on the particular
procedure sophistication of test instruments used.
3. 	SI units are universally accepted units in measurement.
MEASUREMENT
11
1. Time – sec generally used with other parameters.
2. Mass – grams of grains, seeds, soil, fertilizer, etc.
3. Dimension – working area, field dimension, depth of soil, etc.
4. Revolutions – shaft rotation, wheel rotation, etc.

7. Pressure

BASIC MEASUREMENT

7/24/25
7
AMTEC – Agricultural Machinery Testing and Evaluation Center.
This is the premiere and reference testing center of agricultural and
fisheries machinery in the Philippines located at the University of
the Philippines at Los Banos, College, Laguna.
- It aims to promote a self-reliant agricultural and fisheries
machinery industry that would cater to and safeguard the interest
of Filipino farmers and fisher folks.

1. 	Area (m2, ha, etc.)

Derived Measurement
14

7/24/25
8
1.Distance for field
measurement – is
measured by determining the
length of two points with the
use of tape measure or
Engineer’s Transit using
stadia method.
2.Dimension of Machine
Parts – is measured by
means of a push-roll tape,
Vernier caliper for

and outside diameters of
pipes.

Measurement Techniques, Tools
and Instrument
15
4. Temperature – using ordinary
glass bulb thermometer for low
temperature measurement,
bimetallic and capillary
thermometer for slightly high
temperature measurement, or with
thermocouple wire sensor
thermometer for high temperature.
Thermocouple wire with shield are
usually used for a very high
temperature of as much as nearly a
thousand degree C. Infrared
thermometer can measure
surfaces, if needed.

7/24/25
9
5.Pressure – This is measured using
manometer for most low pressure measuring
test. High-pressure measurement is done with
pressure gauges as well as for measuring
vacuum pressure. For high pressure, units as
in psi or kg/m2 or in Pascal. Vacuum gauge
uses in. or mm mercury.
6.Relative Humidity – Simple measurement
using two glass bulb thermometers, one with
wet wick and the other none, can determine the
relative humidity of the ambient
17
5. Speed of Machine – This can
be determined once the
distance and the time required
to traverse the field are known.
Dividing the distance with the
travel time gives the speed of
the machine. Usually, km/hr is
used for field testing.
air. The temperature measured
by the thermometers gives the
RH with the use of
psychrometric chart or
appropriate formula. There are
instruments readily available
which can be used for
measuring RH.
18

A rice thresher was tested in threshing
freshly harvested rice. Tests have shown
that 2000 kilos of palay was threshed in 3
hours time. The amount of loss gathered
were as follows: blower loss is 90 kilos,
separation loss is 200 kilos, unthreshed
loss is 50 kilos, and scattering loss is 120
kilos. What are the percentages losses of
the threshing equipment? What is its
threshing capacity in kg per hour?
Given:
Weight of threshed palay 	- 2000 kg
Threshing time 	- 3 hours
Blower loss 	- 90 kg
Separation loss 	- 200 kg
Unthreshed loss 	- 50 kg
Scattering loss 	- 120 kg
Required: Percentages losses and threshing capacity
39
Solution:
Total Losses 	= 90 kg + 200 kg + 50 kg + 120 kg
= 460 kg
Blower Loss 	= 90 kg x 100 / (2000 kg + 90 kg)
= 4.3%
Separation Loss= 200 kg x 100 / (2000 kg + 200 kg)
= 9.1%
Unthreshed Loss = 50 kg x 100 / (2000 kg + 50 kg)
= 2.4 %
Scattering Loss = 120 kg x 100 / (2000 kg + 120 kg)
= 5.6%
Threshing Capacity = 2000 kg / 3 hours
= 666.67 kg/hr
