REVIEW OF AGRICULTURAL
MACHINERY AND
EQUIPMENT
VOLUME 4 – DESIGN, FABRICATION, AND TESTING OF
AGRICULTURAL MACHINES
by
Engr. Alexis T. Belonio, MS
Agricultural and Biosystems Engineer
ASEAN Engineer
2024 AGRICULTURAL AND BIOSYSTEMS ENGINEERING
BOARD EXAM REVIEWER

Disclaimer
Photos, illustrations and schematic diagrams of equipment or machine parts are shown in the
presentation solely for educational purposes to facilitate comprehension of the topics by the students.
Showing them does not endorse a product nor imply criticism of similar products not mentioned.

☐ Agricultural Machinery – Deals with
the study of the application, use and
management of various agricultural
machines, tools and equipment used for
production and post-production
operations.
☐ Agricultural Mechanization -
Development, manufacture and extension
of appropriate agricultural tools,
implement, and machinery using animal,
human, mechanical, electrical, and other
renewable sources of energy for
agricultural production and development
and post harvest operations.
INTRODUCTION

Classifications of
Agricultural Machines:
☐ Agricultural Field Equipment
a. Agricultural Field Implement
b. Agricultural Tractors
c. Self-Propelled Machines
☐ Farmstead Equipment
a. Livestock Equipment
b. Waste Handling Equipment
c. Material Handling Equipment
d. Crop Drying and Storage
Equipment
e. Others

☐ Agricultural Field Equipment – Equipment designed primarily
for agricultural field operation. 	These include agricultural
tractors, self-propelled machines, implements, and their
combinations.
1. 	Agricultural Tractor – Traction machine designed primarily
to supply power to agricultural implements and farmstead
equipment. 	It propels itself and provides force to the direction of
travel to enable attached soil-engaging and other agricultural
implements to perform their intended function.
2. 	Agricultural Implement - Implement designed to perform
agricultural operations. 	This is further classified into: (a) towed;
(b) mounted; and (c) semi-mounted implements.
3. 	Self-Propelled Machine – Implement designed with integral
power unit to provide both mobility and power for performing
agricultural operations.
4. Self Driven or Autonomous Machine – Computer controlled
machine used for power farming.

☐ Farmstead Equipment – Equipment other than agricultural field
equipment used in agricultural operation for the production of food
and fiber. This includes livestock equipment, waste handling
system, crop drying and milling systems, material handling
systems, and others.
Classifications of Agricultural Field Equipment According to
Operation
☐ Tillage Equipment - Include plow and harrow used to prepare the
land to make it ready for seeding and planting operations.
☐ Crop Establishment Equipment – Equipment used to place
seeds or plant parts into the prepared seedbed and subsequently
fertilize them.

3. Crop Maintenance Equipment – Include cultivating, weeding,
spraying, dusting, as well as irrigation equipment aimed to make
sure that the crop grows to produce its potential yield.
4. Harvesting and Threshing Equipment - Equipment used to
gather and separate the produced from the panicles and make it
ready for primary processing operation.
5. Drying Equipment - Equipment used to reduce the moisture of
the product to a level that it can be stored with minimum loss from
spoilage.
6. Milling Equipment - Equipment used to process the product
ready for consumption.
7. Storage Equipment - Equipment used to keep the product safe
from deterioration or spoilage for prolonged storage period.

☐ Machine used primarily for
traction or pulling purposes.
☐ It can also deliver power for both
stationary and mobile tasks.
☐ It can pull or push implement
through traction from the drive
wheel or pull implement through
the draft developed from the
drawbar.
☐ Its hydraulic drive adjust the
setting or tow implement.
☐ It has a power take off drive that
propels mounted implement.
AGRICULTURAL TRACTOR

☐ They are used as primary tillage
implement that constitutes the initial
major soil-working operation, which is
normally designed to reduce soil
strength, cover plant materials, and
rearrange aggregates.
☐ This includes the following:
1. 	Moldboard Plow – invert soil
2. 	Disk Plow – loosen and invert soil
3. 	Chisel Plow – loosen soil
4. 	Rotary Plow – mix soil and weeds
5. 	Subsoiler – deep loosening of soil
or hardpan
PLOWS

☐ Used as secondary tillage implement
which are designed to control weed growth
and to create specific soil surface
configuration before seeding
☐ This includes the following:
1. 	Disk Harrow
2. 	Peg-Tooth Harrow
3. 	Spring Tooth Harrow
4. 	Comb Harrow
5. 	Power Harrow
HARROWS

☐ Hand-operated machines used
to till small sizes of land enough to
replace draft animals.
☐ This includes the following:
1. 	Hand Tractor - used for pulling
small plows or harrows to
prepare a paddy field.
2. 	Floating-Type Floating Tiller -
equipment used for water-
logged areas where ordinary
power tiller cannot be used.
POWER TILLERS

☐ Machine used to open a furrow, place the
seeds, and cover them in a prepared soil.
☐ This includes he following:
1. 	Drill planter – dropping the seeds
continuously and covering on a furrow.
2. 	Row Planter – dropping and covering the
seeds with specific spacing (row to row and hill
to hill)
3. 	Broadcaster randomly dropping the seed.
4. 	Drum Seeder – dropping pregerminated
rice seeds into the soil.
SEEDER

☐ Machine used to place seedlings or
plant parts in a prepared soil.
☐ This includes the following:
1. 	Rice Transplanter – for
transplanting rice seedlings into
the field.
2. 	Sugar Planter – for placing sugar
cane cuttings into the furrow.
PLANTER

☐ Machine used to break liquid into
droplets of effective size and
distribute them uniformly over the
surface or space to be protected.
☐ This includes the following:
1. 	Compressed-Air Sprayer
2. 	Knapsack Sprayer
3. 	Power Sprayer
4. 	Aerosol Sprayer or Fogging
Machine
SPRAYER

☐ Harvesting machine used for
gathering matured crops from the field.
☐ This includes the following:
1. 	Reaper-Windrower – 	a harvesting
machine used to cut standing crops
and lay them down on the field in an
orderly manner in a row.
2. 	Reaper-Binder – a harvesting
machine used both to cut and to bind
the crops and afterwards lay the
bundles of stalks on the ground.
REAPER

☐ Machine that combines harvesting and
threshing into a single operation. It differs
from combine harvester in that it permits
the removal of grains directly from the
head or panicle without cutting the stalks.
STRIPPER HARVESTER

☐ Self-propelled machine that harvests
and threshes the grain at the same time
to make it ready for drying and
subsequent storage.
☐ This includes the following:
1.Check-Row or Oriental-Type – header
is almost the size size of the machine.
Harvesting s specific with the plant
spacing.
2.Reel-Type or Western-Type – header
is much wider as compared with the
body of the machine. Harvesting is not
specific of the plant spacing.
COMBINE HARVESTER

☐ Machine that separates the rice grain
from the panicle.
☐ This includes the following:
1. 	Hold-on or Thrown-In
2. 	Axial Flow or Radial Flow
3. 	Peg-Tooth, Wire Loop, or Rasp Bar
4. 	With or Without a Cleaner or
Mobile with cleaner
RICE THRESHER

☐ 	Machine used to separate seeds
from the cobs or pods.
☐ This includes the following:
1. 	Corn Sheller
2. 	Peanut Sheller
3. 	Coffee Bean Sheller
4. 	Coffee Sheller
SHELLER

☐ Machine used to reduce the
moisture of the grains from a level that
is in equilibrium with the atmosphere to
about 14% for safe storage.
☐ This includes the following:
1. 	Flatbed Dryer
2. 	Re-circulating Dryer
3. 	Continuous Flow Dryer
4. 	In-Storage Bin Dryer
5. 	Warehouse Dryer
6. 	Flash Dryer
GRAIN DRYER

☐ Machine that is used to convert
paddy into milled rice by removing the
husk ad bran..
☐ This includes the following types:
1. 	Single-Pass Rice Mill and Multiple-
Pass Rice Mill
2. 	Rubber Roll, Stone Disc, Steel-
Fluted Mill, and Centrifugal Huller
RICE MILL

☐ Machine used to lift water at a given flow
rate and head for the purpose of supplying
water to the crop.
☐ This includes the following:
1. 	Axial Pump
2. 	Centrifugal Pump
3. 	Mixed-flow Pump
4. 	Lift Pump
5. 	Screw Pump
IRRIGATION PUMP

☐ Machines used to reduce the size of
materials into granular or powdered form
either by cutting, shearing, impact or their
combinations.
☐ This includes the following:
1. 	Hammer Mill
2. 	Burr Mill
3. 	Steel-Fluted Mill
4. 	Pulverizer
SIZE-REDUCTION EQUIPMENT

☐ Machine used to reduce the size of
fibrous materials and shattered its fiber
through impact action of the beaters or
hammers to loosen.
☐ Commonly used for biofertilizer and for
animal feed production using straw and
grasses as feedstock.
BIOMASS SHREDDER

☐ Equipment used to safely store the
grains immediately after drying without
significant loss in their quality.
☐ This includes the following:
1. 	Bin and Silos
2. 	Bucket elevator
3. 	Belt conveyor
4. 	Screw conveyors
5. 	Etc.
GRAIN STORAGE EQUIPMENT

☐ Farm Development Equipment
a. 	Buldozer
b. Land Leveler
c. Post Hole Digger
☐ Production Equipment
a. Tillage
(1) Plow (Moldboard, Disc, Chisel, rotary, etc.)

b. Seeding and Planting Equipment

LISTS OF FARM EQUIPMENT AND
MACHINES

INTRODUCTION
☐ In designing agricultural machines, understanding of the design
parameters can provide a closest answer in arriving at the goal of
the design.
☐ Design parameters are determined by having these factors
considered. They vary in force, time, length and area as well as in
volume, linear and rotational speeds, pressures, etc.
☐ Agricultural machines are designed considering both theoretical
as well as empirical data obtained through experiments, test results,
and experiences. When all together are considered, it helps in
coming up with a machine that is what is expected by the designer.

☐ All of these are the characteristics that is needed by a designer of
an agricultural machine since agricultural machines are bound to a
much wider factors (machine, environment, social, etc.) as
compared with industrial machinery.
☐ Below describes the different design parameters that are usually
considered in determining the operation performance of agricultural
machines.
☐ Agricultural machines here are those that are small scale in
nature with application most for rice crops.
☐ Strength of materials, power transmission drive selection and
computation needed, bearing selection, and other factors are
described in the separate topics of the handbook.

Moldboard Plow – Basically consists of a
plow share for cutting or slicing soil and a
moldboard to invert or pulverize the soil.
This is very popular in many areas in the
country and widely used by farmers.
Disk Plow – This is circular in shape and
is gaining popularity in wet land paddy soil.
For power tilling, two-bottom disk plow is
commonly used. It is a smoothing
implement with a swath approx. twice of
that of the moldboard. It is advantageous
in terms of repositioning the disk in order
to plow near the edge of the field. Its
disadvantages are the cost, which is more
expensive than the modlboard plow, and
the weight of the power requirement.

A power tiller draws a two-row seeder at 30cm spacing. The seeder
has a 6-pocket metering device and is driven by a 0.4m ground wheel.
If the required hill spacing is 0.3 m, what is the recommended sprocket
ratio for the drive?

= 86.4 deg @ 0.3 m travel
Ratio 	= 86.4 deg / 60 deg
= 1.44

COMPONENTS OF MECHANICAL RICE THRESHER

n Threshing Cylinder – the part of the thresher that rotates about
the axis equipped with either pegs, rasp bar, or wire loop on its
periphery. It is the main part of the thresher that separates the
grains from the panicle.
n Concave – the part of the thresher which encloses the threshing
cylinder and allows the separation of the grains from the panicle.
• 	Lower concave – a semi-circular shape wire mesh or bars
covering the lower portion in which the cylinder rubs and
separates the grains from the panicle and through which the
grains fall.
• 	Upper Concave – a semi-circular-shape top cover of the threshing
cylinder consisting of a metal sheet with louvers and/or grills,
which assist in threshing and in axial movement of the straw.

Compute the drying efficiency of a 1ton-capacity recirculating-type dryer
used to dry paddy from 21 to 14% in 8 hrs. The fuel consumption rate
of the dryer is 7lph of diesel. Assume a 600 kcal/kg heat of vaporization
and a 9,000 kcal/kg heating value of fuel. The density of fuel is 0.76.
Given: 	Capacity - 1 ton 	FCR 	- 7 lph diesel
MC i 	- 21% 	Hv 	- 600 kcal/kg
MC f 	- 14% 	HVF - 9,000 kcal/kg
Td 	- 8 hrs 	δf 	- 0.76
Required: 	Drying Efficiency
Solution:
Wf 	= 1 ton (1-.021)/(1-.14)
= 0.918 ton
WR 	= 1 ton – 0.918 ton
= 81.4 kg
Qo 	= 81.4 kg x 600 kcal/kg
= 48,840 kcal/8 hrs
= 6,104 kcal/hr
Qf = 7 li/hr x 9,000 kcal/kg
x 0.76 kg/li
= 47,880 kcal/hr
Ed = 6,104 kcal/hr x 100/
47,880 kcal/hr
= 12.75%

Compute the overall drying efficiency of a
1ton-capacity flat-bed dryer used to dry paddy
from 21% to 14% in 8 hrs. The fuel
consumption rate of the dryer is 7lph. Assume
a heat of vaporization of 600 kcal/kg and
heating value of fuel of 9,000 kcal/kg. The
specific gravity of fuel is 0.76.
Given: 	Capacity 	- 1 ton
MC initial 	- 21%
MC final 	- 14%
Drying time 	- 8 hours
Fuel consumption rate 	- 7 lph
Heat of vaporization 	- 600 kcal/kg
Heating value of fuel 	- 9,000 kcal/kg
Specific gravity 	- 0.7
Required: 	Drying efficiency

Solution:
WMR 	= 1 ton – [(1 ton (1 – 0.21) / (1 – 0.14)]
= 0.081 ton x 1000 kg/ton
= 81.6 kg
Heat Energy Out 	= 920 kg moisture x 600 kcal/kg moisture
= 48,837 kcal
Heat Energy In 	= 7lph x 8 hr x 9,000 kcal/kg x 1kg/liter x 0.7
= 352,800 kcal
Overall drying efficiency = (48,837 kcal/352,800 kcal) x 100
= 13%
The heat energy out is the total heat utilized in drying the grains while the heat
energy in is the amount of energy used in the fuel in drying the grains.

☐ Shearing is done by placing a piece of

☐ Sawing process of moving a hard-
metal saw blade with teeth along its

metal being cut.

☐ Power Hacksaw – is simply an
improvement of hand hack saw. It is an
extremely economical and efficient way of
cutting bigger sizes of metal bars.
☐ Blades of power hacksaw are available
from 3- to 10-teeth per inch.

to 6-teeth per inch blades are used. For

inch are used.
☐ Stroke per minute ranged from 40 to 150

blade which moves past the piece
being cut in only one direction.
9

soft materials requires larger blades.
☐ The use of too coarse blade on hard metal causes the blade to
become dull very quickly. However, saw with very small teeth
requires longer time to cut metal.
☐ The rule is that at least two teeth should be used when cutting a
piece of metal.

of cutting bars or steel plates having a
thickness of 1/16 to 6 inches.
☐ In flame cutting, the piece of steel must be
heated to its kindling temperature of approx.
1600°F.
☐ Acetylene gas, pure oxygen, and cutting

LASER CUTTING MACHINE
☐ Laser cutting is a technology that use a laser to vaporize material
resulting in a cut edge. Typically used fir industrial manufacturing
application.
☐ A thermal separation process where the laser beam hits the
surface of the material and heat it strongly that it melts or completely
vaporize. Once the laser has completely penetrated the material at
one point, the actual cutting process begins.
☐ Advantages includes cutting of all kind of materials and does not
experience wearing out of the sauces and works with high accuracy
and precision.
☐ Disadvantage it requires massive amount of money for
maintenance.

7/23/25

WIRE CUTTING MACHINE
☐ The machine sends a current between the wire and the workpiece,
causing million of sparks to fly.
☐ The sparking generates heat of about 15,000 F enough to melt
away microscopic bits of the workpiece creating fine cuts and
intricate shape.
☐ Brass is used as electrically charge wire to cut through the work
piece while submerge in a tank of deionized water.
☐ The moving wire erodes any conductive material within 0.0005 in.
of its path while the deionized water cools and flushes away debris
from the cut.

☐ Metal forming machine – The machine suppies work to the

resistance of the material and to initiate and maintain the
formation of he work pieces.

☐ Agriculture is the primary industry
of the Philippines.
☐ Agricultural development can be
speed up through mechanization.
☐ Increase in crop production and

be achieved by the use of
appropriate agricultural machines.

supply of locally-available designs of

become useful for farm operation.

undergoes several phases before it goes
for manufacturing.

are carefully analyze in accordance to the

7/23/25
4
Phase 1 – Conceptual Design Preparation
Sketches are prepared showing the machine to be designed and
explaining how it works.
Phase 2 – Literature Search
Searches for existing machines similar to the machine under
consideration. Results of previous studies can help reduce the
required parameters in developing the machine.
Phase 3 – Preparation of the Design Calculation
Design calculations for the different parameters needed in the
design should be done in order to arrive into the nearest possible
dimension and performance as expected.
GENERAL DESIGN DEVELOPMENT
PHASES (Concept to Final Proto-type
Model for Commercialization)
7
Phase 4 – Preparation of Design and Fabrication Drawing
including Detail Drawing of Parts
This will serve as guide in constructing the proto-type unit of the
machine according to the computed dimension and sizes of parts
as well as the materials needed and specification.
Phase 5 - Preparation of Materials and Tools/Equipment to be
Used I the Fabrication
Materials to be used as per design must be prepared prior to
fabrication. Fabrication tools and equipment must be available so
that the machine can be well fabricated as per design.
Phase 6 – Fabrication of Proto-Type Unit
Proto-type unit of the machine will be first fabricated to determine
its performance once tested.
8

7/23/25
5
Phase 7 – Conduct of Functional and Performance Testing of the
Machine
Testing is conducted to find out whether the machine parts work and
to determine its performance whether the expected result is achieved
or not.
Phase 8 – Modification and Improvement of Parts of the Machine
Machine parts that need modification and improvement after testing
must be done until the designer is fully satisfied.
Phase 9 – Conduct of Pilot Test
Actual field testing and evaluation of the machine at the target
user must be done to further check if the machine can fully
provide the solution to the requirements of target beneficiaries.
Phase 10 – Fabrication of Final Model for Commercialization
Final model is fabricated to check further its acceptability to users
before its commercialization.
9
☐ The designers need to have a full understanding of the variables in
actual field conditions and other factors which influence machinery
performance, including the environmental and human-related factors.
Note that the machine must be operationally reliable and
economically acceptable to farmers.
☐ The designers need to apply engineering principles so that
functional requirements of a certain machine are met. These include
the laws of mechanics, strength of materials, fluid flows, heat transfer,
etc.

AGRICULTURAL MACHINES
10

☐ Designers should have the knowledge of the analytical design
process, which is essential in the design of machine components,
main frames, mounting arrangement, balancing, etc.
☐ Designers must integrate analytical design and results of
previous experimental investigation to develop machines that are
simple to fabricate, affordable, light in weight, easy to maintain, and
require readily-available and low-cost materials.
11
☐ Designer should also be knowledgeable on the level of
manufacturing skills, processes, viability, and cost of materials in
order to have simple machines that could be locally
manufactured.
☐ The design of agricultural machines should involved a multi-
disciplinary approach that involves product design, product
development, testing and evaluation, and modification prior to
commercialization.
12

7/23/25
7
☐ Unless the designer tries to meet the requirements of actual
users, no amount of design work will be utilized.
☐ The success of a good design is indicated by the extent by
which the machine is adopted by farmers.

1. Rational Design – carried out using mathematical formula and
other engineering principles.
2. Empirical Design – based upon empirical formula derived from
existing practices and past experiences.
3. Industrial Design – involved other considerations like aesthetics,
ergonomics, and production aspect.

Compute the diameter of a solid shaft of a flueted mill rotating at a
speed of 100rpm and transmitting a power of 1.2hp. Assume a
design stress for a shear of 6000 psi. Consider that the shaft is
subjected to torsion only.

N 	– 100 rpm
Ss 	– 6000 psi
Hp 	– 1.2
Required: Shaft diameter
Solution:
T 	= 63000 x 1.2 / 100 rpm
= 756 in-lb
D 	= (16 x 756 in-lb / p x 6000 psi) 1/3
= 0.863 in. therefore use 1 in. diameter shaft

DEFINITION
☐ Agricultural Machinery – deals with the
study of the application, use and
management of various agricultural
machines, tools and equipment used for
production and post-production
operations.
☐ Agricultural Mechanization - is the
development, manufacture and extension
of appropriate agricultural tools,
implements, and machinery using animal,
human, mechanical, electrical, and other
renewable sources of energy for
agricultural production and development
and post harvest operations.

☐ Agriculture and Fisheries Mechanization Law – Republic Act
10601 (June 5, 2013) – Improving the Agriculture and Fishery Sector
through Mechanization. 	It covers research, development, and
extension promotion distribution, supply, assembling, manufacturing,
regulation, use, operation and maintenance of project implementation
of agricultural and fishery machinery and equipment.
☐ Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering Law – Republic Act
10915 (July 21, 2016) – An act strengthening, modernizing and
aligning the practice of agricultural engineering in the country into the
internationally recognized practice of agricultural and biosystems
engineering, and for other purposes.
Related Laws

Refers to farm power and machinery for the production, harvesting,
processing, storage, manufacture, preserving, transporting and
distribution of agricultural and biological products/materials and
includes, but not limited to, tractors and their attachments, power
tillers, seeders, transplanters, windmills, harvesting machines, crop
protection and maintenance equipment, irrigation equipment and
accessories, greenhouses and thermal conditioning equipment,
livestock, poultry, fishery and forest equipment, slaughter equipment,
meat/fishery and crop processing equipment, post harvest machines
such as milling machines, dryers, threshers, grain and other strippers,
agricultural transport machinery and storage.
Agricultural and 	Biosystems 	Power and
Machinery

Classifications of Agricultural Machines
☐ Agricultural Field Equipment
(1) Agricultural Field Implement
(2) Agricultural Tractors
(3) Self-Propelled Machines
☐ Farmstead Equipment
(1) Livestock Equipment
(2) Waste Handling Equipment
(3) Material Handling Equipment
(4) Crop Drying and Storage
Equipment
(5) Others

☐ Agricultural Field Equipment – This are equipment designed
primarily for agricultural field operation. These include agricultural
tractors, self-propelled machines, implements, and their
combinations.
(1) 	Agricultural Tractor – A traction machine designed primarily to
supply power to agricultural implements and farmstead equipment.
It propels itself and provides force to the direction of travel to enable
attached soil-engaging and other agricultural implements to perform
their intended function.
(2) 	Agricultural Implement - An implement that is designed to
perform agricultural operations. 	This are further classified into: (a)
towed; (b) mounted; and (c) semi-mounted implements.
(3) 	Self-Propelled Machine – An implement designed with integral
power unit to provide both mobility and power 	for performing
agricultural operations.

☐ Farmstead Equipment – These are equipment other than
agricultural field equipment used in agricultural operation for the
production of food and fiber. 	These include livestock
equipment, waste handling system, crop drying and milling
systems, material handling systems, and others.

INTRODUCTION
☐ Internal combustion engine (ICE) is a device that produces
power by burning normally liquid fuel inside the combustion
chamber of an engine.
☐ It is conventionally used as power source for agricultural machines
to perform various tasks in crop production, in poultry and livestock
farms, as well as in fishery mechanization.
☐ In agriculture and fishery mechanization, small single-cylinder
engines are commonly used by farmers, ranging from 3hp to 16hp
gasoline and up to slightly higher hp diesel engines.
☐ Multiple-cylinder diesel engines are commonly adopted for large
applications like tractors, self-propelled combine harvester, and
many others.
☐ Knowledge on ICE would be helpful for ABE especially when
dealing agricultural and fishery mechanization. It serves as
backbone in ensuring proper and efficient operation of the different
agri-fishery machines.

USES OF ICE
Power Source for Tractors
Power Source for Harvesters
Driving Power Tillers
Power Source for Engines
Used to Drive Generator


CLASSIFICATIONS OF ICE
☐ Spark-Ignition Engine
• 	Uses spark to ignite the fuel.
• 	Uses gasoline as fuel.
• 	Has a carburetor to mix fuel and air.
☐ Compression-Ignition Engine
• 	Uses high compression to raise the
temperature of the air in a chamber and
ignites the injected fuel without a spark.
• 	Uses diesel as fuel.
• 	Uses an atomizer to spray the fuel inside
the combustion chamber of the engine.
According to Ignition of Fuel
Spark-Ignition
Compression-
Ignition

According to Number of Stroke
☐ Two-Stroke-Cycle Engine
• Produces power in one revolution of the
crankshaft.
• Fuel and oil is mixed in the combustion
chamber.
• Usually high in speed and light in weight.
☐ Four-Stroke-Cycle Engine
• Produces power in two revolutions of the
crankshaft.
• Fuel is burned inside the combustion
chamber.
• Relatively low in speed and heavy in
weight.
Two-Stroke
Four-Stroke

According to Number of Cylinders
☐ Single-Cylinder Engine
• 	One piston
• 	Appropriate for small engines
commonly used in the farm,
☐ Multiple-Cylinder Engine
• 	More than one piston (2, 3, 4, 6, 8,
12)
• 	Appropriate for high-powered
engines for driving tractors and
self-propelled equipment.
Single-Cylinder
Multiple-Cylinder

Feature 	Compression-Ignition Engine 	Spark-Ignition Engine
Type of Cycle
Used
● Diesel cycle where combustion occurs at a
constant pressure.
● Otto cycle where combustion occurs at a
constant volume.
Introduction of fuel
to the engine
● Fuel is injected into the combustion
chamber towards the end of the
compression stroke.
● Fuel starts burning instantly due to the high
pressure.
● Fuel pump and injector are required.
● During the piston's suction stroke, a mixture
of air and fuel is injected from the cylinder
head.
● The air-fuel mixture is injected via the
carburetor that controls the quantity and
the quality of the injected mixture.
Ignition of fuel 	● Ignition of fuel occurs due to compression
of the air-fuel mixture, spark plug not
needed.
● Spark plug is placed in the cylinder head of
an engine which creates spark to burn the
fuel.
Compression ratio
for the fuel
● Compression ratio for air is 16 to 20. The
high compression ratio of air creates high
temperature ensuring diesel fuel to self
-ignite.
● Compression ratio of the fuel ranges from 6
to 10, depending on the size of the engine
and of the power to be produced.
Weight of the
engine
● CI engines are heavier than SI engines. 	● Engine weight is lighter than diesel engine.
Speed achieved by
the engine
● CI engines are heavier and the fuel is
heterogeneously burned; hence, producing
lower speeds.
● Petrol or SI engines are lightweight and the
fuel is homogeneously burned; hence,
achieving very high speeds.
Thermal efficiency
of the engine
● The value of compression ratio is higher;
hence, these engines have the potential to
achieve higher thermal efficiency.
● The lower compression ratio of SI engines
reduces their potential to achieve higher
thermal efficiency.

Compression-Ignition Engines

dimension, and performance

☐ It is a graphical representation showing the abilities of rotating
equipment, like engine, at various operating conditions.
☐ It gives the characteristics of an engine in terms of power, fuel
consumption, and torque for a given operating speed .

AGRICULTRAL TRACTOR
☐ Tractor is an engineering vehicle specifically designed to deliver a
high tractive effort (or torque) at slow speeds for the purpose of
hauling a trailer or a machinery used in agriculture.
☐ A machine used primarily for traction or for pulling an implement.
☐ A versatile machine and a mobile power source for wide variety of
agricultural tasks.
☐ A machine that can perform both stationary and mobile jobs.
☐ A machine that can pull or tow implement through traction from the
drive wheel and/or pull implement through the draft developed from
its drawbar hitch, or power implement through its PTO drive.

FUNCTIONS OF TRACTORS
☐ Pulling machine behind it;
☐ Pushing machine in front of it;
☐ Operating machine mounted on it;
☐ Transmitting power to other machines through the PTO drive;
☐ Raising, lowering, and controlling machines and attachment by
its hydraulic power;
☐ Driving machines through belt power;
☐ Transmitting power through flexible shaft; and
☐ Furnishing power for fast highway transportation and handling.

Advantages 	and Disadvantages
☐ Can work continuously even with heavy load.
☐ Not affected by bad weather.
☐ Can be adapted for draft, belt, or PTO work.
☐ Has considerable range of working speed.
☐ Requires little attendance when not in use.
☐ Readily available when urgently needed.
☐ Requires small storage space.
Advantages
☐ Limited overload capacity.
☐ Requires cash outlay for fuel and lubricants.
☐ Requires the operator to have some mechanical skill for
successful operation.
☐ Under some condition, inflexibility of size of power unit for
economical power production.
Disadvantages

DESCRIPTION OF AGRICULTURAL
TRACTORS
☐ Compact Tractor – A four-wheel
tractor of less than 20hp. 	It is used
for landscaping and gardening
rather than for massive agricultural
tasks. It is equipped with single
12in. moldboard plow and is
capable to plow 1 hectare within 11
to 14 hours.
☐ Farm Tractor – A four-wheel
tractor with no less than 20
brake horsepower. It is used
for massive agricultural tasks
such as plowing, harrowing,
seeding and planting, and
other operations.

☐ Special Type of Tractors

consists mainly of two heavy-
duty endless link device
known as tract for traction
purposes. It is used for
heavy-duty operations such
as earth moving and other
industrial jobs requiring
higher power.
• 	All-Purpose or Row-Crop
Tractor – It is designed to
handle field and belt jobs,
including planting and inter-
tillage activities.

- Improves stirring and

TRACTOR SIZE
Tractor size can be determined based on the following:
☐ Weight – The heavier the tractor, the bigger is its capacity.
☐ Horsepower – The higher the tractor horsepower, the bigger is its
size and the more it is capable of doing wider operations.
☐ Implement Capacity – The more the tractor can draw implement,
the bigger is its size and the faster it can finish the operation.

DRAWBAR PULL
☐ It is one of the most important factors affecting the performance
of a tractor.
☐ Plowing and other operations are affected by the drawbar
performance of the tractor.
☐ Drawbar pull is affected by the wheel slip and the engine power.
It is also affected by the tractor weight and type, the type and
shape of the running gears or wheel condition of the ground
surface, inflation pressure of tires, and others.

ENGINE TERMINOLOGIES
☐ Carburetion – for supplying the air/fuel mixture to the combustion
chamber of a combustion engine.
☐ Combustion Chamber – space inside an engine block and cylinder
head.
☐ Compression - 	to create pressure in the combustion chamber.
☐ Compression Ratio – the ratio of volume displaced by the piston to
the volume at the cylinder head of the engine.
☐ Displacement – volume displaced by the piston as it moves up and
down the combustion chamber commonly expressed in liters.
☐ Fuel – a substance either gasoline or diesel that has an energy to
produce power when ignited.
☐ Horsepower – unit of power equivalent to 746 watts.
☐ Ignition System – electrical component of gasoline engine that
produces a high voltage arc or spark across the air gap of the spark
plug to ignite combustible mixture of fuel and air.

☐ Lubricant – substance used to reduce friction, heat, and wear
when applied as a thin film between solid surface.
☐ Piston – cylindrical-shaped engine part that moves up and
down in the combustion chamber to displace volume and create
compression.
☐ Power – rate of consumption of energy from fuel which
produces work per unit time through reciprocating motion and
converts it to rotational motion at a given torque and speed.


FACTORS FOR ENGINE TO
PRODUCE POWER
Gasoline Engine 	Diesel Engine
Compression 	The combustion chamber
must be capable of
compressing air/fuel
mixture in order to create
explosion to complete
power stroke.
The combustion chamber must
be high enough to create the
compression needed to raise
the temperature of the air to
combust the fuel as it enters
the combustion chamber.
Carburetion/
Atomizer
The carburetor must
supply the correct air/fuel
mixture.
The atomizer must be capable
enough to spray the fuel as
thin as possible to create
combustion.
Ignition 	The ignition system must
provide the spark or arc
across the spark plug at
the correct time to ignite
the air/fuel mixture.
The temperature of the
compressed air must be high
enough to ignite the fuel.
Compression ratio of more
than 1:12 is necessary.

ADVANTAGES OF COMPRESSION-
AGAINST SPARK-IGNITION
ENGINE
1. 	Reliability is much higher than SI engine since in case of failure in
the battery, ignition or carburetor system cannot operate; unlike in CI
system, fuel injector for each cylinder has less failure.
2. 	The distribution of fuel to each cylinder is uniform as each has
separate fuel injector; whereas, in SI engine the distribution of fuel
mixture is not uniform owing to the design of single carburetor at the
intake manifold only.
3. 	Since the servicing of fuel-injection system is longer, its
maintenance is less that that of SI engine.
4. 	The expansion ratio of CI engine is higher that that of SI engine
which means the heat loss to the cylinder wall is less. The cooling
system of CI engine can be made smaller in dimension.

5. 	The torque characteristics of CI engine are more uniform which
results in better performance.
6. 	CI engine can be switched over from part load to full load soon
after starting from cold; while, SI engine requires warming up
first.
7. 	The fuel for CI engine is cheaper (except today) that SI engine.
8. 	The fire risk in the CI engine is minimized due to the absence
of ignition system.
9. 	On part load, the specific fuel consumption of CI engine is low.

ADVANTAGES OF TWO-STROKE OVER
FOUR-STROKE CYCLE ENGINE
1. 	Two-stroke cycle engine
gives one working stroke to
each revolution of the
crankshaft. The power
developed for the same
engine speed and cylinder
volume is twice than that of
the four- stroke engine.
Because of poor scavenging
in two-stroke cycle, however,
only 50-60% extra power is
developed.


2. 	The turning moment on the crank shaft of the engine is more
uniform. Hence, two-stroke engine requires lighter flywheel
than four-stroke engine.
3. 	Simple in construction. The design of ports is much simpler
and maintenance is easier than the valve mechanism.
4. 	The power required overcoming the frictional resistance of
the suction and exhaust stroke is saved resulting in some
economy of scale.
5. 	Owing to the absence of cam, camshaft, rockers, etc. of the
valve mechanism, the mechanical efficiency is higher.
6. 	For the same power, two-stroke engine is more compact and
requires less space than a four-stroke cycle engine making it
suitable for use for small machines.
7. 	Lighter in weight for the same power and speed, especially
when the crankcase compression is used.
8. 	Due to its simpler design, it requires fewer spare parts.
9. 	A two-stroke cycle engine can be easily reversed if it is of
the valve-less type.

DISADVANTAGES OF TWO-STROKE
OVER FOUR-STROKE CYCLE ENGINE
1. 	The scavenging being not
very efficient in a two-stroke
engine, the dilution of the
charges takes place which
result in poor thermal
efficiency.
2. 	The two-stroke spark ignition
engines do not have a
separate lubrication system
and normally, lubricating oil
is mixed with the fuel. This
is not effective as the
lubrication of a four-stroke
engine. Therefore the parts
of the two-stroke engine are
subjected to greater wear
and tear.


3. Some of the fuel pass directly to the exhaust, hence, fuel
consumption per horsepower is comparatively higher.
4. 	With heavy loads, a two-stroke engine gets heated up due to
the excessive heat produced making the running of the engine
riot but very smooth at light load.
5. 	It consumes more lubricating oil because of the greater
amount of heat generated.
6. 	Since the ports remain open during the upward stroke, the
actual compression starts only after both the inlet and exhaust
ports have been closed. Hence, the compression ratio of this
engine is lower than that of a four-stroke of the same
dimension. As the efficiency of an engine is directly
proportional to its compression ratio, the efficiency of two-
stroke cycle engine is lower than that of the four-stroke of the
same size.

GASOLINE ENGINE
Engine Not Starting – The engine does not run even the
starting rope is pulled.
1. 	No Gas – In order for the engine to start running, the
carburetor must have a supply of fuel. In small engine, it
appears to have gas when actually none is getting to the
engine. Try rocking the engine back and forth to listen for
fuel sloshing. If you have a gas canister try filling up the
tank and give another shot.

2. 	Damaged Spark Plug – It is one of the consumables of the
engine and it has the tendency to die over a period of
usage. It supplies the spark for the fuel and air mixture to
ignite. Dead spark plug appears corroded with carbon
deposits on its tip.
3. 	Dirty/Clogged Air Filter – If the air filter is too clogged with
dirt and dust, air will not be sufficient in reaching the
cylinder causing the fuel not to burn and the engine not to
start.
4. 	Starter is Shot – In a rope-starter operated engine, the
clutch engagement on the crankshaft already worn out over
time until the starter no longer catch its contact point.

Engine Runs Poorly and/or Stall After Starting
1. 	Governor Needs Adjustment – Spring mechanism that
controls the speed and load of the engine. Spring can lose its
elasticity and subsequently alter the performance of the
engine.
2. 	Engine Accessories are Jammed – If the engine is used to
power a device, ensure that the device that is being powered
is not jammed.

Excessive Smoke while Engine is Running – Engine produces white
or blue smoke while running.
1. 	Oil has reached the exhaust manifold. If the engine is tilted
excessively to one side or the oil is overfilled, oil may leak out of its
chamber and onto the exhaust manifold. The oil burns due to the
exhaust manifold. Check oil level to ensure it is within the
recommended range.
2. 	Cracked head gasket – It is a thin sheet that forms a seal between
the engine block and the engine head. Cracks may cause the oil to
leak and enter the cylinder and burn.

Engine Overheating – noticeably higher than normal and is not
running right.
1. 	Blocked cooling fins – dirt, grasses may build up on the
exterior of the engine inhibiting cooling. Just wait the engine to
cool and remove dirt, etc.
2. 	Dirty/Clogged air intake – If air filter becomes too clogged
with dirt or dust, there will be no sufficient air reaching the
cylinder causing the air-fuel mixture not in proper balance.
The engine will not run efficiently and hotter than normal.

Engine Making a Knocking Noise
1. 	Carbon deposit inside the cylinder - Carbon developed
inside the cylinder from burnt fuel may interfere with proper
combustion. Remove the cylinder head and scrape
accumulated carbon.
2. 	Engine has overheated – If the engine begins to get too
hot, the air-fuel mixture may ignite prematurely causing the
engine to make banging noise.
3. 	Spark-plug is damaged – Does not properly ignite the fuel
which causes the knocking noise in the engine.

Most Frequent Diesel Engine Problems and Solution
1. 	Engine overheating
2. 	Oil leakages
3. 	Oil supply problem
4. 	Using a wrong fuel
☐ Engine Overheating - 	It is caused when engine is pushed
too hard and can give rise to a whole host of negative side
effects such as damage to the bearings and crankshaft,
piston expanding and scraping against cylinder walls,
cylinder head swelling, distorting and breaking.
DIESEL ENGINE

☐ Oil Leak – This stems largely from issues with diesel parts such
as aged seals and gaskets which no longer work effectively. If
left unattended, oil leaks can cause serious diesel problems as
they pose both environmental threats and serious fire risks that
can result in complete failure.
☐ Oil Supply Problem – This stems out from either incorrect oil
use or lack of oil. Using the wrong-type of oil negatively affects
engine parts; whereas, not priming the engine causes it to run
on air rather than on oil, breaking the engine in the process.
☐ Using the Wrong Fuel – Diesel engines are high susceptible to
damage caused by misfueling, which commonly results in either
the need for new diesel engine parts or a completely new
engine altogether. To avoid this common problem with diesel
engines, be sure always to double-check fuel type you are
about to use before refueling.

Parts of Diesel Engine that Frequently Encounter
Problems
1. 	Piston
a. Timing belt snapping.
b. Piston rings becomes worn out.
c. Piston slap (noisy piston).
d. Piston becoming burnt (usually dirty fuel injectors).
e. Piston becoming cracked (caused by frequent use of
poor quality fuel.


2. Gasket - The most common failure in gaskets is overheating via
coolant leaks. In general, diesel engines are more prone to
gasket failure than other types of engine largely because diesel
gaskets regularly face higher combustion pressure. Repair of
diesel gaskets is made all the more complicated by intricate
nature of diesel engines.

3. Cylinder Head. - Problems related to this are usually
categorized by loss of compression. Cracks in cylinder head,
which leads to leakages, are also a common issue as are
internal casting defects.

4. Bearings - 	They face a lot of stress due to the daily friction
experienced, such as insufficient lubrication and improper
selection of bearing material for the engine type at hand.

Most Common Causes of Multiple-Cylinder Diesel Engine
Troubles
☐ Abnormal exhaust
☐ Hard to start
☐ Lack of power
☐ Overheating
☐ Defective instruments
☐ Air leakages
☐ Fuel leakages
☐ Malfunctioning of fuel injection equipment


Abnormal Exhaust
Black Smoke – Insufficient combustion of
fuel due to inadequate supply of air for the
combustion. This arises due to the
restricted air intake.
Cause:
☐ Failure of turbocharger
☐ Restricted air intake
☐ Improper valve clearance
☐ Injector malfunctioning
☐ Fuel-injection pump malfunctioning
☐ Disturbed fuel timing
☐ Poor grade of fuel

Trouble Shooting:
☐ Check the turbocharger speed and charge
air pressure. Overhaul the turbocharger in
case of low speed and low charge
pressure.
☐ Check restriction in air intake.
☐ Check and adjust the valve clearance.
☐ Calibrate the injector and adjust the
correct working pressure.
☐ Check the fuel injection pump and check
the pressure developed by each pump
with steady holding of fuel pressure.
☐ Check and re-adjust the fuel timing.
☐ Change fuel with quality one.

Blue Smoke – This is due to the lubricating oil
conveyed into the combustion chamber and
getting burnt.
Cause:
☐ High oil level in engine sump.
☐ Excessive wear down of cylinder piston
assembly due to increased clearances
between piston and cylinder liner tube oil
carried into the combustion chamber.
☐ Worn out piston rings where the compression
ring is not able to scrape the oil and it remains
on the cylinder walls and conveyed into the
combustion chamber.
Remedy:
☐ Check the sump level and maintain the correct
working level.
☐ Check the compression pressure and if the
results of multi-unit are negative then
undertake overhauling.

Grey (Cloudy) Smoke
Cause:
☐ Retarded injection timing due to
leaky fuel injector, low injection
pressure, or poor atomization of
fuel.
☐ Leaky valve seat rings.
☐ Excessive water mixed in fuel.
Remedy:
☐ Test and calibrate the injectors.
☐ Check the compression pressures.
If less than the specified limit, strip
down the unit and check the valve
seat rings and condition the piston
and liners.
☐ Drain the water from the fuel tanks
regularly.


Engine Hard to Start
Reasons:
☐ Low starting air pressure.
☐ Main air starting valve
malfunctioning.
☐ Stuck starting valve in the cylinder
head.
☐ Ingress of water into the
combustion chamber due to leaky
cylinder head causing hydraulic lock
and restricting the movement during
the starting.
☐ Air in fuel system.
☐ Choked fuel filters.
☐ Closed fuel line valves.
☐ Low fuel oil level in tank or no fuel
in tank.
☐ Water in fuel.
☐ Faulty fuel injector.
☐ Wrong fuel timing.
☐ Fuel-injection pump
leaking.
☐ Leaky fuel-injection
pipes.
☐ Fuel rack stuck in one
position.
☐ Broken deliver valve and
spring.
☐ Cold engine


Lack of Power
☐ Choked air supply
☐ Restriction in the exhaust line
☐ Wear in the valve train
☐ Fuel-injection valve not working properly
☐ Fuel-injection pumps are not supplying the metered fuel with
appropriate pressure
☐ Lack compression
☐ Worn piston rings
☐ Heavy carbon deposits on intake valve or valve seats
☐ Leaky inlet valve
☐ Defective turbocharger
☐ Fouled charge air cooler

Engines Run on Air But Don’t Start
Firing
☐ Valve open
☐ Airlock in the fuel system
☐ Choked filter
☐ Incorrect setting fuel pump
☐ High viscosity fuel
☐ Low lubricating oil level in tank
Excessive Back Pressure
☐ Choked exhaust outlet
☐ Insufficient lift of exhaust valve

Engine Slows Down or Stops
☐ Defective governor driving gear
☐ Low fuel delivery by fuel valve/injector
☐ Fuel contaminated by water
☐ Overload
☐ Unbalance load in cylinders
☐ Cooling water pump stopped/not working
Engine Over Speeds
☐ Governor gear damaged or out of order
☐ Inadequate response of fuel pump to the governor
Engine Kicks Back
☐ Leaky or sticky starting valve
☐ Sluggish roller movement on cam base circle or low air pressure


Low Compression Pressures in Cylinders
☐ Leaky valves
☐ Carbon formation on the valve face
☐ Leaky or broken piston rings
☐ Cylinder head joint leaking
☐ Choked air inlet filter
☐ Dirty charge air filter in the turbocharged engine
☐ Turbocharger not running at the correct speed
Incorrect Firing Times
☐ Wrong clearance between fuel pump cam and roller.
☐ Incorrectly meshed transmission gear between the main gear
and the camshaft.

Engine Runs Irregularly
☐ Damaged governor
☐ Fuel line or fuel pump is with air lock
☐ Water in fuel
☐ Overload
☐ Leaky fuel pump valve
☐ Leaky injection nozzle
☐ Sticking fuel pump
☐ Defective/enlarged injection nozzle
☐ Faulty delivery of fuel
Engine Stops Suddenly
☐ No fuel
☐ Water in fuel
☐ Airlock
☐ Seized piston
☐ Vapor lock in fuel line

Heavy Knocking-in Cylinders
☐ Too early or too late injection
☐ Choked or enlarged nozzle holes
☐ Improper setting back of injector valve
☐ Abnormal pressure setting of the injection nozzle
☐ Slack top or bottom bearing
☐ Piston slap
☐ Too high tapped clearance or inlet or exhaust valve
☐ Overload
☐ Insufficient lubricating oil
☐ Too hot circulating water
Pre-Ignition in Cylinders
☐ Disturbed injection nozzle
☐ Early injection
☐ Early ignition

One Cylinder Stops Firing
☐ Airlock
☐ Leaky fuel pump
☐ Unequal fuel supply
☐ Wrong fuel valve timing
☐ Fallen of compression
Lubricating Oil Pressure Drops
☐ Choked oil filter
☐ Leaky / bypassed valve
☐ Low oil level in the sump

High Cooling Water Outlet Temperatures
☐ Vapor lock in the water line
☐ Low water pressure
☐ Choked plate heat exchanger
☐ Failure of cooling water pump
☐ Engine too hot
☐ Malfunctioning of thermostat valve
Knocking at Top Dead Center
☐ Early injection
☐ Wrong Fuel

a. 	Power stroke is much higher for the

d. 	All of the above
e. 	None of the above

6. 	Possible cause(s) if engine does
not start.
a. 	No gas
b. 	Damage spark plugs
c. 	Dirty/clogged air filter
d. 	All of the above
7. Possible cause(s) when engine
runs poorly and or stall after starting.
a. 	Governor needs adjustment.
b. 	Engine accessories are jammed.
c. 	All of the above
d. 	None of the above
8. Excessive smoke while engine is
running due to:
a. 	Oil has reached exhaust manifold
b. 	Cracked cylinder head gasket
c. 	All of the above

a. 	Blocked cooling fins

a. 	Damage to bearings and crankshaft

and braking

13. Engine parts that frequently

a. 	Piston
b. 	Gasket

14. Most common causes of
multiple-cylinder diesel engine
troubles

TILLAGE
☐ Tillage - is the mechanical manipulation of soil for any desired
purpose.

Primary Objectives
n Elimination and permanent
control of the original

n Creation of conditions
favoring the germination,
emergence, and growth of
the cultivated plants; and
n Conservation and
improvement of the soil as

n Cutting of soil;
n Shear plane formation
(crumbling, pulverization) in

n Roller Packer – An implement for crushing soil clods and

n Roller Harrow – An implement used for seedbed preparation which

n Bed Shaper – A soil-handling implement which forms uniform

¾Culti-Packer – Used to compact the surface of the soil in order to

¾Soil Sifter – Used to remove stones from the field by stirring

as a medium for the growth of

INTRODUCTION
☐ Rice farming is one of the major farming businesses of Filipino
farmers.
☐ The wet paddy field condition in rice farming operation has found
difficulty to employ four wheel tractors as source of power for land
preparation.
☐ With the introduction of two wheel tractor in the early 60’s has
significantly change land preparation from water “buffalo” pulling
plow and harrow to a two-wheel tractor.
☐ The need for a much faster operation for most water logged areas
in the country has led the development of the puddling-type
floating tiller to increase the field capacity of small power machines
in preparing rice field for planting.
☐ Recently, a much faster and versatile tillage machines that can
perform the operation of two wheeled tractor for plowing, rotary
tilling, and even harrowing has led many farmers to finish land
preparation in a much shorter period.

PUDDLING-TYPE FLOATING TILLER
A float-assisted waking-type tractor
or a hydro tiller. It is equipped with a
front-mounted tilling wheel and a
floatation structure to skid in a water-
logged fields. The float structure is a
component of the tiller which
provides buoyancy for the tiller
during operation. The tilling wheel
consists of a single or pair of wheels
with radially-mounted tilling blades
attached to a common shaft or axle
that is supported; power is
transmitted by means of a heavy-
duty sprocket-and-chain drive.

Advantages:
1. 	Can be used to puddle low lying fields uniformly with less
operation and reduced cost;
2. 	Suitable for both primary and secondary tillage when field has
been soaked for at least half a day to soften the soil;
3. 	Most suitable for water-logged marshy lands;
4. 	Easy to maneuver and to control the operation of the machine;
5. 	Faster and more economical to use in water-logged areas for
rice cultivation than conventional two-wheel tractor.
6. 	Can increase production by mixing weeds and green manure
effectively in the soil;
7. 	Small diesel engine can be used to power the machine; and
8. 	Environmentally and economically beneficial.


Disadvantages:
1. 	Considerable effort is required to maneuver tiller and control
its forward speed;
2. 	The rounded bottom of the float displaces the plastic soil and
creates furrows which increase the tine effort and the cost of
subsequent harrowing and leveling;
3. 	Difficult to transport and cannot be used for subsidiary
operation, such as harrowing or transport types of float tillers.

BOAT TRACTOR
Boat tractor – is a new tillage technology
for rice crops comprising of a boat-

control the front end of the machine. The
drive wheel of the machine is provided

tilling wheel roller from the gear box. The
operating levers are provided to be able

separately for mobility. The engine is
located in front of the machine to provide
power to the gear box through belt and
pulley drive.

The boat tractor can prepare rice field in
much shorter time and can operated even
in heavily water logged field condition.
The machine is a riding-type and
operation is much easier the other rice
tillage equipment.

SEEDING AND PLANTING
EQUIPMENT
VOLUME 3 – AGRICULTURAL MACHINERY AND
MECHANIZATION
by
Engr. Alexis T. Belonio, MS
Agricultural and Biosystems Engineer
ASEAN Engineer
2024 AGRICULTURAL AND BIOSYSTEMS ENGINEERING
BOARD EXAM REVIEWER

Disclaimer
Photos, illustrations and schematic diagrams of equipment or machine parts are shown in the
presentation solely for educational purposes to facilitate comprehension of the topics by the students.
Showing them does not endorse a product nor imply criticism of similar products not mentioned.

INTRODUCTION
☐ Seeding and planting equipment are
used to place the seeds or plant parts
into the soil and keep them from weeds
and insect pests and diseases until they
are fully grown and ready for harvesting.

☐ Seeders – are machines used to
place seeds such as corn, rice, etc.
in the soil.
☐ Planters – are machines used to
place plant parts such as sugar
cane cuttings, rice seedlings, etc. in
a prepared soil.

Terminologies
☐ Broadcasting – randomly scattering
of seeds on the surface of the field.
☐ Drill Seeding – randomly dropping
and covering of seeds in furrow.
☐ Precision Planting – accurate
placing of single seed/plant at about
equal interval in rows.
☐ Hill Dropping – placing of group of
seeds at about equal interval in rows.
☐ No-Till Planting – procedure in
which planting is made directly into an
unprepared seedbed or untilled soil.

☐ Minimum Tillage –
minimum soil manipulation
necessary for crop production
or for meeting tillage
requirement under existing soil
condition.
☐ Seed-Tape Planting –
planting system wherein the
seeds are deposited either
singly or in group on a water
soluble tape (polyethylene
oxide) under controlled
condition.

FUNCTIONS OF SEEDER/PLANTER
☐ Meters seeds/plant parts of different sizes and shapes.
☐ Places the seeds/plant parts in the acceptable pattern or
distribution in the field.
☐ Places seeds/plant parts accurately and uniformly at the desired
depth in the soil; and
☐ Covers the seeds/plant parts optionally and compact the soil
around them to enhance germination and emergence.


CLASSIFICATIONS OF SEEDER
1. Drill – a machine that prepares the soil, meters the seed, and
positions the seed in one operation.
☐ According to Methods of Seeding

2. Field Distributor – a machine consisting of a seed box with metering
device in the bottom of the hopper. This is used to prepare the soil for
the seed as well as for fertilizer.

3. Broadcaster – a machine that meters the materials onto a revolving
flange wheel, less expensive to purchase, and has the highest work
capacity but is hardest to calibrate because of uneven distribution from
the flange wheel, unequal seed weight and shape, and difficulty with
wind as well as uneven soil surface.

1. Manually Driven – Machine that is pushed or pulled by human.
2. Animal Drawn – Power source is by the use of draft animal
harnessed either singly or in multiple animals.
☐ According to Source of Power

3. Power-Tiller Operated – seeding or planting machine that is
drawn by a small walking-type tractor powered by a separate
engine. The machine sometimes obtain power from the engine
through the belt-and-pulley drive.
4. Tractor Driven – seeding or planting machine that is either
mounted or pulled-type units. Power source for the machine is
transmitted through the power take-off drive of the tractor.

BASIC COMPONENTS OF A SEEDER
☐ Seed Box – 	used to hold and
contain the seeds in the seeder.
☐ Metering Device – used to meter
the seeds or control the rate of
delivery either in bulk or as single
seed into the seed tube.
☐ Seed Tube – used to convey the
seeds from the metering device to the
rear of a furrow opener and drop them
into the soil.
☐ Furrow Opener – a soil engaging
device used to open a furrow at a
desired depth for placement of the
seeds and partially cover them with
soil.


☐ Covering Device – used to
move the nearby surface soil into
the furrow and then cover the
seeds.
☐ Press Wheel - used to compress
the soil around the seeds in order to
create good contact between the
seeds and the soil aggregates for
improved germination.
☐ Ground Wheel – used to drive
the metering device at a proper
rotational speed in order to attain
the required plant spacing.
☐ Main Frame – used to hold and
support the various components of
the seeder and to provide hitch
attachment to the tractor or power
tiller.

Basic Components of a Seeder
Press wheel
Seed Box
Metering
Device
Seed Tube
Covering
Device

Seed Metering Devices


FACTORS AFFECTING THE PERFORMANCE
OF SEEDER/PLANTER
☐ Seed-Related Factors
• 	Quality of seed
• 	Method of seed treatment

☐ Soil-Related Factors
• 	Soil bulk density
• 	Soil porosity
• 	Soil water
• 	Soil temperature
• 	Specific volume
• 	Soil cohesion
• 	Soil air
• 	Soil strength


☐ Mechanical Factors
• 	Seed damaged during metering;
• 	Uniformity of depth of placement of
seeds;
• 	Uniformity of distribution of seeds
along rows;
• 	Transverse displacement of seeds
from the row;
• 	Prevention of loose soil getting
under the seeds;
• 	Degree of soil compaction above
the seeds;
• 	Uniformity of soil cover over the
seeds; and
• 	Changes of mixing fertilizer with
seeds during placement on the
furrow.


Plant Spacing and Row Spacing of
Various Crops
Crops 	Plant Spacing (cm) 	Row Spacing (cm)
Groundnut 	5-10 	22-60
Soybean 	4-7 	20-60
Maize 	20-25 	45-60
Cotton 	20-40 	50-80
Peas 	5-15 	45-60
Rice 	15-20 	20-30
Sorghum 	10-15 	30-45
Sunflower 	20 	45-80
Wheat 	3-5 	15-22

No-Till Planters – are machines that directly place the seeds
into undisturbed soil.

Rice Transplanters – are machines that place rice seedling
at a proper spacing in a well-prepared paddy soil.


Rice Drum Seeders – are machines that are designed for
planting pre-germinated rice seeds in rows so that manually-
operated mechanical weeders can be used.

Air Seeders – are machines which pneumatically place the
seeds into the soil by means of a deep tillage tool.

References
n ASAE. ASAE Standard 1997.
n Campbell, J.K. 1990. Dibble Sticks, Donkeys, and Diesel:
Machine in Crop Production. International Rice Research
Institute. Los Banos, Laguna, Philippines. 329pp
n RNAM. 1991. Agricultural Machinery Design and Data
Handbook (Seeder and Planter). RNAM/ESCAP. United nations
Building. 	Rajadarmnem Ave., Bangkok 10200 Thailand. 137pp.

QUESTIONS AND PROBLEMS

1. Equipment used to place the
seeds or plant parts into the soil
and keep them from weeds, insect
pests and diseases until fully
grown.
a. Tillage equipment
b. Seeding and planting
equipment
c. All of the above
d. None of the above
2. Method of randomly scattering
seeds on the surface of the field.
a. Broadcasting
b. Drill seeding
c. Seed tape planting
d. None of the above
3. Method of randomly dropping
and covering seeds in furrow.
a. Broadcasting
b. Drill seeding
c. Precision planting
d. None of the above
4. Accurate placing of seeds
singly at equal interval in rows.
a. Broadcasting
b. Drill seeding
c. Precision planting
d. None of the above
5. Placing of group of seeds at
equal interval in rows.
a. 	Hill dropping
b. 	No-till planting
c. 	Seed tape planting
d. 	None of the above
6. Planting method in which
seeds are deposited, either singly
or in group, in a water soluble
tape under controlled condition.
a. Precision planting
b. Seed-tape planting
c. Hill dropping
d. None of the above

7. Method in which seeding is done
directly into previously undisturbed
soil.
a. Much tillage
b. No-till
c. Minimum tillage
d. None of the above
8. Method in which planting is done
directly onto an essentially
unprepared seedbed.
a. Zero tillage
b. No-tillage planting
c. Reduced tillage
d. 	None of the above
9. Equipment used to place seeds in
furrow.
a. Planter
b. Seeder
c. Broadcaster
d. All of the above
10. Equipment used to place plant
parts to a prepared furrow.
a. Planter
b. Seeder
c. Broadcaster
d. All of the above
11. Which of the following is a
classification of seeder according to
method of seeding?
a. Drill
b. Field Distributor
c. Broadcaster
d. All of the above
12. Which of the following is a
classification of seeder according to
source of power?
a. Manually operated
b. Animal drawn
c. Power-tiller operated
d. All of the above

13. Which of the following is the
function of a seeder/planter?
a. To meter seeds/plant parts of
different sizes and shapes.
b. To place the seeds/plant parts
accurately and uniformly at the
desired depth and spacing in the
soil.
c. To cover the seeds/plant parts
optionally and to compact the soil
around it to enhance germination
and emergence.
d. All of the above
14. Machine used to prepare the
soil, meter the seed, and position
them in one operation.
a. Broadcaster
b. Drill
c. Field distributor
d. None of the above
15. Machine consisting of a seed
box with metering device in the
bottom of the hopper used to
prepare the soil for the seed.
a. Broadcaster
b. Drill
c. Field distributor
d. None of the above
16. Machine that is pushed or
pulled by human.
a. 	Manually operated
b. 	Animal drawn
c. 	Power-tiller operated
d. 	None of the above
17. Machine that meters the
materials onto a revolving flange
wheel, less expensive and has the
highest work capacity but is
hardest to calibrate.
a. Broadcaster
b. Drill
c. Field distributor
d. None of the above

18. Which of the following is a reason
why the broadcaster is hard to
calibrate?
a. 	Uneven distribution from the
flange wheel
b. 	Unequal seed weight
c. 	Uneven soil surface
d. 	All of the above
19. Minimum area required for
testing manually-operated seeder.
a. Not less than 100 m2
b. Not less than 500 m2
c 	Not less than 1000 m2
d. 	None of the above
20. Machine with power source from
draft animals harnessed either singly
or with multiple animals.
a. 	Tractor type
b. 	Animal drawn
c. 	Power-tiller operated
d. 	None of the above
21. Seeding or planting machine
drawn by a small walking-type tractor
powered by a separate engine.
a. 	Manually operated
b. 	Animal drawn
c. 	Power-tiller operated
d. 	None of the above
22. Machine that sometimes obtain
power from the engine using belt-
and-pulley drive.
a. 	Tractor type
b. 	Animal drawn
c. 	Power-tiller operated
d. 	None of the above
23. Power source for this machine is
transmitted through the power-take-
off drive of a tractor.
a. 	Manually operated
b. 	Animal drawn
c. 	Tractor type
d. 	None of the above

text:
CULTIVATION AND WEED
CONTROL EQUIPMENT
VOLUME 3 – AGRICULTURAL MACHINERY AND
MECHANIZATION
by
Engr. Alexis T. Belonio, MS
Agricultural and Biosystems Engineer
ASEAN Engineer
2024 AGRICULTURAL AND BIOSYSTEMS ENGINEERING
BOARD EXAM REVIEWER

Disclaimer
Photos, illustrations and schematic diagrams of equipment or machine parts are shown in the
presentation solely for educational purposes to facilitate comprehension of the topics by the students.
Showing them does not endorse a product nor imply criticism of similar products not mentioned.

INTRODUCTION
☐ Cultivation - is an operation that requires some kind of tool that stirs
the surface of the soil to a shallow depth in such a manner that young
weed will not be destroyed and crop growth be promoted.

OPERATIONS
☐ Pre-Planting – This is done prior
to planting after the seed bed has
been prepared.
☐ Post- Planting – This is done in
some crops after planting before the
crops emerges.
☐ Post-Emergence – This is done
usually after emergence of crops
since weeds generally emerge at the
same time with the crop.

OBJECTIVES OF CULTIVATION
☐ To retain moisture by killing the
weeds, by loosening mulches on
surface, and by retaining rainfall;
☐ To develop plant food;
☐ To aerate the soil allowing oxygen
to penetrate the soil; and
☐ To promote activity of
microorganism in the soil.

FACTORS TO CONSIDER IN SELECTING THE
TYPE AND SIZE NEEDED FOR CULTIVATOR
☐ Area of the farm
☐ Kind of crop grown
☐ Soil type and condition
☐ Rainfall
☐ Type of farming
practice
☐ Kind of power available

Field Cultivator


Lister Plow

☐ Field Cultivator – an implement for the seedbed preparation,
weed eradication, or follow cultivation subsequent to some forms of
primary tillage.

☐ Rotary Hoe – an implement for dislodging small weeds and
grasses and for breaking soil crust and is used for fast, shallow
cultivation.

CLASSIFICATION OF TRACTOR-
MOUNTED CULTIVATORS
☐ Central-Forward Tractor-Mounted
Cultivator – Available in one, two, four, six,
and eight-row sizes. It can be mounted on
both four-wheel and three-wheel tractors. The
one-row cultivator is suitable for small farm
and terraced field with curving rows. Two-
rows cultivator, on the other hand, is suitable
for medium-size farms and fields that have
rows either straight or with gradual curves.
☐ Rear-Tractor-Mounted Cultivator -
Usually unit assembly attached to tractors
equipped with a three-point hitch as a single
unit. Each gang is provided with a gauge
wheel to control the depth of cultivation. The
gang is attached to a tool bar or frame bar.

GANGS FOR CULTIVATORS
☐ The gang or rig consists of a
beam to which a shank or
standard that has an adjustable
foot set at an angle is attached
so as shovel or sweep can be
bolted to it. The type of gang
assembly to use depends on
the kind of crops, soils, and
farming practices. The number
and type of soil stirring
members usually determine the
gang style.

SHOVEL AND SWEEPS
☐ There are numerous types and shapes of shovels and sweeps
used for stirring and killing weeds:
• 	Shovels are available in widths up to about 3½in.
• 	Sweeps can be obtained in width ranging from 6 to 24in.


☐ Type of soil
☐ Crops
☐ Weeds
FACTORS TO CONSIDER IN THE
SELECTION OF TYPE OF SHOVEL OR
SWEEP

Cultivator Shovels and Sweeps

SPEED OF CULTIVATORS
☐ Average speed for horse cultivation is 4kph.
☐ For tractor-mounted cultivator is 4 to 4.8kph

BEET-AND-BEAN CULTIVATOR
☐ Beet-and-bean cultivator -
requires shovel and sweeps for
shallow cultivation. Gage wheel
controls the depth of penetration of
the shovel. Sizes of the cultivator
range from two to six rows; four
rows being the most popular in size.
Attachments are available for the
application of fertilizer as a side
dressing.


Lister Cultivator
☐ Lister - is particularly
adapted for the cultivation of a
listed crop in its early stage of
development. Listed crops are
those planted in the furrow or
trench or below the general
level of the ground. For the first
cultivation, the cultivators are
set to throw the soil away (off-
barring) from the row of the
plants. For all later cultivation,
the plow bottom are set to throw
the soil toward (hilling-up) the
plants.

Rod 	Weeders, Field Cultivators,
Subsoil, and Chisel Cultivators
☐ These cultivators are generally used to control weed growth on
fallow (uncultivated) lands.

Rotary-Hoe Cultivator
☐ Rotary-hoe cultivator - is a cultivating implement used to cultivate
and destroy weeds and grasses around young plants.
☐ When rain causes a hard rust to form over the soil and hinders the
emergence of young seedlings, the rotary hoe is an excellent tool for
pulverizing the crust.

Problems on Weeds
☐ Reduction in profit resulting from reduced crop yield.
☐ Reduction in the quality of the crops.
☐ Harbors insects that causes damage to the crops.
☐ Devaluation of the land.

Methods of Controlling Weeds
☐ Cultivation by stirring the soil
☐ Use of flame
☐ Use of chemical
☐ Laying of plastic strips over the row

Rice Conical and Rotary Weeders

Cultivator with Fertilizer Applicator

References
☐ Lovegrove, H.T. 1976. Crop Production Equipment. A
practical guide for farmers, operators, and trainees.
Hutchinson & Co. Ltd. 3 Fitzroy Square, London Wi. 406pp.
☐ Hunt, D. and D. Wilson. 2016. Farm Power and Machinery
Management. 11th Edition. Waveland Press, Inc. Long Groove,
Illinois. 360pp.
☐ Smith, H. P. 1977. Farm Machinery and Equipment. Sixth
Edition. Tata McGraw-Hill Publishing Company Ltd. New Delhi.
488pp.
☐ Stone, A. A. and H. E. Gulvin. 1967. Machines for Power
Farming. Second Edition. John Wiley and Sons. New York.
559pp.

QUESTIONS AND PROBLEMS

1. Operation that requires a kind of
tool to stir the soil surface in shallow
depth to destroy young weeds and to
promote crop growth.
a. 	Weeding
b. 	Cultivation
c. 	Cutting
d. 	None of the above
2. Cultivation operation includes ____.
a. 	pre-planting
b. 	post-planting
c. 	post emergence
d. 	All of the above
3. Which of the following is not an
objective of cultivation?
a. 	Retain moisture by killing the
weeds, by loosening surface of
mulches, and by retaining rainfall.
b. 	Aerate the soil to allow oxygen to
penetrate the soil.
c. Promote microbial activity in the
soil.
d. None of the above
4. Operation performed prior to
planting after the seed bed has
been prepared.
a. 	Pre-planting
b. 	Post-planting
c. 	Post emergence
d. 	None of the above
5. Operation done usually after
emergence of crops since weeds
generally emerge at the same time
with the crop.
a. 	Pre-planting
b. 	Post-planting
c. 	Post emergence
d. 	All of the above

6. Operation performed in some
crops after planting but before the
crop emerges.
a. 	Pre-planting
b. 	Post-planting
c. 	Post emergence
d. 	All of the above
7. Farm implement used for
secondary tillage in which the name
refers to shanks that pierce the soil
as they are linearly dragged through.
a. 	Cultivator
b. 	Seeder
c. 	Weeder
d. 	None of the above
8. Mechanically-operated machine
that removes weeds and grasses
from the crops.
a. Seeder
b. 	Weeder
c. Cultivator
d. None of the above
9. Ratio between the number of
weeds removed by the weeder to the
number of weeds present per unit
area.
a. Weeding index
b. Weeding rate
c. Weeding capacity
d. None of the above
10. Machine used to kill weed seeds
by microwave heating during weeding.
a. Zapper
b. Microwave oven
c. Flame thrower
d. All of the above
11. Device used between the cultivator
sweep and the plant row to prevent
the soil from covering the young
plants.
a. Shield
b. Fender
c. Spread bar
d. None of the above

12. Machine that has one or more
elements rotating about a vertical axis
and cuts the grass by impact.
a. Rotary mower
b. Grass cutter
c. Power scythe
d. All of the above
13. Power-take-off rpm of a lawn
mower and garden ride-on tractors.
a. 1000 rpm
b. 540 rpm
c. 2000 rpm
d. None of the above
14. Which of the following is a
classification of a tractor-mounted
cultivator?
a. 	Central-forward tractor-mounted
b. 	Rear tractor-mounted
c. 	All of the above
d. 	None of the above
15. Type of unit assemblies of
tractor-mounted cultivator attached
to tractors equipped with a three
point hitch as a single unit.
a. 	Central-forward
b. 	Rear
c. 	Any of the two
d. 	None of the above
16. Type of tractor-mounted
cultivator that can be mounted on
both four- and three-wheeled
tractors.
a. 	Central-forward
b. 	Rear
c. 	Any of the two
d. 	None of the above
17. One-row cultivator is suitable
for ____.
a. 	small farms
b. 	terraced fields with curving rows
c. 	All of the above
d. 	None of the above

18. Two-row cultivator is suitable for
____.
a. 	medium-size farms
b. 	fields that have rows either
straight or with gradual curves
c. 	All of the above
d. 	None of the above
19. Gangs are attached to a tool
bar or to a frame bar and each
gang is provided with a gauge
wheel to ____.
a. 	control the depth of cultivation
b. 	have deep penetration
c. 	All of the above
d. 	None of the above
20. Which of the following is a
factor to consider in selecting the
type and the size of the cultivator to
use?
a. 	Area of the farm and kind of crop
grown
b. 	Soil type and condition
c. 	Rainfall and type of farming
practice
d. All of the above
21. Type of gang assemblies
depends on the ____.
a. 	kind of crop and type of soil
b. 	farming practice
c. 	All of the above
d. 	None of the above
22. An implement used for seedbed
preparation, weed eradication, or
fallow cultivation subsequent to
some form of primary tillage,
equipped with steel spring shanks.
a. 	Beet and bean cultivator
b. 	Lister cultivator
c. 	Field cultivator
d. 	None of the above
23. Shovels and sweeps are
available in ____ width.
a. 	2½ in. and 5 to 20 in.
b. 	3½ in. and 6 to 24 in.
c. 	4½ in. and 7 to 28 in.
d. 	None of the above
