SPRAYING AND DUSTING
EQUIPMENT
VOLUME 3 – AGRICULTURAL MACHINERY AND
MECHANIZATION
by
Engr. Alexis T. Belonio, MS
Agricultural and Biosystems Engineer
ASEAN Engineer
2024 AGRICULTURAL AND BIOSYSTEMS ENGINEERING
BOARD EXAM REVIEWER

Disclaimer
Photos, illustrations and schematic diagrams of equipment or machine parts are shown in the
presentation solely for educational purposes to facilitate comprehension of the topics by the students.
Showing them does not endorse a product nor imply criticism of similar products not mentioned.

PRIMARY FUNCTIONS OF SPRAYER
☐ Breaks liquid droplets of effective size.
☐ Distributes the droplets uniformly over the surface or space to
be protected.
☐ Regulates the amount of chemical solution in order to avoid
excessive application that may be harmful or wasteful to the
plants.


TERMINOLOGIES
☐ Application Rate – amount of any
material applied per unit treated.
☐ Active Ingredient Rate – amount of
active ingredient applied per unit treated,
expressed in terms of mass per relevant
unit treated. Examples: kg a.i./ha; mg
a.i./m3; mg a.i./plant or animal.
☐ Formulation Rate – amount of
chemical formulation applied per unit
treated. Examples: kg/ha; mg/m3;
mg/plant or animals.
☐ Spray Rate – amount of spray liquid
applied per unit treated. Examples:
liter/ha; ml/m3; ml/ plant or animals.


☐ Deposit Rate – amount of
any material deposited per unit
area.
☐ Drift – movement of
chemicals outside the intended
target area by air mass
transport diffusion.
☐ Formulation – form of a
chemical that is supplied to the
user, including both the active
and the inert ingredients.

CLASSIFICATIONS OF SPRAYER
☐ Hand Sprayer –manually
operated by driving a pump,
usually by hand.
• 	Compressed-air sprayer
• 	Knapsack sprayer
☐ Power Sprayer –
mechanically driven by an
engine or a motor. In large
scale sprayer with boom, tractor
PTO is used as power source.
• 	Hydraulic or field sprayer
• 	Hydro-pneumatic sprayer
• 	Blower sprayer

COMPRESSED-AIR SPRAYER
☐ Simple in design and operation and is not too expensive to buy and
maintain.
☐ Particularly useful for spot and small-area application.
☐ Tank capacity is usually 7.5 to 15 liters and nozzle operating
pressure is up to 3.5 kg/cm2.

KNAPSACK SPRAYER
☐ Carried at the back by means of shoulder straps.
☐ Simple in design and operation and relatively cheap to buy
and maintain.
☐ Capacity is up to 22.5 liters and capable to operate at a
pressure of 4.2 to 5.4 kg/cm2.
☐ Useful for boom spraying when series of four nozzles or more
are operating at the same time.


Hand-Operated Sprayer

Compressed-Air Sprayer

PARTS OF HAND-OPERATED SPRAYER
Hand Lever
Tank
Pump
Cutoff Valve Spray Hose
Spray Nozzle
Extension
Spray Tube
Shoulder Strap

CALIBRATING HAND-OPERATED
SPRAYER
☐ Prepare the sprayer
☐ Determine the walking speed
☐ Determine the width of spray or swath
☐ Calculate the area sprayed
☐ Calculate the application rate
☐ Calculate the liquid herbicides or insecticides to mix in each
spryer per load.

POWER SPRAYER
☐ Power sprayer – a spraying apparatus that transports or
operates with a power source such as tractor, small engine, or
electric motor.
☐ Usually uses plunger or piston pumps.
☐ Usually operates at a pressure of under 40 kg/cm2.

BASIC PARTS OF POWER SPRAYER

PARTS DEFINITION
☐ Agitator – A rotating device located
inside the hopper of gravity flow
applicators and broadcasts spreader
that enhances the delivery of granules
to the adjustable orifice.
☐ Drop Tube – A conduit either plastic,
metal, or rubber that directs granule
flow of a granular applicator from the
metering device to the target.
☐ Rotor – A metering device used in
positive displacement of granular
applicator that regulates flow rate by
displacing a fixed rate per revolution.


TYPES OF SPRAYER NOZZLE
☐ Cone-Type Nozzle – consists of
tip and core or swirl plate. Usually
operates between 40-60 psi. It is
lever operated.
☐ Fan-Type Nozzle – the shape of
the hole is responsible for the
shape of the spray and the angled
form.
☐ Impact-Type Nozzle –
Pressurized liquid passes through
the nozzle orifice which is relatively
large and strikes the angled face.

Spray Pattern

SPRAY CLASSIFICATION
☐ Aerosol – Distribution of droplets is £50 um.
☐ Mist – Distribution of droplets is >50 um and £100 um.
☐ Fine Spray – Distribution of droplets is >100 um and £400
um.
☐ Medium Spray – Distribution of droplets is >400 um and
£1200 um.
☐ Course Spray – Distribution of droplets is >1200 um.

HOSE-END SPRAYERS

METHODS OF APPLICATION OF CHEMICAL
☐ Banded Application – Distribution of chemical in parallel bands
leaving the area between the bands free of chemicals.
☐ Basal Application – Application of chemical into the base of the
plant.
☐ Broadcast Application – Application of chemical over an entire
area of a field.
☐ Directed Application – Application of chemical to a specific
area, such as row bed or base of the plant.
☐ Foliar Application – Application of chemical to the stems, fruits,
leaves, or needles of the plant.
☐ Spot Treatment – Application of chemical to a small restricted
area, usually to control the spread of pest.

☐ Aerosol generator or fogger - a mechanical or thermal device
that produces a liquid dispersion having a volume median
diameter of <50 um. A fog machine sprays liquid-type
chemicals as an aerosol. It is classified into cold-fog machine
by generating process of fog.
AEROSOL GENERATOR OR FOGGER

Duster
Compressed-air from the fan is guided to the bottom of the tank
to agitate the powder of granules. Due to pressure difference at
the throat in the discharge pipe, the air with a powder or granules
is conveyed to the discharge pipe.

Electro-Static Sprayer

Aerial Spraying

Drone Arial Spraying

REFERENCES
☐ ASAE. ASAE Standards 1997. Standard Engineering
Practices and Data.The Society for engineering in agricultural,
food, and biological systems. 2950 Niles Road, St. Joseph, MI
USA. 978pp.
☐ Hunt, D. and D. Wilson. 2016. Farm Power and Machinery
Management. 11th Edition. Waveland Press, Inc. Long Groove,
Illinois. 360pp.
☐ Hunt, D. 1983. Farm power and Machinery. 8th edition. The
Iowa State University Press. Ames, Iowa. 352pp.

QUESTIONS AND PROBLEMS

1. 	Process of applying
chemicals to agricultural crops.
a. 	Fertilizing
b. 	Spraying
c. 	Dusting
d. 	None of the above
2. Equipment that breaks the
liquid droplets to an effective
size and distributes them
uniformly over the surface or
space to be protected, and
regulates the amount of
chemical solution to avoid
excessive application that
might prove harmful or
wasteful.
a. Duster
b. Sprayer
c. All of the above
d. None of the above
3. When calibrating a sprayer,
an Agricultural Engineer ____.
a. measures the diameter of
its tank
b. cleans the nozzles
c. measures and adjusts its
application rate
d. None of the above
4. Amount of any material
applied per unit treated.
a. 	Application rate
b. 	Active ingredient rate
c. 	Formulation rate
d. 	None of the above
5. Amount of chemical
formulation applied per unit
treated.
a. 	Application rate
b. 	Active ingredient rate
c. 	Formulation rate
d. 	None of the above

6. Primary factor that affects the
performance of the sprayer.
a. Spray-particle size
b. Spraying time
c. Spray materials
d. None of the above
7. Amount of spray liquid per unit
treated.
a. 	Deposit rate
b. 	Active ingredient rate
c. 	Spray rate
d. 	None of the above
8. Unit for spray rate is ____.
a. 	mg a.i./plant or animal
b. 	mg/plant or animal
c. 	ml/plant or animal

HARVESTING EQUIPMENT
VOLUME 3 – AGRICULTURAL MACHINERY AND
MECHANIZATION
by
Engr. Alexis T. Belonio, MS
Agricultural and Biosystems Engineer
ASEAN Engineer
2024 AGRICULTURAL AND BIOSYSTEMS ENGINEERING
BOARD EXAM REVIEWER

Disclaimer
Photos, illustrations and schematic diagrams of equipment or machine parts are shown in the
presentation solely for educational purposes to facilitate comprehension of the topics by the students.
Showing them does not endorse a product nor imply criticism of similar products not mentioned.

INTRODUCTION
☐ Harvesting is the process of gathering matured crops from the
field that is ready for primary processing or consumption.


Kinds of Mechanical Harvester
☐ Grain Harvester
☐ Corn Harvester
☐ Sugar Cane Harvester
☐ Cotton Harvester
☐ Forage Harvester
☐ Root Harvester
☐ Hay Harvester

CLASSIFICATIONS OF GRAIN
HARVESTING EQUIPMENT
☐ Manual Harvesting – using hand tools such as scythe, sickle, and
others. Manpower requirement ranged from 60-80 persons-hr/ha.
Sickle Harvesting 	“Yatab” Panicle Harvesting

Different Kinds of Sickle 	Power Harvester

☐ 	Mechanical Harvesting – using
power equipment and machinery.
(a)Reaper – only cuts the panicle
during harvesting
(b)Reaper binder – cuts the panicle
and bind them together for ease
of hauling into a threshing place.
(c)Stripper – does not cut the
panicle. Instead it separates the
grains by the combing action of
the stripper teeth of the
machine.
(d)Combine – harvests and
threshes the grains in one
operation.

REAPER
☐ Reaper - a machine that cuts the panicles and places them on a
windrow.
☐ It is either power-tiller operated or tractor-operated machine.


LOSSES RELATED TO REAPING
☐ Laying or Windrow Loss – good
grains that are shattered when cut
crops are laid from horizontal
conveyor to the ground.
☐ Header Loss – good grains
shattered during the cutting and
transporting by horizontal flat belts
towards the discharge end.
☐ Crop Damaged Loss –
unrecoverable good grains that are
available from standing crop that has
been knocked down or damaged by
the machine during the cutting
operation.


Reaping and Binding Operations

WAYS TO REDUCE REAPER’S
HARVESTING LOSSES
☐ Avoid sharp turn when cutting.
☐ Reduce cutting speed when
cutting shattering variety.
☐ Clear the rice panicle off the
upper lugs and start wheels
whenever possible.

STRIPPER HARVESTER
☐ Stripper harvester - a grain-harvesting machine that does not
cut the panicle during harvesting operation. Instead, it strips off
the grains from the panicle by combing action of the rotating rotor.
☐ Grains with mixture of cutoff straws and panicles are placed in a
box behind the rotor and unloaded for final threshing once totally
filled.

ADVANTAGES OF STRIPPER
HARVESTING
☐ Simplicity
☐ Ease of construction
☐ Robustness of rotor which
can perform several functions,
such as
• 	Crop lifting
• 	Harvesting
• 	Partial threshing
• 	Crop transport

Harvesting Operation
Transporting

COMBINE HARVESTER
☐ Combine harvester - a grain-
harvesting machine that heads the
standing grains, threshes them and
cleans them as they move over the
field. It eliminates from the harvest
the activity of grain binder, the
header, and the stationary thresher
as well as the activity of stacking
and hauling the grains. The
combine is well adapted for
harvesting small grains, soybeans,
grain sorghum, rice and many
others.


TYPES OF COMBINE HARVESTER
☐ Pull-Type Combine – This
machine is drawn by a tractor.
Power is transmitted through the
power take-off shaft for smaller
unit and with an auxiliary engine
for larger unit.
☐ Self-Propelled Combine – This
machine is powered by a 60 to
150hp industrial engine and is
operated by one person.

BASIC FUNCTIONS OF COMBINE
☐ Cuts the standing grain
☐ Feeds the cut grains to the cylinder
☐ Threshes the grains from the stalk or stem
☐ Separates the grains from the straw
☐ Cleans the grains by removing the chaff and other foreign matters
☐ Handles the grains from the combine to the truck

Mechanism
Cleaning

Mechanism

LOSSES RELATED TO COMBINING OF
GRAINS
☐ Shatter Loss – grains lying on the
ground or out of reach of the cutter bar.
☐ Cutter-Bar Loss – grains lost due to
rough handling by the cutter bar.
☐ Cylinder Loss – grains lost over the
straw rack in the form of unthreshed
heads.
☐ Separating Loss – grains lost out of the
rear of the combine in the form of
threshed grain.
☐ Cleaning Loss – loss in the value of the
crop due to the presence of foreign
matters in the grain tank.

CORN HARVESTER
☐ Corn harvester - is called
as corn picker either a single-
or double-row machine
equipped with snapping rolls
to remove the ears from the
standing stalks.

TYPE OF CORN PICKER ACCORDING
TO POWER UNIT
☐ Pull-Type – It is driven by a tractor as a separate unit; also
power is transmitted through power take-off drive.
☐ Self-Propelled – It is driven by an industrial engine as an integral
part of the machine.

TYPES OF CORN PICKER
☐ Snapper – snaps the ears from
the stalk and does not remove the
husks.
☐ Picker-Husker – is equipped
with a husker attachment in
addition to the snapper and also
removes the husks.
☐ Picker-Sheller – snaps the
corn and shells it in the field.

FACTORS AFFECTING THE
PERFORMANCE OF CORN PICKER
☐ Plant Characteristics
Variety or hybrid suitable for machine harvesting: stiff stalks that
stand up and do not break over and lodge; condition of stalks; height
of ears and stalks; toughness of the ear shanks; size of ears – large
reduces shelling losses; condition of shelling - hard shelling
characteristic reduces shelling losses; snapping and husking
condition - thick and tight husk on ear desirable for snapping but not
husking.
☐ Mechanical Factor
Type of snapping roll surface, adjustment of snapping rollers -
distance apart, timing of snapping rollers, rate of travel, type of
wagon hitch, adjustment of dividers to pick-up stalks which are down.
☐ Miscellaneous Factor
Timeliness of harvesting - field loss is less if harvesting is done early;
carefulness of operator, weather condition, cleanliness of the field,
i.e., freedom from tall weeds and grasses; length of rows; and row
spacing suitable for machine.

LOSSES RELATED TO CORN HARVESTING
☐ Loose-Ear Loss – ears separated from the stalk and lying on the
ground out of reach of the gathering mechanism.
☐ Picker-Ear Loss – ears left on the ground that were attached to the
stalks but escaped the snapping rolls while being picked up by the
gathering points.
☐ Shelled-Corn Loss – shelled corn lying on the ground as a result
of shelling occurring at the snapping roll.
☐ Shelling Loss – corn kernels that were not shelled out of the cobs
lost over the rack.
☐ Separating Loss – single corn kernel that were not separated from
husk, silks, etc. lost over the rack.

COTTON HARVESTER
☐ Cotton harvester - is called as
cotton stripper which harvests cotton by
combing action of a rolling pickets.
Types:
1. Double Roller – harvester with
alternate rows of nylon brush
bristles and flexible rubberized
strips. It may either be centrally
mounted on the tractor or be
self-propelled.
2. Multiple-Finger or Comb
Type – is either centrally-
mounted on the tractor or pulled
behind the tractor.

FACTORS AFFECTING THE
PERFORMANCE OF COTTON
STRIPPER
☐ Plant characteristics
☐ Thickness of plant in row
☐ Cultural practices
☐ Pick-up fingers or limb
lifters
☐ Design of stripping unit
☐ Conveying system
☐ Speed of travel

FORAGE HARVESTER
☐ Forage harvester - a machine
used for gathering silage crops such
as grasses or straws for feeds.
☐ It performs harvesting and
chopping green row crops consisting
of plant-cutting units and chopping
units.

ADVANTAGES OF FIELD-FORAGE
HARVESTER
☐ Eliminates the drudgery of lifting and loading heavy green bundles
of corn per hectare.
☐ Provides ensilage at lower cost.
☐ Provides more tons for a fee per silo.
☐ Permits filling the silo when the crop is at the right stage.
☐ Makes ensilage with greater feeding value.
☐ Provides more uniformity of feeding value from any part of the silo.
☐ Provides more uniform, slid pack without air pockets, thus
preventing molds.
☐ Causes no wilting of leaves or loss of previous moisture.
☐ Leaves no mud or any contaminating soil bacteria on butts.
☐ Avoids soggy material which often occurs when the silo is filled too
early with green, immature corn.

ROOT HARVESTER
☐ Root harvester - a machine used to dig and separate the roots
of the crop from the soil.
☐ Common applications of root harvester are for potatoes, peanuts,
sweet potato, onion, garlic. and many others.

REFERENCES
☐ ASAE. ASAE Standards 1997. Standard Engineering
Practices Data. American Society of Agricultural Engineers.
The Society for Engineering in Agricultural, Food, and Biological
Systems. 2950 Niles Road, St. Joseph, MI 49085-9659 USA.
Pp. 264-275.
☐ Hunt, D. and D. Wilson. 2016. Farm Power and Machinery
Management. 11th Edition. Waveland Press, Inc. Long Groove,
Illinois. 360pp.
☐ Hunt, D. 1982. Farm Power and Machinery Management.
Eight Edition. Iowa State University Press. Ames, Iowa. 325pp.
☐ Smith, H. P. and L. H. Wilkes. 1977. Farm Machinery and
Equipment. Sixth Edition. Tata McGraw Hill Publishing
Company Ltd. New Delhi, India. 487pp.

7. Mechanical harvesting
equipment that only cuts the
panicle during harvesting and

a. 	Reaper
b. 	Stripper
c. 	Combine
d. 	None of the above
8. Harvesting equipment that cuts
the panicle and binds them
together for ease of hauling to the
threshing place.
a. Combine
b. 	Stripper
c. 	Reaper/binder
d. 	None of the above
9. Ratio of the knife velocity to the
forward velocity of a rice reaper.
a. 1.35:1
b. 1.55:2
c. 1.55:0

10. Good grains shattered during
the cutting and transporting by
horizontal flat belts towards the

____.
a. 	laying or windrow loss

that has been knocked down or

a. 	laying or windrow loss

13. Good grains that are shattered

horizontal conveyor to the ground.

harvesting losses include:

15. Mechanical harvesting

16. Machine used for combing the
grain from the plant while the plant

17. Stripper harvesting is more

____.

18. Which of the following functions
can be done by stripper harvesting?

b. 	Stripper

20. Harvesting equipment that
eliminates the use of grain binder,
header, stationary thresher as well

THRESHING AND SHELLING
EQUIPMENT
VOLUME 3 – AGRICULTURAL MACHINERY AND
MECHANIZATION
by
Engr. Alexis T. Belonio, MS
Agricultural and Biosystems Engineer
ASEAN Engineer
2024 AGRICULTURAL AND BIOSYSTEMS ENGINEERING
BOARD EXAM REVIEWER

Disclaimer
Photos, illustrations and schematic diagrams of equipment or machine parts are shown in the
presentation solely for educational purposes to facilitate comprehension of the topics by the students.
Showing them does not endorse a product nor imply criticism of similar products not mentioned.

INTRODUCTION
☐ Threshing is the process of
detaching the grains from the
panicle by means of impact or by
rubbing action, usually applied to
rice, wheat, and other cereal
grains.
☐ Shelling is the removal of
seeds from the cobs, pods, or
husks after separation from the
plant, usually applied to corn,
peanuts, and similar crops.

METHODS
☐ Manual Threshing
By the use of a threshing frame, a flail, or by foot
trampling either human or animals.
Flail Threshing

“Foot“ Trampling

☐ Mechanical Threshing
• By subjecting the grains into rotating parts of the thresher
• Capacity ranges from 500 to 2000 kg/hr


Mechanical Threshing of Grains
Grains
Straw
Concave
Threshing
Cylinder

CLASSIFICATIONS OF MECHANICAL
THRESHER
☐ According to Operation
1. Through Flow – a
machine whereby harvested
product is threshed while the
cut plants are wholly fed into
the machine into an opening
perpendicular to the cylinder
and directed to an outlet
which is also perpendicular to
it. Usually, the diameter to
length ratio of the threshing
cylinder is 1.

Classifications of Through-Flow
1. Single Cylinder – type of thresher consisting of only one
threshing cylinder.
2. Double Cylinder – type of thresher consisting of two cylinders
arranged in series or one after the other.

Multi-Cylinder Through-Flow Peanut Threshing

2. Axial Flow – a mechanical
thresher whereby the stalks with
the grains are fed into one of the
feed trays of the thresher located in
one side. The materials then
moved axially in the threshing
cylinder until the grains are
separated and the straws are
thrown out at the other end of the
straw outlet.

Through-Flow 	Axial-Flow
In
Out
In
Out

☐ According to the Method of Feeding
1. Throw-In Type – A mechanical thresher whereby the whole
cut plants are fed into the machine and major portion of the
grains are threshed by the initial impact of the bars or spikes
on the cylinder and further threshing is accomplished as the
moving panicles hit the spikes or the bars of the concave.

Rice Threshing Operation

2. Hold-On Thresher –
A mechanical thresher
wherein the stalks are
held mechanically by
the operator during the
operation until all the
grains are detached
from the panicle.

☐ According to the threshing Units
1. Rasp bar – is a kind of threshing cylinder wherein equidistant
bar-like protrusions in parallel orientation are laid on the
periphery of the cylinder


2. Wire Loop – is a kind of threshing cylinder wherein wire loops of
the same arch and of equal sizes are attached around the periphery
of the cylinder in tandem arrangement.

☐ Peg-Tooth - 	is a kind of threshing cylinder wherein spikes or
pegs of equal length are attached around the periphery of the
cylinder in tandem fashion.

CLASSIFICATIONS OF AXIAL-FLOW
THRESHER
☐ Portable Axial-Flow Thresher without Oscillating Screen
• 	Simple and light weight for ease of movement of machine in the
field.
• 	Has modular design where major components can be separated
for stress-free transport and assembling when to be used.
• 	Size is usually small with power unit of <16hp and below.

☐ Portable Thresher with Oscillating Screen
• 	Equipped with oscillating screen and centrifugal cross-flow
blower for winnowing.
• 	Does not require winnowing after the grains are discharged
from the thresher.
• 	Power requirement is larger than that of portable threshers.

☐ Mobile Axial-Flow Thresher
• 	Similar with but larger in size than the portable thresher with
oscillating screen.
• 	Usually equipped with engine as power unit and a support
wheel for ease of transport.
• 	It can be easily moved in the field with the use of a power tiller
or animals during operation.

☐ Self-Propelled Axial-Flow Thresher
• A large-size thresher complete with oscillating screen; that is, with
power unit for threshing operation as well as for transport.
• The thresher has the ability to move in the paddy field without
needing for a separate power unit.
• The capacity is much higher than that of the pull-type mobile
thresher.

COMPONENTS OF MECHANICAL
RICE THRESHER

☐ Threshing Cylinder – the part of the thresher that rotates about
the axis equipped with either pegs, rasp bar, or wire loop on its
periphery. It is the main part of the thresher that separates the
grains from the panicle.
☐ Concave – the part of the thresher which encloses the threshing
cylinder and allows the separation of the grains from the panicle.
1. Lower concave – a semi-circular shape wire mesh or bars
covering the lower portion in which the cylinder rubs and separates
the grains from the panicle and through which the grains fall.
2. Upper Concave – a semi-circular-shape top cover of the threshing
cylinder consisting of a metal sheet with louvers and/or grills, which
assist in threshing and in axial movement of the straw.

FACTORS AFFECTING THRESHING
CAPACITY
☐ Moisture content of the grain - 	feed
material with high content reduces the
capacity of the thresher.
☐ Straw-to-grain ratio – higher straw-to-
grain ratio also reduces the capacity of
the thresher.
☐ Length-of-straw cut - 	the longer the
straw, the lesser the capacity of the
thresher.
☐ Variety – Japonica rice variety, which
is bold in shape, is difficult to thresh;
hence, reduces the capacity of the
thresher.
☐ Operational skill – a knowledgeable
person to operate the thresher can
maximize its output capacity.

FACTORS 	AFFECTING 	THE POWER
REQUIREMENT OF A THRESHER
☐ Feeding Rate – The more
panicle is fed into the thresher,
the higher is the power
requirement.
☐ Moisture content of crops –
The higher the moisture content
of feed material, the more power
is required.
☐ Length of straws or stalks –
The longer the straw of the
material being feed into the
thresher, the more power is
required.

grains from the panicle by
means of impact or by rubbing
action.

2. 	Methods of threshing could
be ____.

3. 	Method of threshing that
uses a threshing frame, a flail or

INTRODUCTION
☐ Rice combine harvester – is a 4-in-one machine for rice crop that
combines reaping, threshing, cleaning, and bagging in one
operation. This was developed to help farmers become
competitive and enhance the productivity of the country.
☐ In 1835, Hiram Moore built and patented the first combine
harvester in the US for reaping, threshing, and winnowing cereal
grains.
☐ The header of the harvester cuts the standing stalks and sends it
to the threshing drum of the threshing mechanism to beat the cut
crops to separate the grains from the panicles. The grains fall
through sieves and are collected below through a collection bag.
Chaffs and straws pass through conveyors called straw walkers
towards the back of the harvester for disposal.

A rice combine harvester in operation.

harvester wherein the engine is integral

one operator.

☐ Rear-Mounted or Trailing-Type Rice Combine – is drawn by

☐ Front-Mounted Rice Combine – is attached to the tractor

Header, Reel, and Cutting Mechanisms


☐ Threshing Cylinder – is the the part of the combine that separates
the grains from the panicle through impact or rubbing action of the
threshing unit.
☐ Stripper Beater – is an element placed at the rear side of the
cylinder and above to rearward of the concave to assist the
deflection of straw on the straw walker.
Threshing Cylinders and Concave

☐ Concave – is the stationary element of the threshing unit of the
combine to separate the grains from the panicle during operation.
☐ Straw Walker – is an assembly of two or more racks which
agitates the straw and separates the remaining grains from the
straw.
☐ Blower – is a rotary device which produces a flow of air across
the chaffer and cleaning sieve to blow away the materials or
impurities lighter than grains.
☐ Oscillating Screen – is the cleaning mechanism of the combine
that oscillates at 300 to 400 times per minute on a plane that is
parallel to the screen.

Straw Walker and Oscillating Screen Cleaner

Rubber Crawler Wheel

☐ Shaker Shoe – is an oscillating structure that supports the
cleaning sieve and the support chaffer and the chaffer extension.
☐ Grain Elevator – component of the combine that carries the
grains from the grain auger to the grain tank or bin before feeding
them into bags.
☐ Grain Pan – is used for collecting the clean grains after passing
the cleaning sieve prior to conveying by the auger.
☐ Grain Tank – is used to hold the threshed grains.

☐ Theoretical Field Capacity – The computed rate of harvesting

INTERNAL COMBUSTION ENGINE
☐ Internal combustion engine (ICE) is a device that produces
power by burning normally liquid fuel inside the combustion
chamber of an engine.
☐ In agriculture and fishery mechanization, small single-cylinder
engines are commonly used by farmers, ranging from 3hp to 16hp
gasoline and up to slightly higher hp diesel engines.
☐ Multiple-cylinder diesel engines are commonly adopted for large
applications like tractors, self-propelled combine harvester, and
many others.
☐ Knowledge on ICE would be helpful for ABE especially when
dealing agricultural and fishery mechanization. It serves as
backbone in ensuring proper and efficient operation of the different
agri-fishery machines.

BASIC PRINCIPLE
☐ Internal combustion engine (ICE) - is an engine that burns fuel
and air inside a combustion chamber. It can either be piston or
reciprocating engine, rotary engine, gas turbine, jet engine, or rocket
engine.
• 	It is a machine used to power tractors, combine harvesters,
and other self-propelled field equipment.
• 	In farmstead equipment, it is used to drive generator set to
provide electricity for lighting, driving motors, and providing
power for heating and cooling in various processes.

☐ Bore – refers to the size of the opening of the cylinder which is
almost equal to the diameter of the piston plus the rings.
☐ Stroke – refers to the distance traveled by the piston from the
TDC to the BDC.
☐ Top Dead Center (TDC) – is the uppermost position of the piston
during the compression and exhaust stroke.
☐ Bottom Dead Center (BDC) – is the lowest most position of the
piston during the intake and power stroke.
☐ Engine/Piston Displacement (PD) – is the volume displaced by
the piston in one stroke.
☐ Clearance Volume (CV) – is the volume in the combustion
cylinder when the piston is at the TDC position.
☐ Compression Ratio (CR) – is the ratio of the total volume to the
clearance volume.

Some Engine Parts


☐ Mean Effective Pressure (MEP) – is the amount of pressure
generated during the power stroke of engine.
☐ Revolution – is equivalent to one complete rotation of the
crankshaft.
☐ Cycle – refers to the series of events occurring one after the other
in a definite order and repeating the event after the last one has
occurred.
☐ Indicated Horsepower – is the power generated at the
combustion chamber.
☐ Brake Horsepower – is the power available at the drive shaft or at
the crankshaft of an engine.
☐ Friction Horsepower – is the power loss due to friction of piston
and other components of the engine.
☐ Rated Horsepower – is the power of the engine as specified by
the manufacturer.

Usually, it runs at around 900 rpm.

AGRICULTURAL TRACTOR
☐ Agricultural tractors have been used to supply power in Philippine
agriculture specifically for field operation like tillage cultivation and
many others.
☐ In early 80s large tractors have been used for rice cultivation.
Because of their weight that cause the development of hard pan,
however, these large tractors became unattractive to rice farmers.
Instead, they sort to till their land using small hand tractors or power
tillers.
☐ The use of large tractors remains for large farm on dry land where
operation becomes more efficient without the problem of bug down.
☐ With the advent of rice combine harvester, power tillers are
rendered unable to till the land; thus, small 4-wheel farm
tractors become attractive and are presently utilized in rice farms.

BASIC PRINCIPLE
☐ Tractor is an engineering vehicle specifically designed to deliver a
high tractive effort (or torque) at slow speeds for the purpose of
hauling a trailer or a machinery used in agriculture.
☐ A machine used primarily for traction or for pulling an implement.
☐ A versatile machine and a mobile power source for wide variety of
agricultural tasks.
☐ A machine that can perform both stationary and mobile jobs.
☐ A machine that can pull or tow implement through traction from the
drive wheel and/or pull implement through the draft developed from
its drawbar hitch, or power implement through its PTO drive.

FUNCTIONS OF TRACTORS
☐ Pulling machine behind it;
☐ Pushing machine in front of it;
☐ Operating machine mounted on it;
☐ Transmitting power to other machines through the PTO drive;
☐ Raising, lowering, and controlling machines and attachment by
its hydraulic power;
☐ Driving machines through belt power;
☐ Transmitting power through flexible shaft; and
☐ Furnishing power for fast highway transportation and handling.

TRACTOR TRANSMISSION
☐ A speed-reducing mechanism of a tractor that is equipped with
several sequence of gears and shafts through which the engine
power is transmitted to the tractor wheel.
☐ It consists of various devices that cause the forward and backward
movements of the tractor to suit to the different field conditions.
Power Train – is the complete patch of power from the engine to the
wheel of the tractor. Its functions are:
1. 	Transmission from the engine to the rear wheel of the tractor;
2. 	Speed reduction at the rear wheel of the tractor;
3. 	Alteration in the ratio of wheel speed and engine speed in order to
suit to the field condition; and
4. 	Power transmission through right angle drive because the
crankshaft and rear axle are normally at right angle to each other.


☐ Clutch – Connects and disconnects the engine to and from the
transmission gears of the tractor.
☐ Transmission Gears – Change the speed to be delivered to the
differential.
☐ Differential – Controls the rotation of rear wheels of the tractor. It
allows one wheel to rotate or to stop for the purpose of ease of
pivoting the tractor during operation.
☐ Final Drive – Further converts the high speed to the slow gear to
obtain better torque.
☐ Rear Axle – Delivers the power from the final drive to the rear
wheel of the tractor.
☐ Rear Wheel – Provides the draft to pull the implement.

☐ Plowing and other operations are affected by the drawbar

assuming an engine efficiency of 80%? 	What is the estimated PTO
power, wheel axle power, and drawbar power of the tractor if its
transmission efficiencies are 90%, 92%, and 81%, respectively.

Engine speed 	- 2200 rpm

Mean Eff Pressure - 180 psi

Engine stroke 	- 4
Engine efficiency 	- 80%

Solution:

m/sec-hp] x 2
= 646.7 hp

= 517.4 hp

AGRICULTURAL IMPLEMENTS AND
EQUIPMENT
Agricultural Field Implement 	- These are the machines used
to perform specific task during crop production and post
production operations. This includes tillage, seeding and
planting, crop, cultivating, spraying and dusting, harvesting and
threshing/shelling operations.
Power Source for Field Implement
1. 	Human
2. 	Draft Animal
3. 	Engine and Tractor

☐ Tractor – a machine used primarily
for traction or pulling purposes. It can
also deliver both power for stationary
and mobile tasks. It can pull or tow
implement through traction from drive
wheel and or pull implement through
the draft developed from the drawbar
hitch of the tractor.
☐ Internal Combustion Engine (ICE)
is a device that produces power by
burning normally liquid fuel inside the
combustion chamber of an engine.
Available as spark-ignition or diesel
ignition engines with single or multiple
cylinders depending on the power
needed.

(1) Pull-Type or Trailing
Implement
It is pulled and guided from a
single hitch point and is not
completely supported b the
tractor. The implement is
provided with a ground wheel
which can be used during
transport and trailing operation.
Depth of tillage implement is
completely controlled by the
hydraulic drive of the tractor by
changing the position of the
ground wheel.
TRACTOR-DRAWN IMPLEMENT
TYPES

(2) Mounted Implement
It is hitch completely to the
three-point hitch system of a
tractor. The implement is
usually carried by the tractor
during travel to the field.
Depth of implement cut is
controlled by the three-point
hitch system of the tractor
operated by its hydraulic
system. Commonly used for
small to medium size
tractors or ease of transport
and maneuverability during
operation.

Advantages
(1) Mounted equipment are less expensive that equivalent
pull-type equipment;
(2) Support wheels and accompanying structure required
on pull-type equipment is eliminated;
(3) Single-depth or height control system forming a part of
the tractor.
● Maneuverability better
● Visibility is better
● Transport is easier
● Draft-sensing is advantage
● Vertical load transfer to aid in traction is possible
● Attaching and detaching is easier
● Standardization of three-point hitch and quick attaching
couplers are available.
Limitations
(1) Carrying capacity of tractor chassis
(2) Transport stability is a limitation

(3) Semi-Mounted Implement
It is attached to the tractor
through a horizontal or nearly
horizontal hinge axis and
partially supported by the
tractor at least during transport,
but it is never completely
supported by the tractor.
Support wheel at the rear or in
the middle together with remote
hydraulic are utilized for raising
and lowering the complete
implement machine or it
individual units.


Advantages
(1) Greater flexibility
(2) Better Maneuverability
(3) Better visibility
(4) Better control by operator
(5) Improved mobility
(6) Reduce losses when cutting mechanism is in front of the unit
Disadvantages
(1) High initial investment hence it should have higher annual
use to be economically competitive with pull=type machine.
SELF-PROPELLED MACHINE
☐ Self-Propelled
An implement with propelling unit as
integral part of the machine. Example of
this is rice transplanter, combine harvester,
etc.


☐ Self-Driven or Autonomous
An implement that is equipped
with integrated systems,
computers, and processors.
Electrical impulses is transferred
into the controller or CPU to
enable the equipment to perform.
Example, drone sprayer, field
mower, etc.
The machine is automated to
perform farming tasks, reduce
labor cost, and improve the
efficiency, yield, and crop quality.
SELF-DRIVEN OR AUTONOMOUS
MACHINE
The main disadvantages are:
high initial cost, limited
capability, dependence n
technology, lack of flexibility,
impact on employment.

(1) Theoretical Field Capacity of Machine – Field efficiency
decreases with the increase in TFC and with increase in
operating speed of the implement.
(2) Machine Maneuverability – Farm machine need to be easily
maneuvered in the field and on the roads to the field. Field
machines need to e designed to make short turns at end of the
field and while following crops row planted on the contour and in
curves.
FACTORS AFFECTING FIELD EFFICIENCY
It is the ratio of effective field capacity to theoretical field capacity
in %. It includes the effect of time lost in the field and failure to
utilize the full with of the machine.
FIELD EFFICIENCY

(3) Field Patterns
[To minimize the amount of field travel. The lesser, the
nonproductive time the higher is the field efficiency of the
tractor/implement unit]
(1) Amount of field travel should be minimum;
(2) Number of non-working turn should be minimum;
(3) Number of non-working travel in interior of field should be
minimum;
(4) Field pattern should produce level surface to eliminate
water ponding; and
(5) Repeated machine travel over a particular area of field will
cause compaction of soil.

(4) Field Shape
An irregular field has less field efficiency than rectangular field.
Turning in a rectangular shape will require lesser time as compared
with the irregular shape field.
(5) Field Size
Field efficiency of large field is more than smaller field due to less
time consume in turning the field.
(6) Field Condition
This includes slopy field, type of soil to be processed (example
plowing, harrowing, etc), moisture content of the soil like dry land
farming or wet field and many others.
Therefore it is important to properly select the power source for the
machine and equipment needed in order to properly mechanize the farm.

Photos, illustrations and schematic diagrams of equipment or machine parts are shown in the

mentioned.

☐ Crop production and processing play important roles in
producing food for consumption of million Filipinos and of
people around the world.
☐ Agricultural machines for field operation as well as postharvest
processing equipment necessitated information on the required
energy to provide power in performing the tasks to produce the
expected output for which they are designed and used.
☐ Efficient method of energy conversion to power and their
transmission play a vital role in achieving a shorter process
time and cheaper products.
INTRODUCTION

☐ Reports revealed that more energy is used during the field
operation than during the processing of the product. In US, 90%
of the total energy demanded is used during the field production
and the remaining 10% is used during product processing.
☐ Knowing carefully the importance of efficiently using energy for a
particular application or task would be significantly helpful in
maximizing the use of the available energy; thus, would result in
a more reduced cost in operating the machines and would
achieve cheaper product.
☐ Below describes some important considerations in achieving a
more desirable efficient operation of agricultural machines. Data
on the various efficiencies of agricultural machines during
operation as well as of their components are provided herein to
provide engineers idea on how to achieve efficient operation.

OPTIMIZING TRACTOR EFFICIENCY
1. 	Select AMTEC Test Data as
reference for tractor performance
and other relevant information.
This is more useful when comparing
the different makes and models of
tractors and farm equipment.
2. 	Properly maintain tractor condition
always. 	Timely replacement of air
and fuel filters and lubricants can
reduce fuel use while increasing
horsepower. Repair of leaking valve
and piston rings will improve engine
performance and therefore increase
energy efficiency.
3. 	Reclaim old fuels and oil in one
way to minimize energy use by
using fewer fossil fuels.

4. 	Adopt reduced tillage to save fuel. Conservation tillage
generally uses less fuel than full tillage system because the
soil is tilled less intensively and not frequently. These tillage
practices may also allow seedbed preparation, fertilizer
application, and seeding in fewer passes. Such practices are
also eligible for carbon credits.
5. 	Gear up and throttle back to save on fuel. Make sure not
to overload the engine; excessive black smoke indicates
overloading.

6. 	Optimize wheel slippage to reduce excess wear on tires.
Optimum level is generally 10% but the actual level depends on
the type of tractor, the speed, and the implement being used.
7. 	Ballast the tractor correctly with the recommended tire
inflation rates to improve fuel consumption and increase
tractor efficiency by creating the required amount of tire
slippage for the specific tractor implement and field conditions.

8. 	Match implement size to the tractor. Large tractor for light
loads is inefficient because extra horsepower is used to move
the large tractor. Using tractor to perform operations that
require more horsepower can overload a smaller tractor;
hence, reducing its fuel consumption and efficiency.
9. 	Select the optimal engine and travel speeds. Most tractor
engines have the highest fuel efficiency when operated at or
near rated speed and load or maximum power. For primary
tillage implements properly matched with the tractor, the best
fuel efficiency in the field is achieved by pulling loads at the
fastest speed possible within the acceptable speed range for
the implement.

10. 	Optimize efficiency of field operation. Field efficiency
refers to the time the operation takes versus turning and

11. 	Fuel storage can save fuel before it goes into the
tractor. Keep above ground fuel storage tanks shaded,
and paint them with light color to reduce the loss of fuel by
evaporation.

12. 	Practice precision agriculture because it saves energy.
Site-specific farming using equipment guidance systems, yield
monitoring systems, field mapping, and precision crop input
application provide many economic and environmental benefits
in addition to energy savings.
13. 	Use biodiesel or other biofuels to reduce reliance on
petroleum products. Be sure that the alternative fuel is of good
quality as of the current diesel fuel used.
14. 	Reduce emissions. New engines are expected to be both
more energy efficient and have fewer emission.

PREDOMINANT MEASURES IN
ACHIEVING ENERGY
EFFICIENCY
☐ Use Diesel Fuel and Engines
They are more advantageous for agricultural
applications because they are capable of
accomplishing a given amount of work with
approximately only 10% or less fuel than
gasoline engines. Diesel contains more
energy per liter and usually less expensive
than gasoline. Diesel engines require less
maintenance. Typically, however, diesel
engine requires more capital investment
than gasoline engine.

☐ Match the Equipment with the Operation
Use appropriate machinery for a given task. Tractors are more
efficient when used near capacity. It is desirable to use smaller
tractor for operation requiring lighter load and larger tractors for
operation requiring heavier load.

☐ Follow Good Maintenance Practices
A little preventive maintenance goes a long way towards improving
efficiency. Tune up engine regularly, clean air filters, clean electrical
equipment, and provide proper lubrication. Insure tractor tires are
inflated to the correct pressure to optimize traction. Keep
implements in good repair. Make sure that the blades are sharp in
order to reduce resistance during field operation.

☐ Operate Equipment Properly
Careful operation of the tractor and implements optimizes fuel
efficiency. Make sure that the machinery and controls are adjusted
correctly for the particular operation. Reduce unnecessary idling. It
is more efficient to turn the equipment off during extended breaks
than to run it. Tractor will also work efficiently if the correct tire
tread is chosen for the soil condition.

☐ Use Ballast of the Tractor Correctly
Provide proper ballast for the tractor for a given field condition. If
the tractor is heavier than necessary for an operation, the additional
weight can result in soil compaction as well as decrease fuel
economy. If there is no enough ballast on the tractor, on the other
hand, the wheels are more prone to slip and wear on the tires is
increased. For tractor with insufficient ballast for a particular
operation, adding wheel weights can increase the ballast.

☐ Optimize Traffic Patterns on the Field
It is best to reduce the frequency of turns during the field
operation. One way to accomplish this is by traveling lengthwise
along a rectangular field. This will reduce the number of turns
when compared with traveling parallel to the width of short sides.
Also, it is important to eliminate unnecessary overlap while
traversing the field. Reducing turns and minimizing overlap save
both fuel and time.


☐ Balance Yield with Energy Use
The yield is increased by using equipment capable of operating at
higher speeds and with wider implements. Heavy duty equipment is
more expensive and use more fuel than slower, lighter equipment.
The benefits of increased yield need to be balanced with the higher
capital and energy cost associated with heavier tractors and wider
implements.

☐ Combined Operations to Reduce Trips
Over the Field
To reduce fuel use is to combine multiple implements and operation
in one past. In some cases, it is possible to form seedbed, fertilize,
and sow the seeds in a single pass rather than in three passes.

☐ Select Efficient Equipment
The energy efficiency of the equipment being used is an obvious
determinant of fuel consumption per unit output. It is best to
purchase efficient equipment at the outset even though it might
require a higher initial investment than standard equipment.
However, it is important to conduct an economic analysis to insure
that the calculated payback periods are acceptable. Tractors are
often operable for several decades so inefficient equipment can
result in high operating cost that can continue for many years. It is
less cost-effective to replace existing equipment with high-
efficiency equipment before the original equipment has reached
the end of its useful life.

☐ There is a need to understand
some more additional items in the
careful selection of agricultural
machinery.
☐ The following are important factors
to consider in judging and in
influencing the selection of
agricultural machines: (a) trademark;
(b) trade name; (c) model; (d) repair;
(e) design; (f) ease of operation; (g)
ease of adjustment; (h) adaptability
to work and condition; (i) quick
changes of units; (j) maneuverability;
(k) comfort; and (l) other factors.
INTRODUCTION

☐ A distinguishing mark, device, or symbol affixed by a
manufacturer, merchant, or trader to his goods in order to identify
them as his goods and distinguish them from the goods
manufactured, sold, or dealt in by others.
☐ Trademark gives statutory protection when it is registered
according to law which gives the owner the exclusive right to use its
product.
☐ Trademark provides guarantee of reliability of the machine since
the company will stand behind its product or machine.
TRADEMARK

☐ Name by which an article is called
or the name given by a manufacturer
to an article to distinguish it as one
produced by the company. It is also
called as brand name.
☐ Trade or brand name can be
registered to have statutory
protection in a manner similar to
trademark.
☐ It can only be found in only one
particular machine. It is presently
abandoned in favor of model
designation.
TRADE NAME

☐ Model indicates the
type, size, improvement,
or new design of an old
machine, a special
purpose or combination
of one or more of
machine features.
☐ Model designation are
presented by series of
numbers or letters or
combination of both.
Example, a combine
model SP-12 is a self-
propelled combine
having a width-cut of 12
ft.
MODEL


☐ Before considering a purchase of the machine, it is well to look
into the source of repairs.
☐ Can the repair be made at hand or it needs somebody to send
from a distance?
☐ Machine breakdown can cause delay and lost of crops.
☐ Some manufacturers provide quick service for the machinery they
supplied.
☐ Be sure that repair and supply of machine parts are readily
available in the locality.
REPAIR

☐ Technical Manual – It is a booklet
provided by manufacturers in which the
step-by-step procedure for repair or
disassembly of parts are given.
☐ Operator’s Manual – It is a booklet form
provided by manufacturers in which
adjustment, care and maintenance
procedure, and safety of the machine are
indicated.

☐ Name and address of manufacturer
☐ Brand name, model number, and year made or purchased
☐ Number of parts wanted
☐ If the number of the parts cannot be determined, get the numbers
of the parts with which it works
Keep the pamphlets that are furnished with the machine especially
the one containing the repair parts list. When repair parts are
needed, the part numbers and their description will be found in the
lists parts.
INFORMATION NEEDED IN MAKING
ORDER
FOR REPAIR OF PARTS

☐ Design is the arrangement of the
parts to show the difference of make
up in machine of the same type.
☐ Gears should run in a sealed oil
bath.
☐ Provision of safety devices
should be carefully considered.
Does the machine have finished appearance and style without
sacrificing strength and performance?
DESIGN

☐ Many implements that look well are
fond to require an unnecessary amount of
power and labor to make them operate
successfully.
☐ A dealer who is a good one will usually
take the machine out, have the farmer go
along, make necessary adjustments, and
see that the machine is running perfectly
before turning it over to the farmer.
EASE OF OPERATION

☐ Careful study should be made on the
methods of adjusting the various parts of
the machine.
☐ Devices designed to simplify adjusting
the equipment are time and labor savers.
☐ The owner’s or operator’s manual
should be studied thoroughly to
understand the method of adjusting the
equipment as recommended by the
designers and the test engineer.
☐ Many operators of agricultural
machines are not inclined to taking
sufficient time to make the needed
adjustments.
EASE OF ADJUSTMENT

☐ There are many implements in the market which are not adaptable
to every condition.
☐ A machine may work in one locality and be an absolute failure in
another because it is adapted to a certain soil condition or type of
crop grown.
ADAPTABILITY TO WORK AND
CONDITIONS

☐ The time and labor required to dismount one unit and mount
another unit are important considerations in selecting agricultural
equipment.
☐ Some lines of equipment are built in unit packages and are
designed so that changes can be made in a few minutes from plow
to planter, from planter to cultivator, or from one unit to another for
all the units supplied.
QUICK CHANGES OF UNITS

☐ As a general rule, tractor-mounted equipment are provided with
power and hydraulic lifts. The units can be lifted and the tractor
manuevered almost as though no equipment was attached.
☐ When trailing equipment is attached to the drawbar of a tractor,
turns cannot be made so sharply as with mounted equipment.
MANEUVERABILITY

☐ As the operator of power equipment must
spend days after days riding upon it, the
comfort and safety of the seat should be
considered.
☐ A comfortable seat should be supported
with shock-absorbing devices. The seat
should be stable and adjustable to suit
different-sizes of individuals.
☐ Cabs give protection from cold, heat,
dust, and excessive noise.
COMFORT

☐ Power requirements
☐ Cost of operation
☐ Initial cost
☐ Years of service expected
☐ Whether the purchase of the equipment is economical in relation
to the size of the farm and work to be performed by the equipment.
OTHER FACTORS

GENERAL GUIDELNES IN THE
SELECTION OF TRACTOR
☐ Tractor Size - is estimated based on the validated condition in the
field characterized by soil type and it specific draft, the estimated
working speed, and the type of implement to be used and the
corresponding working width and depth.
☐ Draft - is determined by the resistance of the soil to tillage or the
implement being pulled by the tractor in the field. The higher the
resistance of the soil, the higher is the power requirement. This
can be computed as,
Draft adjusted = Specific draft x Width x Depth x
% draft increase

☐ Speed - Tractor speed is influence by the type of soil and
working width and depth of implement which may affect the
utilization and power during operation. The speed of the tractor
are characterized by slow (2 kph), medium (5 kph, and fast (7
kph). Corresponding increase due to speed should be
accounted in estimating size of the tractor.
☐ Width - The rated width of the implement maybe determined
based on the desired working capacity in the field or the
duration of passing the implement in the entire field to be
cultivated. This can be computed as
Width = Field Capacity x 10 / (Speed x Efficiency)
☐ Depth - 	is the vertical distance from the initial soil surface a a
specified point of penetration of the tool. Different crop have
different depth requirement for tillage.

TERMINOLOGIES
☐ Draft – resistance of the soil to tillage operation.
☐ Drawbar Power – power available and measured at the drawbar or
at the point where implement were attached.
☐ Four-Wheel Tractor – self-propelled wheeled vehicle having two
axles designed to carry, pull or propel\ agricultural implements and
machines.
☐ Four-Wheel Tractor – Two Wheel Drive (2WD) – A four-wheel
tractor that can receive tractive power from the rear axle only and
can deliver up to 50% of their rated engine power at the drawbar.
☐ Four-Wheel Tractor – Four-Wheel Drive (4WD) – A four-wheel
tractor that can receive tractive power from both front and rear
wheel and can deliver up to 60% power at the drawbar.
☐ Implement – tools that are attached to an agricultural tractor for
performing various task on farm land.
☐ Power Take Off – device located at the end of the tractor that
provides rotational power implement and machines.

☐ Rated Power – maximum engine power at rated engine rated.
☐ Roll-Over Protection Structure – cab or frame installed on
agricultural tractors to protect the operator from accidental over
turning during operation.
☐ Specific Fuel Consumption – amount of fuel consumed by the
tractor for each unit of power output.
☐ Tillage – any soil manipulation which develops desirable soil
structure for a seedbed and destroy weeds and rearrange dead
plant materials.
☐ Transmission System – an enclosed system of assembled gears
that transmit and distributes power from engine to the different
parts of the transmission system and maybe classified as sliding
gears, constant mesh, and automatic transmission.

GENERAL GUIDELNES IN THE
SELECTION OF FARM
MACHINES
☐ Farm mechanization is essential for efficiency in farm operation.
☐ Selecting the right farm equipment and machinery allows you to
reduce operational expenses, generate more profit, and grow more
crops with lesser efforts.
☐ Acquiring the right machinery for farm operation is not an easy
task.

KEY FACTORS NEED TO CONSIDER
WHEN SELECTING THE RIGHT
EQUIPMENT FOR FARM BUSINESS
☐ Performance
There are several readily available agricultural machines which are
accessible to farmers use. When selecting machinery, the machine
should be worthy to invest and capable to perform to their field
condition. Example, tillage implement should prepare satisfactory
seedbed while conserving moisture, destroying weed growth and
minimizing soil erosion. Planters and seeder should provide
consistent seed placement and population, etc.
☐ Soils
The equipment to be used should match with the type of soil to be
cultivated. Example, sandy soil must be to use light equipment and
heavy soil with heavy equipment. Use of plow with the type of soil
condition must be properly selected.

☐ Size of Operations
If land area is quite big, the use of tractor, combine harvester can
be justified. If soil is soft and muddy, this may require another kind
of machine to effective till the soil
☐ Capital
Availability f capital determines the type of machines to be
acquired. Possible instead of buying, hiring equipment ca be an
option. With enough capital more durable machines or efficient
equipment can be purchased.
☐ Operating Costs
Amount need associated when operating the machine. Fuel ,
lubrication, service and repairs.
☐ Availability of Repairing Facility or Service Center
Ae there facility where the machine can be repaired in case of
breakdown.
☐ Type of Business
What machinery will be needed? This depend on the type of farm
business is engaged. If rice farming farm machine need fr rice
production, ost havest and processing would be selected.

spent versus the turning and other

a. 	Field capacity
b. 	Field load factor
c. 	Field efficiency

3. 	Ways to save energy through the

SAFETY IN AGRICULTURAL
MACHINES
VOLUME 3 – AGRICULTURAL MACHINERY AND
MECHANIZATION
by
Engr. Alexis T. Belonio, MS
Agricultural and Biosystems Engineer
ASEAN Engineer
2024 AGRICULTURAL AND BIOSYSTEMS ENGINEERING
BOARD EXAM REVIEWER

Disclaimer
Photos, illustrations and schematic diagrams of equipment or machine parts are shown in the
presentation solely for educational purposes to facilitate comprehension of the topics by the students.
Showing them does not endorse a product nor imply criticism of similar products not mentioned.

☐ Operation of agricultural equipment has
many hazards, and accidents can be
reduced if the safety precautions are
carefully followed.
☐“Safety first” is a slogan that should be
kept in mind at all times.
☐ Many of the accidents that occur in
operating agricultural equipment are the
direct results of thoughtlessness and
carelessness.
☐ Accidents are more likely to occur with
power-operated equipment that has moving
parts in performing its operating function.
INTRODUCTION

☐ Avoid climbing over running
machines.
☐ Stay away from loose banks and
ditches.
☐ Do not get in front of moving
machines to make adjustments.
☐ Check haying machines for unsafe
rope, pulley, etc.
☐ Always keep shields and guards over
power shafts, chains and gears.
☐ Keep doors of a building open when
running gasoline equipment inside.
OPERATORS’ RESPONSIBILITY FOR
SAFETY


☐ Make sure the tractor and others are out
of gear before starting.
☐ Do not attempt to put on or take off belts
from power running pulleys.
☐ Check hazards and be careful at all times.
☐ When pulling heavy objects, hitch under
center of the tractor.
☐ When driving on highways, use adequate
signal lights at night and red flags by day.
☐ Keep extra riders off of moving tractors
and vehicles.
☐ Prevent upset and overturns by careful
driving up and down and across steep
slopes.

☐ Hold speed within safe limits of 4.5
mph.
☐ Stop corn picker and other machines
before attempting to unchoke them.
☐ Keep children away from machinery,
both stationary and moving.
☐ Avoid loose clothing and ragged
gloves around moving machinery.

☐ Cabs serve as safety devices on
tractors and they should be reinforced
with a roll bar or the roll-on-protective
structure.
☐ Strong cabs protect the operator from
being crushed in case the tractor rolls
over. It also protects the operator from
dusts, noise, heat, and cold.
☐ When cab is used, a check should be
made to be sure that the exhaust pipe
from the engine is extended far enough
away from the cab to prevent the
exhaust fumes from entering the cab.
☐ All tractors not equipped with strong
cabs should be provided with safety roll
bars.
CABS FOR FARM EQUIPMENT


☐ The National Safety Council of US recommends that all slow-
moving vehicles operated on highways should have a safety
emblem attached to the equipment in a manner so that the emblem
can be easily seen.
☐ The emblem is triangular in shape. The central portion is
fluorescent orange; while, the 4in. border is reflective dark red.
☐ If a slow-moving vehicle moves at night, it should be equipped
with amber-colored flashing lights.
SAFETY EMBLEM


☐ Power driven implements.
• Ensure all guards are in place;
• Do not make adjustments on moving parts or clear
blockages while the machine is running;
• Always disengage the PTO drive when work ceases
even if only temporarily; and
• Even when the PTO is disengaged, it is safer to stop the
tractor engine before working on the machine.
☐ Do not work under implement held in raised position by the
tractor hydraulic.
SAFETY PRECAUTIONS


☐ Never leave the driving seat while outfit is in motion.
☐ Always attach trailed implement to the proper drawbar and
never to a high position on the rear of the tractor.
☐ Always use proper draw pin with a locking device.
☐ Never leave self-lift implements in raised position.
☐ Allow adequate headlands, especially when using trailed
implements near bank, river, and ditches.
☐ Ensure that the tractor is jacked securely when altering
wheels for row-crop work.
☐ Avoid the temptation to clear tooth harrows by lifting them
manually when the outfit is in motion, and never leave such
harrows inverted in the field after use.

☐ Smith, H. P. and L.H. Wilkes. 1976. Farm Machinery and
Equipment. 6th Edition. Tata McGraw-Hill Publishing Company Ltd.
New Delhi. 488pp.
REFERENCES

QUESTIONS AND PROBLEMS

safety code is used for _____.
a. 	floors or work areas around
machines and equipment
b. traffic and housekeeping areas
c. areas with radiation hazard
d. All of the above

and white color, it indicates that the
pipe contains _____.
a. liquid of inherently low hazard
b. fire extinguishing materials
c. flammable or explosive materials
d. All of the above

moving vehicles such as animal-drawn
or motorized conveyance, including
implements in tow, should not exceed
____ travel speed.
a. _30 kph
b. 40 kph
c. 50 kph
d. 	None of the above
4. For safety purposes, slow-moving
vehicles such as agricultural machines
must be provided with _____.
a. 	rear bumper to protect the machine
from impact
b. 	identification emblem to guide
motorists that the machine is slow
moving
c. signal light when travelling
d. None of the above
5. Protective device which is usually
made of rail, fence or frame to keep
dangerous parts of a machine out of
reach inadvertently.
a. Shield
b. Casing
c. Enclosure
d. None of the above

6. Protective device designed and fitted
to prevent dangerous parts of a machine
from being reached from the side.
a. Shield
b. Casing
c. Enclosure
d. None of the above
7. Protective device designed and fitted
to prevent dangerous parts of a machine
from being reached from all sides.
a. Shield
b. Casing
c. Enclosure
d. None of the above
8. In ASABE’s safety code for
laboratory equipment and typical
applications, the safety yellow color
stands for _____.
a. danger stop
b. warning
c. caution
d. None of the above
10. When running gasoline equipment
inside an enclosed farm shed, it is
required that the door of the building
must be ____ for safety.
a. 	closed
b. 	opened
c. 	covered
d. 	None of the above
11. Shape for the safety emblem of
moving agricultural equipment.
a. 	Square
b. 	Rectangle
c. 	Triangle
d. 	All of the above
12. Standard color of the central
portion of the safety emblem for slow
moving vehicle.
a. 	Fluorescent orange
b. 	Reflective dark red
c. 	Light fluorescent green
d. 	All of the above

13. Size of the reflective dark red
boarder for the safety emblem.
a. Double 2-in boarder
b. Four 1-in boarder
c. 4 in. boarder
d. None of the above
14. When doing repair of the PTO driven
implement it is required that ______.
a. 	operation PTO must be stopped
b. 	the implement must be lowered on
ground
c. 	the tractor engine must be stopped
d. 	All of the above
e. 	None of the above
15. When hitching trailed implement
always use ________ .
a. 	three-point hitch system to draw the
implement
b. 	drawbar hitch pin with a bolt
c. 	proper draw pin with lock
d. 	None of the above
16. When altering wheels of a tractor
for row-crop work, the tractor must be
____ .
a. 	In neutral position
b. 	jacked securely
c. 	supported manually
d. 	All of the above
17. All tractors not equipped with strong
cabs should be provided with _______.
a. 	safety roll bars
b. 	safety support frame
c. 	Safety glass cover
d. 	All of the above
18. When starting the tractor, make
sure that it must be ___.
a. 	filled with fuel
b. 	out of gear
c. 	Properly connected to a battery.
d. 	None of the above

19. All belt and pulley drive of rice
threshing machine must be provided
with _____ for safety reason.
a. 	belt guard
b. 	belt support
c. 	belt cover
d. 	None of the above
20. Belt replacement must be done
when pulley is in _____ .
a. running position
b. stopped position
c. idling position
d. None of the above
21. Strong cabs protect the operator
from _____ .
a. 	being crushed
b. 	dusts and noise
c. 	heat and cold.
d. 	All of the above
e. 	None of the above

☐ Agricultural machines undergoes
design and development process before
it become useful for farm operation.
☐ The design and development
processes undergoes several stages
before it goes for manufacturing.
☐ Manufacturing of the final proto-type
units are carefully analyze in accordance
to the materials required, manufacturing
processes to be done before units are
finally produced ready for market.
☐ On the other hand, manufactured

such as machine, power, and operator
performances before it is fully utilized in
the farm

DESIGN
☐ Designing agricultural machines
suitable for farmers is quite a difficult
job because one should come up
with a machine that is applicable,
efficient but of low cost.
☐ In order for the designer to meet
this challenge, he or she needs to
have enough skills and ability to do
the job.
☐ Unless the designer tries to meet
the requirements of actual users, no
amount of design work will be
utilized.
☐ The success of a good design is
indicated by the extent by which the
machine is adopted by farmers.

☐ Designing Agricultural machines – Highly innovative and
cross-disciplinary process that uses the most acceptable
aesthetic, efficiency, and economical means to satisfy farmer’s
need.
☐ This process includes the following:
1. Literature search – to understand the technology based on
the reports their parameters, performance, relationship of various
components and others. This minimize the issue on “reinventing
the wheel” or repeating the same mistakes.
2. Conducting Proof of Concept Study – A simplified study of
the design to check if it works according to the design or not. In
here, the operation is check whether it will work or not.
3. Experimental Test of Variables Needed – conduct
experimental test to gather data that cannot be obtain in the
literature search. This will help the designer to minimize possible
error or problem during the design process.

4. Conceptual Design Preparation – a simple drawing identifying
the various components of the machine and their functions to the
machine. At least three design will be made for detailed analysis
and discussion.
5 Deign Drawing Preparation – Isometric and detailed
component need to be prepared to see the accuracy of the different
components in terms of mechanical movement, etc. There are
computer programs can help on the other parameters needed in th
design.
6. Preparation of the Material and Equipment Lists – This can
provide the information of all the materials (Fabrication, Standard,
Consumable, etc) needed to fabricate the proto-type unit of the
machine.

☐ Rational Design – carried out using mathematical formula and
other engineering principles.
☐ Empirical Design – based upon empirical formula derived from
existing practices and past experiences.
☐ Industrial Design – involves consideration like aesthetics,
ergonomics, and production aspects.
A. 	Based on the Design Information and Consideration Needed in
Coming Up with the Product
Classifications of Design

B. Based on the Process Taking Place in Coming
Up with the Product
☐ Original Design – does not exist before and it is only done by
few dedicated designers who have personal qualities of a
sufficiently high order. This also requires a lot of research,
experimental activities, and creative brains.
☐ Adaptive Design – more concerned on the adoption of existing
designs. This does not demand special knowledge or skills.
Problems can be solved with ordinary training.
☐ Development Design - 	begins with an existing design but the
final result may quietly differ from the initial product.

Development Design
Adaptive Design
Original Design

Characteristics of Well-Designed Agricultural
Machine
(1) Performance target is attained with high efficiency.
(2) High reliability, robust, dependable requiring minimum repair
and, if possible, trouble-free.
(3) User-friendly and easy to understand and operate.
(4) Minimum maintenance is required that can be done even by
the local people.
(5) Spare parts are readily available and easy to replace once
needed.
(6) Investment cost is at the reach of farmers or to the one who will
own it and use for custom operation.
(7) Low operating cost and readily-available inputs, such as fuel,
electricity, manpower.
(8) Environmentally safe to operate and, as much as possible. no
toxic emissions are emitted.
(9) Enough warranty service.

FABRICATION MATERIALS
☐ Metals
(1) Ferrous - Iron and steel
Cast Iron, Carbon Steel,
Alloy Steel, etc.
(2) Non- Ferrous
Aluminum, copper, magnesium,
etc.
☐ Non-Metal
(1) Inorganic materials
glass, ceramics, plastic, etc.
(2) Organic Materials
wood, rubber, leather, canvass,
etc.
Classifications of Materials

☐ Standard parts of agricultural
machines play a very important role in
the construction and performance of the
machine.
☐ They are especially manufactured
and mass produced to perform a
specific function.
☐ They can be readily purchased from
stores and hardware, and are available
in various sizes.
This includes the following: (1) Bearing,
(2) Belt and Pulley, (3)Sprocket and
chain, (4) gears, (5) Bolts and nuts, (6)
etc
Standard Materials

Fabrication Materials
☐ These are the raw materials that came from hardware or steel
manufacturers/distributors which are processed into various sizes
and shapes as required to build a agricultural machines.
☐ They vary in the engineering properties, quality, cost, etc which
are supplied in standard sizes such as 6m for bars and pipes, and
1.2m x 2.4 for plates and sheets.
☐ Mostly are made of malleable steel, high carbon steel such as
cold rolled and high carbon steel. In terms of sheets and plates, BI
or GI sheets are readily available including stainless steel.
☐ Boiler plate and pipes including tool steel can be ordered from
steel suppliers in big cities like Manila.
☐ This includes the following:
(1) Sheet
(2).Plates
(3) Bars
(4).Pipes
(5) Etc

Consumables
☐ These are the materials use to accomplish the various fabrication
processes until the desired product is built and ready for evaluation
and development.
☐ This includes the following:
(1) Cutting (14in.) and grinding disks (4 in.)
(2) Drill bits
(3) Oxygen and acetylene
(4) Compressed air
(5) Welding rods (6013, etc)
(6) Welding wires and CO2 (MIG) and argon (TIG)
(7) Cutting Tools for milling machine
(8) Paint, Thinner (Acrylic and lacquer), brush and roller

☐ Layouting – preparing the materials into a specific shapes and
dimensions manually using prick punch, divider, measuring tape,
etc. In state of the art fabrication, the drawing can provide the
command to cut the materials into the specified layout.
FABRICATION PROCESSES

☐ Cutting – separation of the
materials accurately as per
required in the layout.
1. Shear Cutting
a. Thin shear
b. Cut off or disc cutting
b. Bench shear
2. Saw
a. Power hacksaw
b. Band saw
3. Flame Cutting
a. Oxyacetylene torch –
high pressure using oxygen
and acetylene
3. Plasma Cutting – using
electricity and compressed air
4. Wire Cutting – bronze wire
with electricity on it
5. Laser Cutting – laser jet
6. Water Jet – High pressure


☐ Forming 	- This is the process usually carried out for sheet,
plates, and bars using malleable steel to form cylinders, boxes,
circles, or bends. Equipment commonly used are as follows:
(1) Roller bender – to form cylinders and cone
(2) Press brake – smaller piece to fold into a suitable angles
(3) Bar folder – to form boxes that cannot be done in
press brake
(4) Etc
In small fabrication shops, this process is sub contracted from well
established machine shops.

☐ Milling – Commonly used
for high carbon materials such
as axle to fit in bearings,
pulleys, drives, and keyways
for axles. 	This uses various
milling machines to make
shapes of hard metals as
machine components.
Similarly, this milling of
machine parts in small shops
ar subcontracted from machine
shops.

☐ Welding – is the process of
joining metal parts fixed together
by melting each part and allow
to fuse together with other
metals. There are varieties
methods of welding materials as
follows:
(1) Soldering
(2) Brazing
(3) Resistance
(4) Arc
(5) MIG
(6) TIG
(7) Laser
In agricultural machines, jigs are
commonly used during welding
to properly fixed parts in
position.


☐ Finishing – is the removal of
protruded parts of machine
parts by means of grinding and
to make its surface smooth.
Suitable paints are also applied
during finishing metal to protect
the metal from corrosion and to
improve its esthetic value.
(1) Grinding
(2) Painting (brush, rollers,
spray)

☐ Assembling – putting all parts together to completely form
the different parts of the machine. In large manufacturing firm,
this process is being done in an assembly plants ready for
market and delivery. Assembly tools includes the following:
(1) Wrenches (open. box, socket, torque, pipe, monkey,
etc)
(2) Vise grip and pliers
(3) Ballpeen hammer
(4) Screw drivers (Philippine and flat)

1. 	Determine whether the machine parts
function as designed or not;
2. 	Observe and gather information on the
specific performance of machine parts;
3. 	Determine parts of the machine that need to
be modified or improved;
4. 	Determine the overall performance
(technical and operational) of the machine;
5. 	Prepare the machine specifications;
6. 	Determine whether machine performs
according to the specification set by the
manufacturer; and
7. 	Compare the machine with other similar
machines in terms of technical, economics,
social, and environmental acceptability.
TESTING AND EVALUATION

MANUFACTURING
☐ Manufacturing of agricultural machines in the Philippines begun
as early as Spanish period when tools and small equipment are
fabricated for farm use.
☐ In early 60’s, manufacturing was concentrated on the fabrication
of small farm tools and attachment for four-wheel tractors used in
sugar plantation.
☐ Locally-made hand tractors started to appear in 1972. The
design of a hand tractor was adopted from manufacturers in Bicol
and at IRRI. Back then, about 33 manufactures and enterprises
assemble farm machines.

☐ In the middle of 70’s, locally-produced hand tractors captured 40% of
the market. Most of the manufacturers fabricating hand tractors have
the capability in producing other farm machines.
☐ In 1984, the DA-IRRI Program for Extension of Small Farm
Equipment reported that there were about 206 cooperating
manufactures in the country producing various agricultural machines.
☐ This handout gives the brief description and classifications of
manufacturing agricultural machinery in the Philippines.

☐ By Piece – The manufacturer fabricates the machine by piece,
i.e., only one at a time. Usually, one to two persons are
commissioned to do the entire work to produce the machine. The
machine basically is directly contracted from individual farmer or
user.
Classification of manufacturer according to
manufacturing capability

☐ By Batch – The manufacturer fabricates the machine in
several number of pieces as per contract with the dealer. The
manufacturer has almost have all the tools and equipment except
for special machine components, that need to be subcontracted.

☐ Mass Production – The manufacturer produces the machine
beyond the number of pieces produced in the batch system. Even
without direct order or purchase from the customer or dealer, the
manufacturer still produces the machine for possible unforeseen
market.

☐ Small Manufacturer – small manufacturing enterprises that are
usually capable of manufacturing agricultural machines by piece
only. They are usually backyard fabrication in operation and
basically use common fabrication equipment, such as hand saw,
welding machines, and some power drill and sanders.
Classification of manufacturer according to
size

☐ Medium-Size Manufacturer – capable to operate and produce
agricultural machine by batch and do mass production of small
machines, if ever needed. They have more equipment and
facilities to do manufacturing than small manufacturers do. Special
process needed to manufacture a certain machine is done by
subcontracting to other machine shops.

☐ Large-Size Manufacturer – capable of mass producing agricultural
machines because they have almost complete line of equipment
needed in manufacturing. Small and medium manufacturers
sometimes request subcontracting job to large-size manufacturers.

☐ Manufacturers – are those that produce one or several types of
farm machinery and usually do not sell other items from other
manufacturers.
☐ Manufacturer-Dealers – manufactures their own line of items but
also sell either consigned items or several brands of single-cylinder
engines, pumps, pump set, and other types of farm machinery.
☐ Dealers – carry several items and brand from varying sources and
are not usually engaged in manufacture and fabrication.
Classification of agricultural machinery
manufacturing industry

Data. ASAE USA.

Printice-Hall, Inc. Englewood Cliffs, New Jersey. 120pp.
☐ Krutz, G. Thompson, L, and P. Claar. 1984. Design of

473pp

Engineering Journal.
