PSYCHROMETRY
Volume 6 –AGRICULTURAL AND FOOD PROCESS ENGINEERING
by
Engr. Alexis T. Belonio, MS
Agricultural and Biosystems Engineer
ASEAN Engineer
2024 AGRICULTURAL AND BIOSYSTEMS ENGINEERING
BOARD EXAM REVIEWER

Disclaimer
Photos, illustrations and schematic diagrams of equipment or machine parts shown in
the presentation are solely for educational purposes to facilitate comprehension of the
topics by the students. 	Showing them does not endorse a product nor imply criticism
of similar products not mentioned.

INTRODUCTION
☐ A knowledge on the terms used in psychrometry, which is
the study of the properties of the air, and use of the
psychrometric chart are essential for an understanding of the
processes involved in drying and storage of grains and other
agricultural crops, and in analyzing individual requirements for
a particular climatic condition.

PSYCHOMETRIC CHART
☐ The psychometric chart is a device that simplifies the
measurement of air properties and eliminates many time-
consuming and tedious calculations that would otherwise be
necessary.
☐ A psychometric chart is simply a graphic presentation of the
conditions or properties of air, such as dry and wet bulb
temperatures, dew point temperature, relative humidity, specific
volume, and humidity ratio.
☐ Knowing two parameters will able you to determine other
properties of the air for a given set of condition.
This is importance when dealing unit operations like drying,
cooling, humidification, dehumidification, and others.


Dry Bulb and Wet
Bulb thermometer
Sling Pyschrometer

Digital Thermohygrometer

PSYCHROMETRIC TERMS
☐ Dry-Bulb Temperature
Is the temperature of the air
as measured using an
ordinary thermometer, such
as a household thermometer.
The bulb is the sensitive
portion of the instrument. As
the temperature of the bulb
increases, the liquid in the
bulb expands and rises in the
stem.

☐ Wet-Bulb Temperature
Is the temperature of the air as
measured using an ordinary
thermometer in which the glass
bulb is covered with a wet cloth
or gauze. The clean cotton
wick absorbs water.
Evaporation of this water
reduces the temperature of the
wick, and the resultant
temperature is indicated by the
mercury in the thermometer
stem.
The airflow passing over the
wet cloth should have a
velocity of at least 15ft per
second.

☐ Dewpoint Temperature
Is the temperature at which
moisture condenses on the
surface. 	It is the
temperature at which
condensation occurs when
air is cooled at constant
humidity ratio and constant
atmospheric pressure.

☐ Relative Humidity
Is the ratio of the partial
pressure of water vapor in
the atmosphere to the
pressure that saturated
water vapor exerts at the
temperature of the air. The
relative velocity is expressed
as decimal or a percentage.
In agricultural process such
as grain drying, relative
humidity values between 0 to
100% are often encountered.

☐ Humidity Ratio
Is the weight of the water vapor
contained in the moist air per
unit weight of dry air. 	Other
terms used for humidity ratio
are absolute humidity and
specific humidity.
☐ Enthalpy
The enthalpy of a dry-air-water-
vapor mixture is the heat
content of the moist air per unit
weight of dry air above a certain
reference temperature.

☐ Specific Volume
The specific volume of
moist air is defined as the
volume per unit weight of
dry air. The specific density
of the moist air is equal to
the reciprocal of its specific
volume.

☐ Grains of Moisture
Is the unit of measurement
used to determine the
amount of moisture in the air;
7000 grains equal 1 lb (0.45
kg) of water. This can be
determined from any of the
following combinations: dry-
bulb temperature and
relative humidity (RH); dry-
bulb temperature and
dewpoint; wet-bulb
temperature and relative
humidity; wet-bulb
temperature and dewpoint;
dry-bulb and wet-bulb
temperatures; dewpoint
alone.

☐ If the dry-bulb and wet-bulb temperatures are known, the
relative humidity can be read from the chart.
☐ If the dry-bulb temperature and the relative humidity are known,
the wet-bulb temperature can be determined.
☐ If the wet-bulb temperature and the relative humidity are known,
the dry-bulb temperature can be found.
☐ If the wet-bulb and dry-bulb temperatures are known, the
dewpoint can be read from the chart.
☐ If the dry-bulb temperature and the relative humidity are known,
the dewpoint can be found.

IDENTIFICATION OF LINES AND
SCALES ON THE CHART
☐ The dry-bulb temperature scale extends along the sole from toe
to heel. The dry-bulb lines extend straight up from the sole, one
for each degree of temperature.
☐ The wet-bulb scale extends along the instep from the toe to the
top of the shoe. The wet-bulb lines extend diagonally downward
to the sole and the back of the shoe, one for each degree of
temperature.


☐ The condensation or dewpoint is the same as the wet-bulb scale.
However, the dewpoint lines extend horizontally to the back of
the shoe, one for each dewpoint temperature.
☐ The relative humidity lines are located along the side of the shoe
and follow approximately the same curve as the instep. 	The
instep line is actually the 100% relative humidity line.
☐ The grains of moisture scale follows along the back of the shoe
from the heel to the top. The lines are the same as the dewpoint
lines.
☐ The enthalpy line is the same with the wet-bulb line extending
outward. Unit for enthalpy is given either in BTU/lb or Kcal/kg of
dry air.
☐ All properties of air, at any given condition, can be represented
on a psychrometric chart by plotting a single point.

PSYCHROMETRIC PROCESSES
Heating	Cooling
Humidification
Dehumidification
Evaporative
Cooling
Tunnel ventilated
poultry and swine farm
Cold storage of
vegetables, e.g. onion,
coco sugar, etc
Drying of agricultural
crops
Poultry incubation and
hatcheries; Greenhouses, etc

Heating – Increasing air
temperature
Cooling – Decreasing
air temperature
Dehumidification – removing
moisture from air
Humidification – adding
moisture to the air

REFERENCES
☐ Brooker, et. al. Drying Cereal Grains. The AVI Publishing
Inc. 	Wesport, Connecticut.
☐ 	SEARCA. 	1981. 	Grain 	Post-Harvest 	Processing
Technology. 	Southeast 	Asia 	Cooperative 	Post-Harvest
Research 	and 	Development 	Programme. 	SEARCA. 	Los
Baños, Philippines. 281pp.

QUESTIONS AND PROBLEMS

1. A psychrometer measures the ____
of the air.
a. 	dry and wet bulb temperature
b. 	dry bulb temperature and relative
humidity
c. 	wet bulb temperature and relative
humidity
d. 	None of the above
2. Temperature of the air as measured
using ordinary thermometer.
a. Wet bulb temperature
b. Dry bulb temperature
c. Dewpoint temperature
d. None of the above
3. Temperature of the as measured
using ordinary thermometer whose
glass bulb is covered with wet cloth of
gauge.
a. Wet bulb temperature
b. Dry bulb temperature
c. Dewpoint temperature
d. None of the above
4. Temperature of the air at which
the moisture condenses on the
surface at which condensation
occurs at constant humidity ratio
and constant atmospheric
pressure.
a. Wet bulb temperature
b. Dry bulb temperature
c. Dewpoint temperature
d. None of the above
5. It is the ratio of the partial
pressure of water vapor in the
atmosphere to the pressure that
saturated water vapor exerts at
the temperature of the air.
a. Humidity ratio
b. Relative Humidity
c. Enthalpy
d. None of the above

6. Weight of water vapor
contained in the moist air per
unit weight of dry air.
a. Humidity ratio
b. Relative humidity
c. Enthalpy
d. None of the above
7. Heat content of the mist air
per unit weight of dry air above
a certain reference
temperature.
a. Humidity ratio
b. Relative humidity
c. Enthalpy
d. None of the above
8. The volume of the moist air
that is equal to the reciprocal to
the its density.
a. Specific volume
b. Specific density
c. Relative humidity
d. None of the above
9. The amount of moisture
in the air that equal to
number of particles per 1
pound of water.
a. Specific density
b. Specific volume
c. Grains of moisture
d. None of the above
10. Lines vertically upward
from the sole of the
psychrometric chart.
a. Dew point temperature
b. Wet bulb temperature
c. Dry bulb temperature
d. None of the above

11. What is the relative humidity of
the air if the psychrometer
measures 40°C for both the dry
bulb and the wet bulb
temperatures?
a. 	40%
b. 	80%
c. 	100%
d. 	All of the above
12. If the point is moved horizontally
to the left of the psychrometric
chart, the process is ____.
a. 	heating
b. 	cooling
c. 	drying
d. 	None of the above
13. Referring to the psychrometric
chart, the humidity ratio is ____
during heating process .
a. 	increasing
b. 	decreasing
c. 	constant
d. 	None of the above
14. In the psychrometric chart, the
relative humidity ____ during
heating process.
a. 	increases
b. 	decreases
c. 	is constant
d. 	None of the above
15. Still referring to the
psychrometric chart, the enthalpy
of air ____ during heating process.
a. 	increases
b. 	decreases
c. 	is constant
d. 	None of the above
16. Wet bulb thermometer
measures the temperature of the air
at a condition that the air is ____.
a. 	unsaturated
b. 	fully saturated
c. 	dry
d. 	None of the above

17. In the psychrometric chart, the
enthalpy of air is ____ during
adiabatic process.
a. 	increasing
b. 	decreasing
c. 	constant
d. 	None of the above
18. In the psychrometric chart, the
relative humidity of air is ____
during adiabatic process.
a. 	increasing
b. 	decreasing
c. 	constant
d. 	None of the above
19. In the psychrometric chart, the
dry bulb temperature of air is ____
during adiabatic process.
a. 	increasing
b. 	decreasing
c. 	constant
d. 	None of the above

INTRODUCTION
☐ Pump is generally a
handling device used for
elevating or moving liquids.
In agricultural and food
industry they are used to
handle liquids, such as
water, brine, liquid food
products, lubricating oil, and
many others.

CLASSIFICATION OF PUMPS
☐ Positive Displacement
(1) Piston or Plunger
(2) Rotary or pumps with rotating displacer

Piston or Plunger
☐ Characteristics
• 	Pulsating
• 	Periodic output
• 	Very good seal between displacer and cylinder wall
• 	Self-priming
• 	Suitable for very large head
• 	Sensitive to counter pressure
• 	Very high volumetric efficiency
• 	Low speed
• 	Expensive due to large-sized and complicated drive
• 	Long life
• 	Not suitable for liquids containing solid materials
• 	Easy and accurately controlled delivery rate
• 	At high viscosities, it is necessary to use special valves


Rotary or Pumps with Rotating
Displacer
☐ It is the most important group of pumps used for food. 	This
includes 	gear 	pumps 	with 	different 	rotor 	arrangement, 	rotary
vane pumps, worm pumps (kneading pumps), and pumps with
side-by-side rotors or rotors fitting inside each other.

Characteristics
• 	No valves is required
• 	Higher speed thus smaller and cheaper than piston pump
• 	Pulsates little and not at all
• 	Self-priming
• 	Seals between sides are not as good as that of piston pumps
• 	Volumetric efficiency is considerably high
• 	Delivery rate hardly diminishes with increasing counter pressure
• 	Applicable for large head and high delivery rates
• 	Applicable for high viscosity and fluids containing mixture of
liquids and solids

Momentum Pump
☐ This includes the centrifugal pumps which are used for large
and relatively low delivery, and the axial-flow pump which are
used for large delivery but low counter pressure. Propeller pumps
for liquids have limited application in food industry.

Types of Pumps
¡ Reciprocating or Piston-Type
Pump
The mechanical efficiency may be
as high as 80-90%. 	It is usually
adapted for high-pressure
operation.
¡ Rotary Pump
It is a positive displacement pump,
inexpensive and simple to
construct. 	Mechanical efficiency is
usually more than 90% under best
conditions.

¡ Gear Pump
It is well suited for many
processing operations
because of its positive
displacement action, provide
continuous smooth flow of
material, and are easy to
disassembled for cleaning.

¡ Vane Pump
It is characterized by sliding
vanes, cylindrical seals in
slots, and hinged lobes that
maintain a seal in the pump.

¡ Jet Pump
This type of pump
operates on the velocity
energy of the jet of the
fluid. Fluids are forced
through a jet or nozzle
where the energy
involved are converted
into velocity energy.


¡ Air-Lift Pump
In this type of pump, air
is delivered at the bottom
of the lift pipe and mixes
with the liquid. The air-
liquid mixture, having
less specific weight, rises
in the pipe and is
discharged at a point
above the level of the
liquid.

¡ Centrifugal Pump
It is widely used for
pumping water, milk,
lubricants, chemical
solutions, materials being
processed, and others. It
is simple and has
mechanical efficiency as
high as 90% under
favorable conditions.

¡ Peristaltic Pump
It is a positive
displacement type of
pump and is important in
food industry. 	The
advantage is that the
product only comes in
contact with the material
of the flexible tubing.

¡ Extruder Pump
It is a liquid-handling
equipment used in food
industry. It is used for the
extrusion of plastic materials
like butter, dough, chocolate,
etc. in the form of sheet,
rods, or other shapes. 	This
machine also resembles a
displacement pump except
that it has a spiral-shaped
connection between inlet and
outlet causing it to operate
on a dragging effect.

Head Loss
☐ The head loss is the resistance of flow against which the
pump must work, usually expressed in terms of head.
Basically, head is the pressure equivalent exerted by a
column of any open liquid.
Head, in feet, is determined by the equation:
Head, ft = psi x 144/ω
where:
ω 	= weight, in lb/cu. ft. of any substance


PUMP HORSEPOWER
Fluid Power – is the power required to lift and move liquid from
one location to another location in a system.
FHP = Q H Y / 33,000 ft-lb/min-hp
where:
FHP 	- fluid power, hp
Q 	- mass flow rate, lb/min
H 	- total head loss, ft
Y 	- specific gravity of fluid
Horsepower can be converted into other system as follows:
1 hp 	= 550 ft-lbs/sec
= 76.2 kgf-m/sec
= 746 watts

A coconut oil is to be pumped at a rate of 100 kg per
minute to a tank at 6meters high from a container 1 m
above the pump. The estimated dynamic head loss in
the system is 0.2 m of water. What is the horsepower
required in pumping the oil? Assume a specific weight
of oil of 0.93 kg/l. Also, compute for the brake
horsepower and motor horsepower, if the efficiencies
for pump, transmission, and motor are 60%, 80%, and
90%, respectively.
Given:
Q 	- 100 kg/min
Hsd 	- 6 m
Hss 	- 1 m
Hd 	- 0.2 m
Y 	- 0.93 kg/l
Required: Fluid Horsepower

Solution:
FHP 	= Q H Y / 33,000 ft-lb/min
Q 	= 100 kg/min
= 220 lb/min
H 	= (6 m + 1 m + 0.2 m) x 3.28 ft/m
= 23.6 ft
FHP 	= 220 lb/min x 23.616 ft / 33,000 ft-lb/min-hp
= 0.158 hp
BHP 	= FHP / Ep
= 0.158 hp / 0.6
= 0.263 hp
MHP 	= BHP / (Em x Et)
= 0.263 hp / (0.9 x 0.8)
= 0.36 hp
Therefore, use ½hp pump

CENTRIFUGAL PUMP LAWS
The performance of pumps are similar with that of the
blowers which conforms with certain mathematical laws.
These laws may be used to extend the performance data of a
specific pump to a geometrically similar pump of different size
or operating at different speed.
Note that these laws only apply to the pump and not to the
system to which they are attached as well as to the specific
point on the performance curve.

For specific pump with speed varying:
(a) The capacity varies directly with the speed.
N1 	Q1
------- 	= 	------
N2 	Q2
(b) The pressure head, total static head, or velocity varies as to the
square of the speed.
N12 H1
------ 	= 	------
N22 H2
(c) The power required varies as the cube of the speed.
N13 HP1
------- 	= 	-------
N23 HP2

A centrifugal pump that is used in pumping water to a tank operates at a
rate of 1gpm. The pump is driven directly by an electric motor with an
input power of 1.5hp running at a speed of 1700 rpm. The total head
loss of the system is 10m. If the motor drives the pump at 2200 rpm,
what is the rate of flow of the pump? What is the change in the total
head delivered by the pump? What would be the increase in the input
power of the pump?
Given:
Q1 	- 1 gpm
Hp1 	- 1.5hp
N1 	- 1700 rpm
H1 	- 10 m
N2 	- 2200 rpm
Required: 	Q2, Hp2, and H2

Solution:
N1/N2 	= Q1/Q2
Q2 	= N2Q1/N1
= 2200 rpm ( 1gpm)/1700 rpm
= 1.294 gpm
N12/N22 = H1/H2
H2 	= H1 (N22) / N12
= 10 m (2200 rpm)2 / (1700 rpm)2
= 16.75 m
N13/N23 = HP1/HP2
HP2 	= HP1 (N23) / N13
= 1.5hp (2200 rpm)3 / (1700 rpm)3
= 3.25hp

For a number of geometrically similar pumps with speed constant and
diameter varying:
(a) The capacity varies as the cube of the diameter
D13 Q1
------ 	= 	------
D23 Q2
(b) The head varies as the square of the diameter
D12 H1
------ 	= 	-------
D22 H2
(c) The power varies as the fifth power of the diameter
D15 HP1
------- 	= 	--------
D25 HP2
where: 	N 	- speed of the pump, rpm
H 	- head of the pump, ft
Q 	- volumetric flow rate of the pump, cfm
D 	- impeller diameter, in
HP 	- brake power of the pump, hp

System Characteristics Curve
☐ The system characteristics curve of a pump is a graph showing
the total head plotted against the capacity or rate of flow of pump
through the system. 	When a pump is coupled to a system, the rate
of flow depends upon the characteristics of the system and the
characteristics of the pump.


VISCOSITY
Fluids that are pumped in processing operation are frequently
more viscous as compared with water. Examples of these fluids
are milk, cream, oil, sugar solution, molasses, and many others.
Some important observations that help in solving problems
involving viscous fluids are:
(1) 	The efficiency of pump decreases as the viscosity increases;
and
(2) 	The working head increases as the viscosity increases.

Multi-staging
☐ The velocity, amount of lift, and static head may be increased by
using two or more single-unit or single-stage pump in series. This
can be done by connecting the discharge end of one pump to the
intake of the second pump. However, this only holds true only if the
capacity of both pumps are the same.
☐ Usually, multi-stage pumps are designed with the impellers on the
same shaft and with the straightening vanes between each impeller.


References
☐ Gunther, R. C. 1969. Refrigeration, Air conditioning, and Cold
Storage. Principles and Applications. Chilton Book Company.
Radnor, Pennsylvania. 1398pp.
☐ Henderson, S. M. 1976. Agricultural Process Engineering. Third
Edition. The AVI Publishing Company, Inc. Westport Connecticut.
442pp.
☐ Leniger, H. A. and W. A. Beverloo. 1975. Food Process
Engineering. D. Reidel Publishing Company. Dordrecht, Holland.
552pp.

QUESTIONS AND PROBLEMS

1. Device used to lift or to
transfer liquid from one source to
another.
a. 	Pump
b. 	Wind turbine
c. 	Electric motor
d. 	None of the above
2. Which of the following can be
used as a power drive for
pumps?
a. Electric motor, human and/or
animal
b. Gasoline or diesel engine
c. 	Solar and wind
d. 	All of the above
3. Type of pump that uses the
back-and-forth motion of
mechanical parts, such as piston
or diaphragms, to pressurize the
fluid.
a. 	Centrifugal
b. 	Reciprocating
c. 	Axial
d. 	None of the above
4. Type of pump that uses the
centrifugal force imparted to the fluid
by one or more rotating elements
called impellers to increase the kinetic
energy and the pressure energy of the
fluid.
a. 	Centrifugal
b. 	Reciprocating
c. 	Axial
d. 	None of the above
5. Type of pump that develops most of
the suction and of the discharge head
by propelling or by the lifting action of
the impeller vanes in the water.
a. 	Centrifugal
b. 	Mixed-flow
c. 	Axial-flow
d. 	None of the above

6. Type of pump that uses gears,
vanes, lobe or screw to trap and
to convey the fluid from the inlet
to the outlet of the pump.
a. 	Centrifugal
b. 	Reciprocating
c. 	Rotary
d. 	None of the above
7. Type of pump with impellers
rotating inside a closed casing
which draws water into the pump
through a central inlet opening
and forces water out through a
discharge outlet at the periphery
of the housing by centrifugal
force.
a. Diffuser pump
b. 	Centrifugal pump
c. 	Volute pump
d. 	None of the above
8. Type of centrifugal pump in
which its impeller is surrounded by
a set of vanes.
a. Diffuser pump
b. 	Centrifugal pump
c. 	Volute pump
d. 	None of the above
9. Diffuser vanes have ____ near
the impeller and are gradually
enlarged toward their outer
diameter where the fluid flows into
the chamber and around the pump
discharge.
a. 	big openings
b. 	medium-size openings
c. 	small openings
d. 	None of the above
10. Type of a centrifugal pump with
spiral-curve casing.
a. Diffuser pump
b. Volute pump
c. Self-priming pump
d. None of the above

11. Casing of the volute pump is
proportioned to gradually reduce
the ____ as it flows from the
impeller to the discharge, thus
discharging velocity heat to the
pressure head.
a. velocity of water
b. pressure of water
c. volume of water
d. None of the above
12. Type of impeller for
centrifugal pumps.
a. Open
b. 	Semi-open or Semi-enclosed
c. 	Enclosed
d. 	All of the above
13. Type of suction inlet for
centrifugal pumps.
a. 	Single action
b. 	Double action
c. 	All of the above
d. 	None of the above
14. Type of suction inlet for which
its impeller has suction cavity on
both sides.
a. 	Single-action
b. 	Double-action
c. 	Any of the above
d. 	None of the above
15. Axis of rotation of centrifugal
pumps that has a vertical impeller
mounted on a horizontal shaft.
a. 	Horizontal axis
b. 	Vertical axis
c. 	Any of a & b
d. 	None of the above

16. Centrifugal pump that
develops vacuum enough for the
atmospheric pressure to force
the liquid through the suction
pipe into the pump casing without
initially feeding the pump to
create suction.
a. Pressure pump
b. Self-priming pump
c. Mixed-flow pump
d. None of the above
17. Amount of discharge of a
pump at maximum efficiency.
a. 	Head
b. 	Cavitation
c. 	Capacity
d. 	None of the above
18. Formation of cavities filled with
water vapor due to local pressure
drop which collapses as soon as the
vapor bubbles reach high pressure
region.
a. Bubbling
b. Cavitation
c. Water hammer
d. None of the above
19. Amount of energy required to lift
and to move fluid from any arbitrary
datum.
a. 	Head
b. 	Friction head
c. 	Static suction head
d. 	None of the above
20. Volume of fluid pumped per unit
time.
a. 	Capacity
b. 	Discharge
c. 	Static discharge head
d. 	None of the above

INTRODUCTION
☐ Fans and blowers are used in
agricultural and food processing in
connection with drying, ventilating,
heating, cooling, refrigerating, aspirating,
elevating, conveying, etc..
☐ Currently, processing of agricultural
and food products inevitably requires the
use of fans and blowers.
☐ Since costs are becoming more and
more important in designing equipment
and establishing processing plants, it is
necessary that ABE be able to design,
select, and apply the best air moving
device that would give the right size,
serviceability, and economic for the given
conditions in consideration. Blower
Fan

GRAIN DRYING PLANT

DUST CONTROL SYSTEMS IN PROCESSING PLANTS

TUNNEL VENTILATED POULTRY FARM

Food Processing Plants

GENERAL CLASSIFICATIONS
☐ Blower
• 	Operate at pressures equal to or more than 1 lb/in2 (27.7 in. of
water). 	Machines 	in 	this 	class 	also 	include 	centrifugal
compressors and turbo compressors.
☐ Fans
• 	Operate 	at 	pressures 	of 	less 	than 	1 	lb/in2 (27.7 	in. 	of 	water).
Machines 	in 	this 	class 	are 	also 	called 	fans, 	sometimes
exhauster for ventilation purposes


CLASSIFICATIONS OF FANS AND
BLOWERS ACCORDING TO DESIGN
1. 	Axial-Flow or Propeller
Fan
Air flow is parallel to the shaft or to
the axis. Propeller fan is a generic
term. Technically, axial and
propeller fans are the same based
on past experience and general
usage. However, have segregated
the duties of which each fan is used.

☐ Propeller Fan
Used to handle large
volumes of air against free
delivery or low heads. 	This
may have two or more blades
which maybe of sheet or
airfoil shape. The blades
may either be narrow or wide.
Likewise, they may have
uniform or varied pitch.

☐ Axial-Flow Fan
This is similar to desk fan
but is more defined. 	The
hubs have been enlarged.
The blade is warped for
better efficiency and the
blades have a close radial
clearance with the housing.
As a result, it operates
against higher pressure and
has a better efficiency.

☐ Tube-Axial Fan
Consists of an axial-flow wheel
within a cylinder and includes
driving mechanism supports
either for the belt drive or for
direct connection.


☐ Vane-Axial Fan
Consists of an axial-flow
wheel within a cylinder, a set
of guide vanes located
either before or after the
wheel, and a driving-
mechanism support for
either belt drive or direct
connection.

2. 	Centrifugal Blowers
Consists of wheel or rotor within a scroll spiral-type housing.
The air enters parallel to the shaft, makes a 90 degrees turn
in the fan wheel, and is discharged from the wheel (and
housing) in a radial manner.


☐ Forward Curved
A low-speed fan capable of
operating at several inches
pressure under most
conditions but is limited to
handling clean air. It has a
squirrel-cage rotor and a
large number of blades.
Commonly seen and use in
air conditioning or cooling
systems. Noise emanating
from the blower is less as
compared with the other
blowers.

☐ Backward Curved
Has about 12 blades
essentially flat and tilted
backward from the direction of
wheel rotation. It is inherently
a high-speed type of fan with
self-limiting horsepower
characteristics. It is the most
efficient type of centrifugal
fans and more expensive than
the other types.

☐ Radial-Tip
It has a smaller number of blades
from 6 to 20, and the blades are
essentially in a plane radiating from
the shaft. The blades normally
about 2 to 3 times as long radially
as they are wide. 	This type of fan is
usually has a larger housing than
the other types and is more
expensive; however, its price is
justified by its ability to handle dirty
air and to convey materials that go
through the fan, or to develop
pressures beyond the range
permissible with lighter weight fans.

☐ Cross-Flow Blower
It has a uniform discharge flow throughout its axial length and high
air rate when referred to wheel periphery speed. It is mainly a high-
volume, low-pressure fan. Examples are bakery ovens, unit
heaters, baseboard heaters, air curtains, drying equipment, kitchen
hoods, etc. Also used in grain cleaning purposes.

CHARACTERISTICS OF AIR-MOVING DEVICE
WHEN DIAMETER OF IMPELLER
IS INCREASED
Air Moving Device 	Airflow 	Pressure Head
Fan 	Increase 	Decrease
Blower 	Decrease 	Increase

WHEN WIDTH OF IMPELLER IS INCREASED
Air Moving Device 	Airflow 	Pressure Head
Fan 	Decrease 	Increase
Blower 	Increase 	Decrease

BLOWER
Noise Level 	Pressure 	Airflow
Backward 	High 	High 	Low
Radial 	Medium 	Medium 	Medium
Forward 	Low 	Low 	High

FAN THEORY
☐ The propeller fan is essentially an air screw. The twist or angularity
of the blades is called “pitch,” which is theoretically 	the distance the
air would be moved when turning the rotor 1 revolution.
P = 2 π r tan A
where:
P 	- pitch of of blade, cm
r 	- radius of blade, cm
A 	- angle of fan blade twist, deg

Given:
Diameter 	- 12 in.
Speed 	- 1800 rpm
Static efficiency - 40%
Required: 	Fan Flow Rate
Solution:
Pitch 	= 2 π ( 6.in) Tan 10 deg
= 6.6 in.
Q 	= 6.6 in per rev x 3.1416 (12 in)2 /4 x 1800 rpm x 40%
= 313.35 cfm
A 12in.-diameter fan rotates at 1800rpm
speed. The fan blade has 10-degree pitch
angle. What is the fan pitch and flow rate if it
has 40% static efficiency?

☐ The pitch increases as the radius for a fan with a constant
blade twists or angularity. Consequently, the air near the tip of
the fan is moved at a faster rate than the air nearer the axis, the
speed being theoretically proportional to the distance from the
axis. Therefore, when the fan is operating against a material
static head, air is forced back through the fan near the hub and
recirculation or turbulence occurs and lowers the efficiency.
☐ Recirculation can be reduced or eliminated by warping the
blades so that the pitch is constant. The warp design can be
determined from the equation by holding P constant and
determining A for variation in r. A large streamlined hub
improved performance by eliminating the region or
recirculation. A cylindrical housing improves performance by
guiding the stream of air that passes through the fan.

☐ The performance and efficiency of the axial-flow fan can be
further improved by the addition of straightening vanes behind the
rotor. The discharge from a “propeller” fan is in the form of a
spiral, the rotation being in the same direction as the rotation of
the fan wheel. 	Straightening vanes catch the air, turn it so its flow
parallel to the shaft. 	Elimination of turbulence reduces noise and
improves efficiency of the fan. Straightening vanes should be 2 to
4 inches from the blade wheel to minimize noise.
☐ Pressures in excess of 60 inches have been developed by
single axial-flow fan with a total efficiency of more than 85%.


Fan Selection
Factors to consider in fan selection:
• 	Quantity of air to be moved per
unit of time.
• 	Estimated system resistance and
expected variations.
• 	Amount of noise permitted.
• 	Space available for fan.
• 	Economic implications.

Design Procedure
1. 	Calculate the specific speed (Ns) of the air moving unit at
specified static pressure (Ps)
Ns 	= N Q 0.5 / Ps 0.75
where:
Ns - specific speed of the air moving unit, dmls
N 	- rpm of the air moving unit
Q 	- airflow, cfm
Ps 	- pressure requirement, in. water
2. Determine the type of air-moving unit which operates at higher
efficiency or at near peak efficiency for the calculated specific
speed. If there are more than one type of air-moving unit to be
selected, base the selection on the relative cost of the unit, size
and shape of space available, and the characteristics of the airflow
path.

Given: 	Speed 	- 800 rpm
Rate of flow 	- 100 ft3
Required: 	Specific Speed of the Fan
Solution:
Ns 	= N x Q 0.5 / Ps 0.75
= (800 rpm)(100 cfm)0.5 / (1 in.H2O)0.75
= 800 x 10 x 1
= 8,000

Sample Casing Dimension

9. Fans perform in the same general manner as centrifugal
pumps. Consequently, the following hold true for any fan. To
compute for the air hp of the air-moving device, the formula is
AHP 	= q v H / 33,000

☐ The quantity of air to be moved per unit of time will be

☐ Noise is a factor in processing which is not as important as in air

☐ 	The 	static 	pressure 	drop 	or 	resistance 	head 	can 	be 	determined

power.
☐ The energy pressure indicates the energy needed to accelerate the

In most instances, the velocity energy is lost at discharge in which case
the power required must be based upon the total pressure head.

☐ 	Fan 	performance 	data 	are 	usually 	presented 	by 	the
manufacturer in tabular form. 	The data represent only the practical

needed to select a fan for a specific job.

SIZE REDUCTION
Volume 6 –AGRICULTURAL AND FOOD PROCESS ENGINEERING
by
Engr. Alexis T. Belonio, MS
Agricultural and Biosystems Engineer
ASEAN Engineer
2024 AGRICULTURAL AND BIOSYSTEMS ENGINEERING
BOARD EXAM REVIEWER

Disclaimer
Photos, illustrations and schematic diagrams of equipment or machine parts shown in
the presentation are solely for educational purposes to facilitate comprehension of the
topics by the students. 	Showing them does not endorse a product nor imply criticism
of similar products not mentioned.

INTRODUCTION
☐ Size reduction usually refers to
cutting, chopping, crushing,
grinding, and milling of solid mass.
☐ The size reduction in the size of
the product is brought about by
mechanical means without a
change in chemical properties of
the material and in uniformity in
size and shape of the individual
grain and units of the product is
usually what is desired.

☐ In case of liquids and semi-solids
which are common in food processing
operation size reduction operation
includes mashing, atomizing,
homogenizing, etc
Applications of Size Reductions
Operation
1. Milling of cereal grains
2. Fine grinding or refining of sugars and
chocolates
3. Flaking of soybeans prior to solvent extraction
4. Cutting of vegetables (cubes, strips, slices)
5. Homogenization of milk and cream
6. Decortication of coconut husk for production of
fiber
7. Shredding of straws and grasses as source of
feed

Objectives of Size Reduction
1. 	Facilitate separation of different parts of materials like in rice
and feed milling;
2. 	Obtaining a desirable product texture (whitening of rice,
refining chocolates, meat grinding, etc);
3. 	Facilitating mixing and dispersion (milling and crushing
ingredients for dry mixing of feeds, homogenization of liquids
and others);
4. 	Accelerating heat and mass transfer on the products in
preparation for other operations like extraction, atomization of
powder in spray dryer;
5. 	Portion control (slicing cold-cuts for meat and fish, breads,
cakes, etc); and
6. 	Obtaining pieces and particles of define shapes (cubing meat
for stew, cutting pineapple and other fruits, cutting dough to
make cookies, etc.)

Examples of Size-Reduction
Processes
• 	Cutting of fruits and
vegetables for canning
• 	Shredding of sweet
potato for drying
• 	Chopping corn fodder
• 	Grinding limestone for
fertilizer
• 	Grinding grains for
livestock feed
• 	Milling flour
• 	Etc.

SIZE CHARACTERISTICS
☐ Machine performance in
reducing the size of material is
characterized by the following:
• 	Capacity
• 	Power required per unit of
material reduced
• 	Size and shape of the
product before and after
reduction
• 	Range of size and shape of
the resulted product

MILLING
☐ This is the trade term used relative to the reduction of grain into
meal or flour.
☐ The milling process includes:
• 	Size reduction – mechanical process converting large
particle to small particles.
• 	Hulling – removal of husk or cover from the product.
• 	Scarifying – removal of dirt or unwanted material at the
surface of the product.
• 	Polishing – making the surface smooth like in rice milling.
• 	Sorting – separation of various sizes of the milled product.
• 	Mixing – is combining various size of products to produce
the required mixture in the final product.

CLASSIFICATIONS OF REDUCED
MATERIALS
Class 	Size
Dimension Range 	Size 1/8 in or more
Sieve Range 	0.125 to 0.0029 in
Microscopic Range 	less than 0.0029

SIEVES
☐ These are the simplest
method of classifying
granular materials by
passing them into
series of Tyler sieves.

Tyler Standard Screen Sieve
Mesh No. Openings,
in.

FINENESS MODULUS
☐ This indicates the uniformity of grind in the resultant product.
☐ It is the sum of the weight fractions retained above each sieve
divided by 100.
☐ Sieve used are: 3/8-, 4-, 8-, 14-, 28, 48-, and 100-in. mesh.
☐ Standard samples is 250 grams oven dried to constant weight
to 100°C and shaken to Ro-Tap for 5 minutes.

using a hammer mill:

Opening

Example

PARTICLE SIZE
D 	= 0.0041 (2)FM
where:
D 	- average grain size, inches
FM 	- fineness modulus, dmls
Using the data above, the particle diameter D = 0.0041 (2)2.57
is 	0.024 inch.
☐ Particle Size – commonly used is the particle having equivalent
dimeter in question.
☐ Particle Size Distribution – refers to the proportion of particles
within a certain range in a population of particles. It importance is on
the quality of food and processing.
☐ Particle Shape – form of particle which has importance in bulk
density and flowability of material.

Size-Reduction Procedure
☐ Cutting – is a separation or
reduction which is produced by
pushing or forcing a thin, sharp
knife through the materials to be
reduced.
☐ Crushing – is the reduction by
applying a force to the unit to be
reduced in excess of its strength.
☐ Shearing – is the combination
of cutting and crushing. 	This can
be done either singly or in
combination. Shear cutter is an
example of producing sheared
products.

CUTTING
☐ Minimum deformation and
rupture of the reduced particles.
☐ New surfaces produced by
this sharp knife are relatively
undamaged.
☐ Well adopted to fruits, meat,
and vegetables.
☐ Knife of extreme sharpness
and as thin as possible is the
most satisfactory cutting
device.
☐ Knife with edge that has
sawing component provides a
smoother cut with probably less
energy.

CUTTER MILL
☐ It is best for reducing the size of fibrous materials like
forages, straws, and weeds.
☐ Usually cutter produces a more uniform product as
compared to crushing.


CRUSHING
☐ Characteristics of the new surfaces are irregular in size and in
shape.
☐ The characteristics of the new surfaces and particles are
dependent upon the type of material and the method of force
application.
☐ Crushing by means of rigid roll or bed is an example of static
force application.
☐ Hitting the product with hammer is an example of dynamic
force application.
☐ Crushing usually have a product that have no regular form.


SHEARING
☐ It is usually used for reducing materials of tough fibrous
nature where some crushing may be advantageous and the
resulting units are of large but uniform sizes.
☐ For best performance, the clearance between the bar and
the knife should be as small as possible and the knife as sharp
and thin as possible.


Grain Milling Devices
☐ Hammer Mill – reduction caused by
impact
• 	Fixed Hammer
• 	Swinging Hammer
☐ Attrition Mill or Burr Mill or Plate
Mill – reduction caused by twisting
pressure
☐ Crushers – reduction cause by
simple normal pressure
• 	Jaw
• 	Gyratory
• 	Roller mill

HAMMER MILL
☐ It consists essentially of a rotating
beater and a heavy perforated screen.
☐ Sometimes called as impact mills
where crushing elements are hammers
fitted on a high-speed rotor inside a
cylindrical chamber.
☐ The material is introduced into the
housing and the beater that rotates
1500 to 4000 rpm beats and pounds
the material until it is small enough to
pass through the screen.
☐ The fineness of the material is
controlled mainly by the size of holes of
the screen.

☐ Hammers are rigidly fixed to
the shaft or swing.
☐ Swinging hammers are used
when necessary to reduce the
risk of damage in the case of
encounter between the
hammer and large hard chunk
material inside the chamber.
☐ The striking edge of the
hammer is designed in many
great ways.
☐ The swinging hammer is
usually reversible.

Advantages of Hammer Mill
☐ Simplicity
☐ Versatility
☐ Freedom from significant
damage due to foreign objects
☐ Freedom from damage
when operating empty
☐ Hammer wear does not
materially reduce its efficiency

Disadvantages of Hammer Mill
☐ Inability to produce
uniform grind. Maximum
size is controlled by the
size of the perforated holes.
☐ High power requirement
– heavy to rotate the
hammer at the start
requiring a higher input
current at the drive motor.

ATTRITION, BURR, OR PLATE MILL
☐ It consists essentially of two
roughened plates, one stationary and
other rotating.
☐ The material is fed between the
plates and is reduced by crushing and
shearing.
☐ Example is the stone mill and the
familiar household coffee grinder. The
material is ground between wo
corrugated surfaces moving with
respect to each other.
☐ Over feeding reduces the
effectiveness of the grinder and
excessive heating results.
☐ Operating speed is usually less
than 1200 rpm.

☐ The fineness of reduction is
controlled by the type of plates
and by the spacing.
☐ It is heavy–duty precision
used for preparation of feed
and food.
☐ Each burr rotates and is
driven independently, speed is
much higher, and design and
construction are more precise.

Advantages of Burr Mill
☐ Low initial cost
☐ Product may be relatively
uniform
☐ Power requirement is very
low. Slow moving compared to
hammer mill.

Disadvantages of Burr Mill
☐ Foreign objects may cause
breakage. Plates are provided
with limited space clearance.
☐ Operating empty may cause
excessive burr wear. Plate
may tend to contact without
load.
☐ Worn burrs yield poor
results.

CRUSHERS
☐ It reduce the material by pressing or
squeezing it until the material breaks.
☐ Sometimes called as pressure mill
where material is compressed between a
pair of counter-rotating heavy rollers with
hardened surfaces to the point of fracture.
☐ The rollers maybe smooth or corrugated.
☐ Crushers includes the following:
• 	Jaw crusher – cheaper and slower used
for smaller operation.
• 	Gyratory crusher – cone in shape,
smoother operation, and capacity is higher
• 	Roll crusher – used for primary
reduction of material following attrition or
hammer mill.

Jaw Crusher 	Gyratory Crusher
Roller Crusher


Milling of Rice Bran and Hulls for Feed Material

PERFORMANCE CHARACTERISTICS
Performance parameters needed during milling of products:
☐ Uniform product as to size – as much as possible particle
must have almost the same in sizes.
☐ Minimum temperature size during reduction –rise in
temperature of the particles should be minimal
☐ Minimum power requirement – as much as possible power
required to operate the machine must be low.
☐ Trouble free operation – minimal maintenance and repair if
possible

PRODUCT SIZE
Hammer Mill 	Vary the size of screen opening
Burr Mill 	Vary spring pressure on the burrs
Roller Mill 	Vary opening between roll
Cutter Mill 	Vary the rate of feed of material with respect to the
cutter rpm

UNIFORMITY OF THE PRODUCT
☐ Attrition mill does not
significantly produce a
more uniform product than
hammer mill. The
clearance between plates
dictates the size of particles
and once smaller particles
are produced during the
process, they will just pass
freely through the
clearance between plates.

POWER REQUIREMENT
☐ Affected by the type of materials,
moisture content, fineness of
grinding, rate of feeding, type
and condition of mill, etc.
☐ Fibrous materials require more
power than crystalline materials.
☐ Moist grains are difficult to grind
than dried grains.
☐ The power required to operate
empty increases swiftly as the
speed of the mill increases.
☐ Capacity of hammer mill is
limited by the power available.

(KW-HR/TON)

TEMPERATURE RISE
☐ The energy for grinding dissipates as
heat energy raises the temperature of the
ground product, the mill, and the ambient
air.
☐ Some heat are lost in vaporizing
moisture.
☐ Temperature may rise higher when
grinding fibrous materials, particularly
when producing fine materials.
☐ Hammer mill produces a cooler product
because it uses air in conveying the
materials.
☐ High temperature contributes to
decomposition of ground materials,
especially if the moisture content is high.

☐ Henderson, S. M, and R. L. Perry. 1976. Agricultural Process

QUESTIONS AND PROBLEMS

1. 	Process of making too-large-
to-be-used solid materials
usable.
a. Size reduction
b. 	Grinding

d. All of the above
2. Size-reduction processes
include ____.

d. 	All of the above

processed primarily using a
size-reduction equipment to
____.
a. 	increase the surface area of
contact of the material to
facilitate taking place of reaction
b. 	make it palatable when used
as feed for animals
c. 	facilitate conveyance operation
at the feed mill
d. All of the above
4. Physical mechanism used in
size-reduction process.
a. 	Compression
b. 	Impact
c. 	Attrition
d. Cutting
f. 	All of the above
5. 	Which of the following
statements is true in relation to
size-reduction operation?
a. 	Size reduction is the most
inefficient unit operation in terms of
energy use.
b. 	Size reduction is the most
efficient unit operation in terms of
energy use.
c. 	Size reduction is neither efficient
nor inefficient unit operation in
terms of energy use
d. 	None of the above

6. Which of the following
statements is true in relation to
reducing particle size of a material?
a. Reduction of materials to very
fine sizes is more costly in terms of
energy as compared with reduction
to relatively coarse particles.
b. Reduction of materials to very
fine sizes is much cheaper in terms
of energy as compared with
reduction to relatively coarse
particles.
c. Reduction of materials to very
fine sizes has the same cost as with
reduction to relatively coarse
particles.
d. None of the above
7. 	Which of the following is an
example of size-reduction
processes?
a. 	Chopping corn fodder
b. 	Slicing of sweet potato
c. 	Milling of cassava into flour
d. 	All of the above
8. Trade term used relative to the
reduction of grains into meal or
flour.
a. 	Shredding
b. 	Crushing
c. 	Milling
d. 	None of the above
9. Vertical-axis hammer mill is more
advantageous to use than
horizontal-axis for the reason that:
a. 	It is more effective in grinding
grains with higher moisture content
of up to 25%.
b. 	The power requirement of the
vertical-axis hammer mill is much
lower than that of the horizontal-
axis hammer mill.
c. Less broken grains can be
derived from vertical-axis.
d. None of the above

10. Size-reduction machines are
characterized based on ____.
a. capacity
b. power required unit material reduce
c. size and shape of the product after
reduction
d. range of size and shape of resulted
product
e. All of the above
11. Process of reducing the size of
materials by applying force to the
product in excess of its strength.
a. Shearing
b. Crushing
c. Milling
d. None of the above
12. Process of reducing the size of
materials by pushing or forcing a thin
sharp knife into it.
a. Shearing
b. Crushing
c. Cutting
d. All of the above
13. Process of reducing the size of
materials by cutting and crushing
actions.
a. Milling
b. Grinding
c. Shearing
d. None of the above
14. Power requirement in reducing the
size of grains is ____ for moist grains
than for dried grains.
a. 	lesser
b. 	the same
c. 	higher
d. 	None of the above
15. Indicator of the uniformity of
ground materials in the resultant
product.

text:
PARTICLE SEPARATION
Volume 6 –AGRICULTURAL AND FOOD PROCESS ENGINEERING
by
Engr. Alexis T. Belonio, MS
Agricultural and Biosystems Engineer
ASEAN Engineer
2024 AGRICULTURAL AND BIOSYSTEMS ENGINEERING
BOARD EXAM REVIEWER

Disclaimer
Photos, illustrations and schematic diagrams of equipment or machine parts shown in
the presentation are solely for educational purposes to facilitate comprehension of the
topics by the students. 	Showing them does not endorse a product nor imply criticism
of similar products not mentioned.

INTRODUCTION
☐ Grains and other crops when processed undergo various
particle separation activities to obtain the desired product.
☐ In agricultural processing this may include separation of
impurities, husks, bran layers, and various fractions from the
grains or cereals.
☐ In the case of separating liquid from solid which is common in
food processing, particle separation is basically done on the
process of filtration combined with scrubbings.
☐ Filtration as define as the operation by which solid particles
are separated from liquid or gas by forcing mixture through a
porous medium that retains the particles.

APPLICATIONS
☐ Cleaning - Is the process of
removing contaminants or foreign
matters from the materials like in grain
processing.
☐ Grading - is the process of
separating cleaned products into
various quality fractions that may be
defined based on the size, shape,
texture, colors and other factors.
☐ Sorting – is the process of
separating the product according to
size.
☐ Filtering – is the process of
separating solids particles to liquid or
gas.

PRINCIPLES AND MACHINES IN
SEPARATION OF PARTICLES
☐ Size
☐ Width and Thickness
☐ Length
☐ Weight
☐ Surface Texture
☐ Affinity for Liquids
☐ Color
☐ Electrical Conductivity
☐ Shape

SIZE
☐ Size is the most common difference between grains and
undesirable materials. In separating grains and foreign matters
according to size, a size separation air-screen machine with
perforated-sheet metal or woven-wire screen is used. An air-
blast separation is also incorporated in the air- screen machine
to remove light materials from the grain mixture. In the typical
air-screen machine, the grain mixture drops through an air blast
onto several screens and then through a second or even third
air blast where remaining light materials are removed.

WIDTH AND THICKNESS
☐ 	Width and thickness are special size
dimension used in operations for sizing
varieties of grains, weed seeds, and
impurities.
☐ Thickness separation is accomplished
through a cylindrical or flat screen which
has slotted perforations in the bottom of
recessed grooved. The shoulders of the
groove turn the seeds on edge before they
reach the slotted perforation. Thinner
grains fall through while thick grains are
subjected and go out a separate discharge
spout.

☐ Width separation is accomplished in a round hole perforations
at the bottom of indent or cup like depression in cylindrical or flat
screens. The shoulders of the indent tilt the grains on the end
and present the width dimension to the perforation. If the grain
is narrow, it drops through the perforation. If it is wider the
perforation, however, it is rejected.

LENGTH
☐ Length difference is common among the grain crops and
weed seeds. The differences in length are used in upgrading
and improving the quality of the product. In separating grains
according to length, an indented cylinder and a disc separator
are used.


☐ The indented cylinder separator consists of long round cylinder
in which the inner surface has many indented pockets or cup of
precise size. 	Inside the cylinder are other parts that help the
separation, including a lifting through to catch the grains. 	Grains
are fed into the cylinder as it rotates. Long seeds do not fit
completely into the indent so they do not remain in the indent long
enough to be lifted as the cylinder rotates. 	Shorter seeds that fit
into the indent are lifted higher up the arc of the cylinder’s rotation
and are dropped into the lifting through and go out a separate
spout. 	Thus, the length of the grain determines the fit of the
grains in the indents and how they are lifted.

☐ The disc separator also separates grains of different length. The
disc is a cast iron wheel with many undercut pockets cast into both
faces. 	As the disc turns through a mass of grains, each grain has a
chance to seat in a pocket. 	If the seed is short they will seat into
the pocket and be lifted out of the mass. Lifted grains are carried
up and dropped into a separate discharge spout.

WEIGHT
☐ Weight or specific gravity is the effective separation principle
in the air-blast separation in the air machines. However, the
gravity separator, the de-stoner, the aspirator, and the pneumatic
separator are all designed to make specific separation by
differences in weight or specific gravity of the grains. Table
below gives the specific gravity of various grains.

Specific Gravity of Various Grains
Grain 	Kernel Specific Gravity
Barley 	1.13 – 1.33
Buckwheat 	1.10
Corn 	1.19 – 1.30
Flaxseed 	1.10
Millet 	1.11
Oats 	0.95 1.06
Rough Rice 	1.11 – 1.12
Rye 	1.23
Sorghum 	1.22 – 1.26
Soybeans 	1.13 – 1.18
Wheat 	1.29 – 1.30

☐ Gravity separator, de-stoner, and other weight separators
deck that permits movement of a contaminants remaining in
the grains after utilization of dimensional differences of the
grains cleaned.

☐ The specific separator consists basically of a perforated
deck that permits movement of a stream through it. 	Grains
are fed unto this deck and into the air stream. This air stream
is adjustable allowing the operator to lift light seed while
heavier seed lie on the deck surface. The deck has a
reciprocating motion through the horizontal axis of the deck


☐ Since the deck surface is mounted at a slight angle, light
grains held up by the air will flow downhill and discharge from the
low side of the deck. 	Heavier seeds in contact with the deck
surface are tossed uphill as they reciprocate. This motion moves
the heavy grains to high side of the deck where they are
discharged. The gravity makes a graded separation from the
lightest seeds at the lower end of the deck to the heaviest grains
at the higher end of the deck.
☐ The stoner makes only a two component gravity separation:
• 	Heavy Fraction
• 	Light Fraction
☐ The principle is the same as the gravity separator.


☐ Separation in the aspirator is accomplished by pulling a
negative pressure air stream through a column. Grains fed into
the air stream move up and down, depending on their terminal
velocity. 	Grains of low terminal velocity are carried along with
the air stream and are discharged through a spout.

☐ The pneumatic separator is similar
to the aspirator. 	Separation is
accomplished by forcing a positive
pressure air blast through a separating
column where light and heavy seeds
are separated according to their
terminal velocities.

SURFACE TEXTURE
☐ Roughness or smoothness of the grain coat (surface
texture) is very common between grains. Machine such as
velvet roll mill, draper belt, magnetic separator, buckhorn
machine, and vibrator separator all effect the separation of
seeds differing in surface texture.

☐ The basic unit of the velvet roll mill consists of a long,
cylinder-like rollers covered with a velvet material and
mounted side by side so they touch along their entire
length forming a trough above and between the rollers.
The paired rollers are slightly inclined along the long axis.

☐ The grain mixture is fed into the trough formed by the
rolls at the high end. 	As the rolls revolve in opposite
direction up and out from the trough center, rough grains
adhere to the velvet material and are carried over the edge
of the rolls and fall into the discharge spout. Smooth grains,
on the other hand, do not catch on the velvet material and
roll to the low end of the paired rolls and discharge. Several
pairs of rolls are mounted in one frame to make up a
complete velvet roll mill.

☐ The inclined draper belt also separates grains that have
difference in surface texture and can also separates flat from
round grains. 	The draper belt is a tilted flat-surface, endless
belt that moves in an uphill direction. 	The grain mixture is fed
unto the center of the belt. 	Smooth or round grains roll or
slide easily to the low end of the belt and are discharged.
Flat or rough grains adhere to the belt surface and are carried
to the upper end of the belt where they are discharged.

AFFINITY FOR LIQUIDS
☐ Grains differ in their affinity for liquids, or the rate at which
their surface absorbs liquid. 	The magnetic separator and the
buckhorn machine separate seeds on this basis.

• 	In the magnetic separator, grains are fed in the machine where
a small amount of water is added in the mixture. Some seeds
absorb moisture, while others do not. Finely-ground iron
powder is added to the mixture, if the seed surface is moist, the
iron powder sticks to the grain. The grain mixture pass over a
magnetized drum or cylinder. 	Grains which retained the iron
powder on it are attracted by the magnet, stuck to the drum,
and separated from the grain stream. Grains which did not
retain the iron powder are not attracted by the magnet and are
discharged by the machine.

☐ The buckhorn machine operates on a similar principle. It
is specifically designed to remove or separate different grains.
The grain mixture is fed into a mixing chamber where moisture
is added. 	Finely-ground hard wood sawdust is then added to
the grain mixture. 	When the moisture comes in contact with
the buckhorn the surface of the seed becomes sticky thus
allowing the sawdust to adhere to the grains. The other grains
which do attract sawdust remain, and the grains that attracted
sawdust are then separated by a gravity separator or by air-
screen machine.

COLOR
☐ Many grains differ in color or reflectivity. 	Electronic color
sorters make color separations. 	Each grain is subjected to an
electronic sensing device which compares the grains with a
pattern or a given color background. If the grain color or
reflectivity is acceptable, it is allowed to continue to the
discharge spout. 	Grains in the correct ranges of color or
reflectivity are rejected from the main stream by compressed air
or other devices.

☐ Color sorters have relatively low capacity, but their
versatility makes them usually valuable for difficult
separations on large or valuable grains, such as beans
and vegetable seeds.

ELECTRICAL CONDUCTIVITY
☐ Grains also differ in their ability to hold or conduct an
electrical charge. 	Very difficult separations can be made with
electrostatic separator. A typical electrostatic separator
consists of a conveyor belt, which carries a single-layer of
grains beneath an electrode.

☐ Two types of electrostatic separator used in grain
cleaning. The belt-type conveys the seeds below the
electrode, grains which have poor conductivity absorb and
hold the charge, stick to the grounded conveyor belt and are
carried to a discharge spout. 	Good conductors lose their
charge readily and are dropped into a separate spout.

☐ The “lifting” electrostatic separation is made by passing
grains through an electrical field created by a different type
of electrode. 	Grains are attached to the electrode and lifted
into a different flight path as they fall from a belt or roller.
Other seeds which react less to the charge follow a normal
flight path to the discharge spout.

SHAPE
☐ The shape of grains varies widely. Cleaning machines
such as the air-screen machine, the indented cylinder, and
the disc separator take advantage of shape differences in the
grains.

☐ The spiral separator consists mainly of a simple vertical
series of spiraled flights. 	The grain mixture (round and
non-round seed) is fed into the inner spiral at the top of the
machine. 	As the seeds roll down the spirals under the
influence of gravity, the velocity of the round seeds
increase to the point where they roll over the inclined edge
of the inner flight of the spirals, unto an outer flight. 	The
outer flight discharges into a separate spout. The non-
round, flattened grains or irregular-shaped grains, slide
down rather than roll down over the edge of the internal
flight and continue down the flight to the discharge spout.
Thus, grains are separated by the spiral separator
difference in their ability to roll.

FILTRATION
☐ An operation by which solid
particles are separated from a
liquid or gas b forcing the
mixture through a porous
medium that retains the
particles.
☐ Modes of filtration includes:
(1) Surface filtration, and depth
filtration.

Surface Filtration
☐ The fluid is forced through a
porous medium (filter medium)
that retains the particle on its
surface. Particle larger than the
openings of the porous surface
are retained.
☐ Filter media include paper,
cloth porous ceramics, sintered
glass or metal, membranes.
☐ Device includes the bag filter
commonly used in air cleaning in
agricultural processing plant.
☐ Usually coupled after the
cyclone separator to do the final
removal of dusts.


Depth Filtration
☐ The mixture flows through a thick
layer of porous material of fibrous.
☐ The solid particles of the mixture
are retained as a result of collision
with the fiber fibers or particles of
the filter medium or by adsorption.
☐ Example, glass wool and rock
wool or particulates such as sand
structure.
☐ Usually the purpose of filtration is
the removal of undesirable solid
particles from the liquid product like
clarification of wine
☐ For recovery of solid product from
solid/liquid mixture in separation of
sugar crystal from mother liquor.

REFERENCES
☐ Araullo, E. V., de Padua, D B., and M. Graham. 1976. Rice
Postharvest and Technology. International development
Research Center. 	Bos 8500, Ottawa, Canada. 394pp.
☐ Henderson, S. M. and R. L. Perry. 1976. Agricultural Process
Engineering. Third Edition. The AVI Publishing Company, Inc.
Wesport, Connecticut. USA. 442pp.
☐ SEARCA. Grain Post-Harvest Processing Technology.
Southeast Asia Cooperative Post-Harvest Research and
Development Programme. SEARCA. Los Baños, Laguna.
279pp.
☐ Wallace, B. and J. Naylor. Introduction to Seed and Grain
Cleaning. Paper for Presentation at the 1981 Winter Meeting of
the American Society of Agricultural Engineers. Palmer House.
Chicago, Illinois. USA. 12pp. December 15-18, 1981.

QUESTIONS AND PROBLEMS

1. Process of removing contaminants
from the product.
a. 	Sorting
b. 	Grading
c. 	Cleaning
d. 	None of the above
2. Process of separating cleaned
products in various quality fractions
that maybe defined based on the
size, shape, texture, colors, and other
factors.
a. 	Sorting
b. 	Grading
c. 	Cleaning
d. 	None of the above
3. Which of the following parameters
are taken into consideration during
cleaning and grading products?
a. 	Size
b. 	Weight
c. 	Surface Texture
d. Affinity to liquid
e. Color
f. 	Shape
g. All of the above
4. Rough cleaning of paddy by
removing most foreign materials prior
to drying and storage.
a. Aspiration
b. Scalping
c. Sieving
d. All of the above
5. Self-cleaning sieves used for rice
mills basically consist of ____.
a. a brush to remove particles that
clogs the screen of the cleaner
b. 	one or two balls that continuously
hammer the top sieve of the cleaner
c. 	assigned operator to do the
cleaning while the machine is
operating
d. 	None of the above

6. Process of separating lower
density materials from grains.
a. 	Aspiration
b. 	Cleaning
c. 	Fanning
d. 	All of the above
7. Kind of cleaner that uses air in
separating lesser-density materials
from corn kernel/corn grits such as
floured corn, germ and bran.
a. 	Aspirator
b. 	Oscillating screen
c. 	Cleaner
d. 	Cyclone separator
e. 	All of the above
8. Machine used to remove hard
materials of almost the same size as
milled rice through gravity
separation using air stream to
cause rice grains to be carried away
by the air stream leaving heavy
materials behind.
a. 	Aspirator
b. 	De-stoner
c. 	Sifter
d. 	None of the above
9. Machine used to separate grains
according to color or reflectivity.
a. 	Color meter
b. 	Electronic color sorter
c. 	Electric color separator
d. 	None of the above

larger particles from rice, also known
as “rough cleaning” of rough rice.
a. 	Rotary sieve
b. 	Scalper
c. 	Vibrating screen
d. 	All of the above

11. Recommended size of scalper
for paddy is ____.
a. 0.2-0.25sq.m. per ton
b. 0.3-0.35sq.m. per ton
c. 0.4-0.45sq.m. per ton
d. None of the above
12. Type of screen cleaners that
uses air blast to assist in the
cleaning.
a. 	Screen separator
b. 	Fanning mill
c. 	Blower
d. 	None of the above
13. Percentage of grains free from
foreign matters.
a. 	Percentage foreign matter
b. 	Percentage Cleanliness
c. Purity
d. None of the above
14. When removing light particles
from threshed grains that go with the
chaffs during operation, what would
be the best course of action that you
should recommend as an Agricultural
Engineer in order to achieve better
cleaning and separation?
a. 	Install additional perforated sheets
in the cleaning system.
b. 	Provide an air-blast system using
a blower so it can carry light particles.
c. 	Reduce the feeding of threshed
grains.
d. None of the above
15. Grain separator for seed based
on the affinity for liquid or on the rate
at which the surface of the seed
absorbs liquid.
a. 	Vibrator separator
b. 	Aspirator

16. Separator used for particles with

a. Air-blast separator

17. Vibrator separator is recommended

18. Amount of foreign materials in a

19. Material commonly used in
separating grains from chaffs

20. When using a cylindrical slotted
rotating screen or sheet, the material

21. Indented rotating cylinders are

text:
MIXING AND BLENDING
Volume 6 –AGRICULTURAL AND FOOD PROCESS ENGINEERING
by
Engr. Alexis T. Belonio, MS
Agricultural and Biosystems Engineer
ASEAN Engineer
2024 AGRICULTURAL AND BIOSYSTEMS ENGINEERING
BOARD EXAM REVIEWER

Disclaimer
Photos, illustrations and schematic diagrams of equipment or machine parts shown in
the presentation are solely for educational purposes to facilitate comprehension of the
topics by the students. 	Showing them does not endorse a product nor imply criticism
of similar products not mentioned.

INTRODUCTION
☐ Mixing or blending of materials is a very extensive processing
operation.
☐ Difficulty in mixing may result if the solids have the same size but of
different specific gravity or if they have different sizes or shapes.
☐ Heavier particles tend to remain near the bottom of the container
during mixing.
☐ Round or small particles tend to move toward the top of the
container.
☐ A different case in food processing will be encountered when
mixing solid with liquid or liquid to liquid.

Feed Processing Plant where Feed Ingredients are Blended and Mixed

INDICATORS OF SATISFACTORY
MIXING PROCESS
☐ Produces uniform mixture – the final product need to
have properly represented by the different ingredients used
during the mixture.
☐ Less time in mixing the materials – shorter time needed
in mixing operation since it may reflect on the capacity and
costs.
☐ Minimum cost for overhead, power, and labor – cost for
the labor, power, and overhead must be minimal.

Batch Mixer
☐ It is used from moderate to small
operations where overhead cost must
be low and labor cost is not critical.
☐ Ingredients are weighed or
measured.
☐ It can be adopted in semi-
continuous process by using a number
of batch mixers which empty into
common conveyor or storage.
☐ Concurrent filling, mixing, and
emptying facilitate the use of labor and
equipment.

Continuous Mixer
☐ It is most satisfactory for large and extensive operations.
☐ Ingredients are usually added volumetrically by an auger, start
wheel, or other device to a screw conveyor.
☐ Continuous mixing operation is carried out in a screw conveyor that
may have special flights to insure thorough mixing.

Horizontal-Batch Mixer
☐ It consists of a horizontal cylindrical
or U-shaped vessel in which a shaft
with mixing blades or paddles rotates
(approx. 25 rpm).
☐ It is filled from the top and
discharged through the valves at the
bottom.
☐ Compared with the vertical mixer,
the installed power is relatively higher.
☐ Mixing time is much shorter in this
type of mixer.
☐ It is used from moderate to small
operations where overhead cost must
be low and labor cost is not critical.

Advantages and Disadvantages of Horizontal Mixer
• 	Short mixing time that results in high capacity.
• 	Rapid discharge.
• 	Mixing of liquids is possible.
• 	Low building height.
• 	Incomplete cleanout when outlet valves are small.
• 	Higher investment because of more complex construction
and higher installed power.
• 	Filling level influences mixing efficiency.

Vertical-Batch Mixer
☐ It consists of either cylindrical,
rectangular, or hexagonal bin with a
conical-shaped bottom.
☐ Inside the vessel is a vertical screw-
conveyor which moves the material
upward and subsequently flows
downward at the wall of the vessel.
☐ Filling is from then top or through a
screw conveyor into dump-hopper at the
bottom of the mixer.
☐ After mixing, the material is discharged
through an outlet at the bottom or at the
side of the vessel.
☐ Mixing time varies from 15 minutes, for
normal feeds, to 30 minutes, for
production of premixes.

Advantages and Disadvantages
of Vertical Mixer
• Relatively low installed motor
power.
• Low investment.
• Flexible capacity utilization as
the filling rate does not influence
mixing quality.
• Relatively long mixing time.
• Slow discharging which can
reduce feed mill capacity.
• Relatively high building height
required.

KNEADER
☐ Kneading is commonly used in
food processing particularly in
bread, cake and other similar
preparation.
☐ It is an intensive mixing
operation applied to dough and
paste-like product.
☐ Mixers on this type of
application are characterized by
their ability to deliver high rotation
momentum.
☐ They operate at relatively low
rotational speed with
considerable energy input per
unit mass.

IN-FLOW MIXING
☐ Liquid, gases or particulate solids
flowing through piping or equipment
can be mixed without mechanical
mixers by simply using turbulence.
☐ Mixing the substances into the
flow channel specially shaped
elements, regular flow patterns may
be distorted.
☐ Devices such as venturi tubes
and other kind of restrictions maybe
used for in-flow mixing.
☐ This method is basically useful in
continuous process operation.
☐ Not very efficient for heavy
mixing duty like mixing viscous
liquids.

☐ 	Berk, Z. 2009. Food Process Engineering and Technology. First
Edition. Elsevier. Academic Press London. UK. 605pp.
☐ 	Clavel, R. DATEC Micro Feedmill. A pilot project proposal. Dingle
Agricultural and Technical College, Dingle, Iloilo. August 2001. 43pp.
☐ 	Henderson, S. M. and R. L. Perry. 1976. Agricultural Process
Engineering. 3rd Edition. The AVI Publishing Co., Inc. Wesport,
Connecticut. 442pp.
☐ 	Paul Singh, R., D.R. Heldman. 2009. Introduction to Food
Engineering. Fourth Edition. Elsevier. Academic Press, London,
U.K. 839pp.
REFERENCES

QUESTIONS AND PROBLEMS

1. Process of combining different
materials until a certain degree of
homogeneity is achieved.
a. 	Milling
b. 	Mixing
c. 	Feeding
d. 	None of the above
2. Assembling and measuring of
the needed amount of every solid
raw feed material in the
formulation of the desired
composition of a mixture.
a. 	Mixing
b. 	Blending
c. 	Pelleting
d. 	All of the above
3. Blending of ingredients or of
materials in agricultural
processing operation.
a. 	Sorting
b. 	Molding
c. Mixing
d. All of the above
4. Purpose of mixing is basically
____.
a. 	to promote the transfer of
heat
between hot and cold products
b. 	to obtain good contact
between
materials being mixed
c. 	to promote reactions between
reactants
d. 	All of the above
e. 	Any two of the above
5. During mixing, heavier
particles tend to remain ____ of
the container.
a. 	near the bottom
b. 	away from the bottom
c. 	at the middle
d. 	None of the above

a. 	Produce uniform mixture.
b. 	Less time in mixing materials.
c. 	Less cost.
d. 	All of the above
e. 	None of the above
7. Feed materials are purposely
mixed to ____.
a. 	obtain a homogenous feed to
ensure that animals are given the
same proportions of nutrient
b. reduce the density of the feed
material so that it can be easily
transported
c. improve the digestability of
feeds
d. None of the above
8. During mixing, round or small
particles tend to move towards the
____ of the container.
a. 	top
b. 	middle
c. bottom
d. All of the above
9. Difficulty in mixing may result
if the solid particles has ____.
a. the same size but of different
specific gravity
b. different sizes
c. different shapes
d. 	All of the above
10. If mixing is needed during
conveying, the suitable conveyor
to use is ____ type.
a. 	bucket
b. 	screw
c. 	belt
d. 	All of the above

11. Mixer with U-shaped bin
containing a central-mixing blade
or a ribbon mounted on a
rotating shaft.
a. Horizontal mixer
b. Inclined mixer
c. Vertical mixer
d. All of the above
12. Feed mixer characterized by
high capacity, short mixing time,
and high power requirement.
a. Horizontal mixer
b. Inclined mixer
c. Vertical mixer
d. All of the above
13. Horizontal feed mixer is not
advantageous for feed mixing as
compared with vertical feed
mixer for the reason that ____.
a. it has lower capacity
b. it has high power requirement
c. it has shorter life span
d. None of the above
14. Feed mixer characterized by
low capacity, longer mixing time
and low power requirement.
a. 	Horizontal mixer
b. 	Inclined mixer
c. 	Vertical mixer
d. 	All of the above
15. Difficulty in mixing often occurs
if the solids are ____ size and
shape but of different specific

INTRODUCTION
☐ The performance of processing plant is affected by the efficiency
of the movement of materials from one unit operation to another. In
agricultural and food processing systems, harvested products are
moved, transported, and conveyed from one place to another.
☐ For grains and cereals, for example, they move from the drying bin
to the storage bin or from the truck to the dryer or bins.
☐ Material handling generally implies the movement of materials in
any direction whether it be horizontal, vertical, or any combination of
the two. Lifting, shifting, placing, stacking and transporting are the
various phases of handling the materials.
☐ ABE should be familiar with these equipment design and operation
particularly when they are dealing with agricultural and food process
as profession.

☐ Lifts, trucks and carts - horizontal

Belt Conveyor
☐ Belt conveyor is essentially an endless belt operating between
two or more pulleys with its load supported on idlers. The
installation may either be simple or heavy belt that is supported by
antifriction bearings. 	In grain processing, it may be flat for moving
bags of paddy or V-shaped for moving bulk of paddy. The belt
conveyor consists of a belt, drive and end pulleys, idlers, a drive
and tension mechanism, and loading and discharge devices. Its
capacity depends on the belt width, angle of trough, and belt
speed. Good in conveying product that requires very minimal
damage.

Advantage Features of a Belt Conveyor
☐ High mechanical efficiency
☐ Negligible damage to product being conveyed
☐ Conveying capacity is high
☐ Can convey materials at long distance
☐ Self-cleaning
☐ Long service life
☐ Limited elevating capacity
☐ High initial cost

☐ Belt conveyors have high mechanical efficiency because the
load is carried in an antifriction bearing. 	Damage to product, like
grains, is almost nil since there is no relative motion between the
product being carried and the belt. The carrying capacity is high
since relatively high speed is possible. Materials can be
conveyed in long distances but limited to angle in some extent.
Property designed belt conveyors have long service life but the
initial cost is usually high. These are widely used for moving
paddy in many installations. They range from 30 to 100 cm in
width and may be up to several hundred meters in length.

Screw Conveyor
☐ Screw conveyor is used to handle finely divided powders, damp,
sticky, heavy viscous materials, hot substances that may be
chemically active, and granular materials of all types.
☐ The typical screw conveyor consists of a conveyor screw in a
trough supported by end hanger bearings.

☐ The screw rotation pushes the
material it conveys along the trough.
The standard pitch screw has a pitch
approximately equal to the diameter.
It is used on most horizontal
installations and on inclines up to 20
deg. 	Half standard pitch screw may
be used for includes greater than 20
deg double and triple flight, variable-
pitch, and steeped-diameter screws
are available for moving difficult
materials and controlling feed rate.
Ribbon screws are used for mixing,
both singly and in connection with
conveying.

Determine the recommended speed of the following screw
conveyors:
a) 4 inches at 30% loading @ 50 ft3 per hour
b) 6 inches at 45% loading @ 100 ft3 per hour
c) 10 inches at 30% loading@ 200 ft3 per hour
Given: 	Screw diameter - 4, 6, and 10 inches
Loading 	- 30 & 45 % loading
Capacity 	- 50, 100, 200 ft3 per hour
Required: 	Recommended speed of the screws

☐ Horizontal screw conveyors are usually operated in U-shaped
trough with or without cover, depending upon the type of service
and the characteristics of the material being moved. They may be
designed either clockwise or counterclockwise rotation without
change in the capacity. The screw is also supported by brackets at
various standard spacing. For elevating at a steep incline, a
cylindrical housing is used. The tube is operated full, and no
brackets are used between the end since they would interfere with
the movement of the material. The material supports and guides
the flight so that satisfactory operation results if the conveyor is
kept full.

Screw conveyors are well suited
as feeders or metering devices
under bins or hoppers. The
portion of the screw under the bin
or hopper is usually designed with
half or third pitch, the balance of
the screw full pitch. Thus, the
main portion of the screw operates
half or third full; whereas, the
metering portion of the screw
operates full.

☐ The capacity of full screw conveyor as used for feeding and

N 	- shaft speed, rpm

☐ The actual capacity is much lesser than the theoretical capacity
because of screw-housing clearance, fluid characteristics of
material, screw length, head of material, and elevation or lift.

diameter is 2 inches with a screw pitch of 4 inches. The speed

Shaft diameter 	- 2 in.
Screw pitch 	- 4 in.
Screw speed 	- 80 rpm
Loading 	- 45%

= [(8 in.)2 – (2 in.)2 /36.6] [4 in. x 80 rpm]
= 524.59 ft3/hr
@ 45% loading
= 524.59 ft3/hr x 0.45
= 236.07 ft3/hr

☐ The power requirement of a screw conveyor is a function of its
length, elevation, type of hanger brackets, type of flights, viscosity or
internal resistance of the material, coefficient of friction of the
material on the flights and housing, and weight of the material. Extra
power required to start a full screw and to free a jammed screw
must be given consideration together with the power required if the
material has a tendency to stick to the trough sides or to ball.

Bucket Elevator
☐ A bucket elevator consists
of buckets attached to a chain

typical bucket elevator.
☐ Inclined conveyors or
elevators are less efficient

cost is minimal.

• 	Centrifugal
• 	Positive (gravity)
• 	Continuous (direct gravity)

grains. 	It is designed and engineered to conform with general
practice in handling grains. 	Head and boot shafts are provided
with roller bearings. 	Take-ups are generally screw-type except on
tall, high-capacity units where gravity-type take-ups are more

Elevator Head, Boot and Legs
☐ Elevator heads should be of proper shape and size with smooth
contours. The discharge side of the head should be shaped in
such a way that the material thrown from the buckets will not be
deflected into the downleg. The throat should be considerable
below the head shaft to catch the materials that are slow leaving
the buckets.

☐ Most bucket elevators provide in the boot section a belt take-

through and does not rub on either side of the boot. A manual
screw-type take-up boot pulley is used. This provides the
correct belt tension at all times. 	Cleanouts should always be
included on both sides of the boot to permit fast, easy cleaning.

☐ Elevator legs are constructed either all welded, bolted,
or riveted units. There are several designs of cross-

lengths of 2.4 m but could be manufactured in any length
